sections.label: Programmes and schemes listed
sections.summary: The passage lists programmes and schemes including MediShield Life, Smart Nation, Community Network for Seniors, Industry Transformation Maps and Adapt and Grow.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: A lot done with programmes and schemes, such as MediShield Life, Smart Nation initiatives, Community Network for Seniors, Industry Transformation Maps (ITMs), Adapt and Grow for workers and so on.

sections.label: Through train education pilot
sections.summary: The passage proposes piloting through train education to Secondary school for special needs students in mainstream schools.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: One, to pilot “through train” education to Secondary school for special needs students in mainstream schools.

sections.label: VIA as admission criterion
sections.summary: The passage proposes de-emphasising academic excellence by including VIA performance as a standard school admission criterion.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Second, to de-emphasise academic excellence by including VIA performance as a standard school admission criterion.

sections.label: Building soft skills creativity
sections.summary: The passage proposes building soft skills and creativity of students from young.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Third, build soft skills and creativity of students from young.

sections.label: Government role in job-matching
sections.summary: The passage states the Government has to play a greater role in shaping the job-matching scene.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: One, the Government has to play a greater role in shaping the job-matching scene.

sections.label: Institute for Human Resource Practitioners
sections.summary: The passage states IHRP was established by MOM, NTUC and the Singapore National Employers' Federation as an example of an enabling initiative.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: The establishment of the Institute for Human Resource Practitioners (IHRP) by Ministry of Manpower (MOM), National Trades Union Congress (NTUC) and the Singapore National Employers’ Federation is a good example of an initiative that can enable such changes within organisations and professional communities.

sections.label: Aged HDB flats and SERS
sections.summary: The speaker says it is time to include other considerations for HDB flats above 50 years old and to augment the Selective En-bloc Redevelopment Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: At the same time, I believe we still want to instil a sense of responsibility in our people and have them take ownership towards securing their basic needs.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Thus, I think it is time for us to include other considerations for the aged HDB flats and, in this, I mean flats that are above 50 years of age, and augment the Selective En-bloc Redevelopment Scheme (SERS).

sections.label: Valuation of ageing leasehold flats
sections.summary: The speaker says aged flats should not be valued by past market transactions but by remaining lease, owner's occupation length and right-sizing potential.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: The fact is that the value of any ageing leasehold property will be different from a young property, regardless of how attractive its location is.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Thus, aged flats should not be valued using the current comparison method of past market transactions.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: I suggest the valuation be based instead on its remaining lease, the length of time the current owner has occupied the place and its right-sizing potential.

sections.label: Subsidies for non-working mothers
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Ministry can consider equal subsidies for non-working mothers who plan to return to the workforce and stay employed after their children are placed in care services.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: As we encourage women to return to the workforce and balance their parental duties, can the Ministry consider giving equal subsidies for non-working mothers who plan to return to the workforce and remain gainfully employed after their children are placed in care services?

sections.label: Caregiving leave entitlement change
sections.summary: The speaker says caregiving duty falls mainly on women and hopes the request is seen as a legislative change letting an individual's existing entitlement be used to care for loved ones.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: As this duty still primarily falls on the shoulders of the women, those coming from single-child families or are the main caregiver to the elderly will feel more pressure, balancing work and caregiving.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: I understand the Ministries have been studying this topic with the employers and unions, but I hope they see the request not as one asking for more entitlement and thus inconveniencing the companies.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Instead, it is about making a legislative change that allows an individual’s existing entitlement to be used for caring of their loved ones.

sections.label: Women in STEM research
sections.summary: A UN research showed that only 28% of global researchers in STEM were women in 2016.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: A UN research showed that only 28% of the global researchers in STEM are women in 2016.

sections.label: Structural changes for seniors
sections.summary: The structural changes include a nation-wide expansion of Community Networks for Seniors by 2020, formation of the Silver Generation Office, and consolidation of planning and policy oversight from MSF to MOH.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: The structural changes include a nation-wide expansion of Community Networks for Seniors by 2020, the formation of the Silver Generation Office and a further consolidation of planning and policy oversight of health and social support services from the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) to the Ministry of Health (MOH).

sections.label: National Steps Challenge MediShield incentives
sections.summary: The speaker suggests MOH consider incentivising Singaporeans with MediShield Life premium discounts to boost the National Steps Challenge.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: The National Steps Challenge seems to be a simple and effective platform to get our citizens moving.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Hence, I suggest for MOH to consider boosting these efforts by incentivising Singaporeans through discounts on their MediShield Life premiums.

sections.label: Government inflation support for low-income
sections.summary: The Government has supported people against inflation and rising costs through subsidies and schemes, with the largest support going to low-income individuals and households.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Over the years, the Government has conscientiously supported our people in mitigating the impact of inflation and rising external costs through different forms of direct subsidies and creating schemes to ensure affordability.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: While our safety net support is a targeted approach, the largest and continued financial support has always been extended to the low-income individuals and households to ensure they can keep up with basic needs and are not left behind as we progress.

sections.label: Conditions for Government to achieve
sections.summary: The speaker says this can be done only if the Government keeps necessities affordable, provides sufficient choices, and builds a giving society.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: To me, this can only be done if the Government is able to: one, keep necessities like utilities, food, transport and healthcare affordable; two, provide sufficient choices to meet the varied needs; and, three, build a society of giving individuals and corporations.

sections.label: Singaporeans on Forbes 30 Under 30
sections.summary: In Forbes 30 Under 30 Asia 2018, 24 Singaporeans were listed among 300 young disruptors, and Singapore tied with Japan for fifth highest honorees.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Last month, in "Forbes 30 Under 30 Asia 2018" edition, themed "Disruption and Innovation", 24 individuals from Singapore made it to the list.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: The list featured 300 young disruptors, innovators and entrepreneurs across Asia who are under the age of 30.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: And Singapore tied with Japan for the fifth highest number of honorees this year.

sections.label: Singapore trade, FTAs and investments
sections.summary: Singapore's trade-to-GDP ratio is about 400%, it has 22 implemented FTAs, hosts about 37,000 international companies, and EDB draws about $10 billion yearly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Our total trade to GDP ratio at about 400% is the highest in the world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Singapore has an extensive network of 22 implemented FTAs, with 12 others in the works.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Conversely, an estimated 37,000 international companies have their headquarters in Singapore, including about 7,000 MNCs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: And EDB continues to draw in about $10 billion worth of foreign investments into Singapore each year.

sections.label: Building trade links and CPTPP
sections.summary: The speaker says Singapore should build more trade and investment links with more countries, and welcomes the conclusion of the CPTPP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Instead, we should look to build even more trade and investment links with more countries and to spread our risks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I am glad that the remaining 11 countries of the TPP persisted to conclude the TPP 11, now known as CPTPP, despite the US’ withdrawal.

sections.label: Physical connectivity infrastructure investment
sections.summary: It has helped connect Singapore to the world, and investment should continue in Terminal 5, Tuas Mega Port and other infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: It has helped better connect and plug our tiny island to the rest of the world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: We should continue to invest and upgrade our physical connectivity, such as building Terminal 5, Tuas Mega Port and other infrastructure to stay ahead of the pack.

sections.label: Non-physical connectivity strategy
sections.summary: The Addendum outlined a strategy of enhancing non-physical connectivity so companies and people worldwide do business with and through Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The Addendum outlined the strategy that by further enhancing our connectivity in the non-physical dimensions, it will facilitate companies and people from around the world to do business with Singapore, through Singapore and on Singapore platforms.

sections.label: Digital capabilities and infrastructure
sections.summary: Deepening digital capabilities and infrastructure requires digital connection with other jurisdictions, including the ASEAN Innovation Network under negotiation, and key commercial players.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: For this to work, we need to deepen our digital capabilities and infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: We need to digitally connect with other jurisdictions, such as the currently being negotiated ASEAN Innovation Network, as well as with other key commercial players in the digital space.

sections.label: R&D hub and Global Innovation Alliance
sections.summary: Singapore is an established R&D hub involving research institutes, IHLs and enterprises, in line with FEC plans for a Global Innovation Alliance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Singapore is now an established hub for R&D activities involving the research institutes, IHLs and the enterprises.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This is in line with FEC’s plans to build a Global Innovation Alliance (GIA) which serves as a platform for innovation collaboration between Singapore-based enterprises and institutions with overseas partners.

sections.label: Financial connectivity and ITM targets
sections.summary: Singapore must scale up financial connectivity, and the ITM for financial services aims to grow the sector 4.3% annually and create 4,000 jobs yearly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: It is, therefore, imperative that Singapore further scale up its financial connectivity capacity, both in breadth and depth so that it can fully benefit from the growing opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I am heartened that the ITM for financial services sets out a comprehensive strategy to grow the sector by 4.3% per annum and to create 4,000 jobs every year, including 1,000 jobs in the fintech sector.

sections.label: Connectivity to China's markets
sections.summary: The CCI Southern Transport Corridor leverages the BRI, and connectivity to China's financial markets is crucial for Singapore as a financial centre.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The Chongqing Connectivity Initiative (CCI) Southern Transport Corridor (STC) is an innovative positioning to leverage on the BRI and also on what we can offer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: We also look forward to the conclusion of the upgraded China-Singapore FTA to expand trade relations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Singapore is now one of the RMB clearing centres and China has extended its RMB Qualified Foreign Institutional Investors (RQFII) programme to Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: For Singapore to stay relevant as a financial centre, the connectivity to China’s financial markets is crucial.

sections.label: Future economy strategy moves
sections.summary: The future economy strategy continues bold moves to build the digital economy, deepen transformation via 23 ITMs and build a future-ready workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Under the future economy strategy, we continue to make bold moves to build the digital economy, to deepen transformation efforts via the 23 ITMs and to strive ahead with a whole-of-system effort to build a future-ready workforce.

sections.label: Singapore hosting historic summits
sections.summary: Singapore hosted the 1993 Wang-Koo and 2015 Xi-Ma meetings and will host the June US-North Korea summit, with its principled stand and neutrality cited as reasons.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: If others ever attach a price to our position or stand, no one will take us seriously ever again.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: We were the host to the historic meetings between China and Taiwan – the Wang-Koo meeting in 1993 and the Xi-Ma meeting in 2015.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: We will be the host for the upcoming summit between the US and North Korea in June.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Our principled stand and neutrality were some reasons why Singapore was chosen for these meetings.

sections.label: Partnering China in third markets
sections.summary: With China venturing abroad, Singapore must ask how it can partner the Chinese to explore third markets or become a platform for them.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Only then can we provide more relevant ideas for mutual benefit in a timely manner.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Now that China has moved beyond attracting foreign investments into venturing abroad, we must ask ourselves how we can play a role in partnering the Chinese to explore third markets or how we can become a platform for them to reach out to third markets.

sections.label: US collaboration and gateway role
sections.summary: With the US, Singapore deepens collaboration with American companies in smart-city solutions and e-commerce and is a gateway for their regional growth.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: With the US, we not only deepen collaboration with American companies in areas, such as smart-city solutions and e-commerce, we are also an established gateway, a launch-pad, for American companies seeking growth opportunities in the region.

sections.label: SMU overseas programme requirement
sections.summary: Students joining Singapore Management University from August this year must participate in at least one overseas programme before graduating.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Students who join Singapore Management University (SMU) from August this year, will need to participate in at least one overseas programme, before they can graduate.

sections.label: Overseas outreach and talent network
sections.summary: EDB and associated agencies will collaborate to expand overseas outreach and build a Singapore Talent Network engaging Singaporean families, friends and fans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: To this end, EDB and associated agencies will collaborate to better organise and expand our overseas outreach.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: We will build a Singapore Talent Network to engage Singaporean families, friends and fans to be part of the Singapore Story.

sections.label: Singapore business dynamism and global network
sections.summary: Dynamism keeps Singapore vibrant for business, and the speaker aspires to a global network of Singaporeans, friends and fans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Such dynamism is what keeps Singapore a vibrant, exceptional place to do business in and this is the vital ingredient for our economic future.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: I have always aspired that we will, one day, build a global network of more than three million Singaporeans, 30 million Singaporean friends and, perhaps, 300 million Singaporean fans.

sections.label: Renegotiating and upgrading FTAs
sections.summary: Economic agencies are working to re-negotiate new Free Trade Agreements and upgrade existing ones.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Our economic agencies are working hard to re-negotiate new Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) and upgrade existing ones.

sections.label: Focus on Gross National Income
sections.summary: For the next lap of growth, Singapore must focus not only on GDP in Singapore but also on GNI in Singapore and beyond.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: For the next lap of our economic growth story, we cannot just look at the Gross Domestic Product (GDP) of what we do in Singapore only.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: We need to also focus on what we call the Gross National Income (GNI) of what we do in Singapore and beyond.

sections.label: Enterprises innovate, scale up, translate R&D
sections.summary: Enterprises must innovate and scale up, translating R&D investments into capabilities and enterprises, led by A*STAR and Enterprise Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Our enterprises must innovate and scale up and we need to better translate investments in research and development, into new capabilities and enterprises.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: A*STAR and Enterprise Singapore will lead this and work closely with our companies – be they large local enterprises or small, medium enterprises and trade associations – for all of us to realise this together.

sections.label: Helping middle group, training and skills
sections.summary: Singapore must help the striving broad middle group and ensure training and skills upgrading are relevant and accessible throughout workers' lifecycle.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: We need to continue to better help the striving broad middle group to keep improving their lives.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: We need to make sure that our training and skills upgrading are relevant and accessible, helping our workers to access opportunities throughout their entire lifecycle.

sections.label: Social mobility slows as society matures
sections.summary: As society matures, social mobility tends to slow down and social inequality becomes more apparent over time.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: As society matures, social mobility tends to slow down, with social inequality becoming more apparent over time.

sections.label: Accessible opportunities for all
sections.summary: The passage states that opportunities should be accessible to all who are hardworking, talented and committed, and tied to aptitude and skills, not just academic grades.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: We want everybody to have a good start and to achieve their full potential.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: This means ensuring that opportunities are accessible to all who are hardworking, talented and committed; that opportunities are not just tied to academic grades, but also to the right aptitude and skills.

sections.label: Whole-of-nation strategy
sections.summary: The passage states that policies are constantly updated to meet evolving needs, and that a whole-of-nation strategy will be used, not just a whole-of-Government one.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: More importantly, for us to also constantly update them to meet our evolving needs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: This has been our approach on issues like National Service, HDB and housing, CPF, as well as the GRC system and Elected Presidency.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: For example, in our efforts to renew our economy through the ITMs and help our workers seize the opportunities ahead, we will not just involve the Government agencies alone.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Rather than a "whole-of-Government" strategy, we will work on a "whole-of-nation" strategy.

sections.label: Overlapping leadership generations
sections.summary: The passage states that the leadership model is to have overlapping generations of leadership teams to help the next generation do even better.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Our leadership model is to have overlapping generations of leadership teams to help the next generation do even better.

sections.label: Appreciation to Low Thia Khiang
sections.summary: The passage places on record appreciation to Mr Low Thia Khiang as leader of the Workers' Party for the last 17 years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: At this juncture, I would also like to place on record our appreciation to Mr Low Thia Khiang, as leader of the Workers’ Party for the last 17 years.

sections.label: Refreshed systems and politics
sections.summary: The passage states that Singapore must value add, build networks and compete globally, and that its systems and politics must be special and refreshed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: To secure our place in the world, we have to value add to stay relevant, build our networks and be able to compete globally, in order to transcend our constraints of geography and resources and, instead, turn them into opportunities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: To keep Singapore successful, our systems and politics must be special and refreshed, suited to our own unique circumstances and needs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: We will also need to do more to inspire yet another generation of Singaporeans to come forth to serve Singapore, in spite of.

sections.label: Leaving a better Singapore
sections.summary: The passage states that the current generation can leave behind an even better Singapore, limited only by the scale of its ambition and drive.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: They had overcome their share of the challenges to leave us the Singapore we have today.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: There is absolutely no reason why our generation which has so much more cannot leave behind an even better Singapore for the next generation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: We can only be limited by the scale of our ambition and drive.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: And our scale of ambition and drive will determine how far we progress as a nation for the next 50 years and more.

sections.label: Marine parks protection extension
sections.summary: Protection under the Parks and Trees Act was extended to marine parks last November to better protect biodiversity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In order to better protect the biodiversity, we have extended the protection under the Parks and Trees Act to marine parks last November.

sections.label: Singapore Stewardship Fund proposal
sections.summary: A Singapore Stewardship Fund is proposed where 10%-20% of a foreign worker's salary goes into a special savings account without costing employers more.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Another aspiration I have is to consider the setting up of a Singapore Stewardship Fund.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Without costing employers more, a percentage of the salary of a foreign worker, perhaps 10%-20%, can be put directly into a special savings account.

sections.label: Opt-in levy discount
sections.summary: If the arrangement is opt-in, a levy discount could be considered, benefiting employers and giving them a financial incentive to opt in.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: If this arrangement is done on an opt-in basis, a discount on the worker's levy could be considered, thereby benefiting the employer, which, in turn, could provide a financial incentive for the employer to opt in.

sections.label: Casino licence renewal question
sections.summary: When renewing casino licences every three years, the fundamental question is whether casinos are needed in the present economic climate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: For example, when renewing casino licences every three years, the question for us should not just be whether there should be a three-year extension but the question we should visit and contemplate is a more fundamental one: whether in this present economic climate, we need casinos at all.

sections.label: Prevention of Human Trafficking Bill
sections.summary: The Prime Minister supported a Private Member's Bill on the Prevention of Human Trafficking, and it was a team effort between three Ministers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: For example, I had asked the Prime Minister to consider whether he would support the introduction of a Private Member's Bill on the Prevention of Human Trafficking.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The Prime Minister offered his guidance and shared his insights on how any introduction of a new law would entail collaboration with multiple agencies, in terms of enforcement and that, at some stages, the path to a private Bill would be tough.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Yet, the Prime Minister supported it and it was very much a team effort between Minister Masagos from Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA), Minister Chan Chun Sing who was leading MSF at the time and Minister Tan Chuan-Jin who helmed MOM.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Without Prime Minister's support, and each of the Ministers lending their weight to the policy, it would not have been pushed into law.

sections.label: Duties for Dr Balaji's ward
sections.summary: He explained to Mr Inderjit Singh and the Prime Minister the duties needed so residents in Dr Balaji's Ang Mo Kio ward would continue to be served.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In the Members' Room, I saw him sit down with Mr Inderjit Singh, and I think the Prime Minister was there, too.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: And he was explaining to Mr Inderjit Singh and the Prime Minister all the duties that had to be fulfilled so that the residents in Dr Balaji's ward in Ang Mo Kio would continue to be served and would not be prejudiced by his illness.

sections.label: Motivation and teamwork in Parliament
sections.summary: The speaker concludes that right motivation and teamwork produce an effective Parliament, Cabinet, Prime Minister and strong leader.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The conclusion I have drawn thus far is that, if there is right motivation and there is teamwork, we will have an effective and efficient Parliament, which makes for an effective and efficient Cabinet, which makes for an effective and good Prime Minister; a strong leader.

sections.label: Values and principles for Singapore
sections.summary: The speaker values incorruptibility, aspiration, right motivations, selfless service and teamwork as the genetic make-up of any team propelling Singapore forward.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: It matters less to me the good traits of an individual or a group of individuals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: It matters more to me that the values and principles of incorruptibility, the dare to aspire, the right motivations, importance of selfless service and strong teamwork continue to be the genetic make-up of any team that is to propel Singapore to greater heights.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: That makes for a very secure formula, a very unique formula, that will benefit Singaporeans for generations to come.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: That formula of teamwork will ensure that Singaporeans will win.   3.02 pm

sections.label: Economic and productivity growth figures
sections.summary: Last year the economy grew 3.6%, labour productivity grew 4.5%, fewer workers were retrenched and real wages rose for all income groups.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Last year, our economy grew at 3.6%, exceeding forecasts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Overall, labour productivity grew at 4.5%, marking the highest productivity growth since 2010, fewer workers were retrenched for the first time in seven years and real wages rose steadily for all income groups.

sections.label: Predicted severe talent crunch
sections.summary: A Korn Ferry Futurestep study predicted Singapore faces high risk of a severe talent crunch, short of over one million skilled workers by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: A recent study by Korn Ferry Futurestep predicted that Singapore will be one of the countries with the highest risks of a severe talent crunch, estimating that we will be short of more than one million skilled workers by 2030.

sections.label: SkillsFuture cited as global best practice
sections.summary: The World Economic Forum's White Paper on the Fourth Industrial Revolution highlights Singapore's SkillsFuture movement as a global best practice and role model.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: In fact, the World Economic Forum’s White Paper on Realising Human Potential in the Fourth Industrial Revolution actually highlights Singapore’s SkillsFuture movement as a global best practice and role model.

sections.label: SkillsFuture evolving to link learning and jobs
sections.summary: The movement must evolve from offering thousands of courses to a system linking lifelong learning to skills and jobs dynamically.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: The movement needs to evolve from one that prides itself on offering thousands of courses in a plethora of fields catering to individuals’ interests, to a system that lays out a clear path linking lifelong learning to skills and jobs dynamically.

sections.label: World Economic Forum jobs report
sections.summary: The World Economic Forum's Future of Jobs report estimates 35% of core skills for today's jobs will change or be wholly new by 2020.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: The World Economic Forum’s report on the Future of Jobs estimates that 35% of core skills required to perform today’s jobs will change or be wholly new by the year 2020.

sections.label: SkillsFuture for ITMs proposal
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Government to consider launching SkillsFuture for ITMs to align training with industry needs and future growth.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: With our economic transformation efforts focused around the 23 ITMs, I urge the Government to consider launching SkillsFuture for ITMs, in order to ensure strong alignment of training efforts with industry needs and future growth.

sections.label: Integrating job-matching efforts
sections.summary: Job-matching efforts should be integrated with SkillsFuture, ITMs and income safety nets during periods of displacement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Job-matching efforts should be integrated with SkillsFuture and ITMs as well as income safety nets during periods of displacement.

sections.label: Differentiated foreign manpower intake
sections.summary: The speaker supports a manpower-lean approach and maintaining the local-to-foreign talent ratio, but urges a differentiated foreign manpower intake approach.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: I support the manpower-lean approach as the way forward and agree that we should maintain the overall ratio of local to foreign talent in our workforce.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: However, we should review our foreign manpower policy to introduce a differentiated intake approach to enable acquisition of capability in new domains critical to Singapore's future growth, such as expertise in data analytics, artificial intelligence and cybersecurity, whilst balancing this with reduced intakes in other areas.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: So, rather than adopting a one-size-fits-all approach, foreign manpower policy should evolve to include skill-based factors that prioritises certain types of skills and expertise over others, within a quota system.

sections.label: Cost of living and GST
sections.summary: Cost of living issues have dominated headlines, with more price rises and a prospective GST hike raising anxieties further.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In the last few years, cost of living issues have dominated the headlines and more price rises are on the way, with a prospective hike in the Goods and Services Tax in the near future raising anxieties further.

sections.label: Enhanced GST U-Save Voucher
sections.summary: At Budget 2018 the Government enhanced the GST U-Save Voucher, giving eligible households $5 more every three months from 2019 to 2021 for the carbon tax.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: One response to pre-empt cost of living concerns by the Government at Budget 2018 has been to enhance the GST U-Save Voucher, with each eligible household standing to receive $5 more every three months between 2019 and 2021 to compensate for the recently announced carbon tax.

sections.label: Transport costs to rise
sections.summary: The Transport Minister confirmed Singaporeans can expect transport costs to rise soon, reflecting growing network capacity and ridership.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: At the Committee of Supply debate this year, the Transport Minister confirmed that Singaporeans can expect to see a rise in transport costs in the very near future, too, to reflect growing network capacity and ridership.

sections.label: Raising Total Fertility Rate
sections.summary: Raising the Total Fertility Rate is an existential issue, with a survey showing couples want more children but cite financial costs, stress and work-family demands.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Raising our Total Fertility Rate (TFR) is an existential issue for our nation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We know from a recent Government survey that many married Singaporean couples actually do wish to have three or more children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Similarly, while 53% of couples ideally wanted two children, only 37% were able to actualise it; 61% of respondents raised financial costs as their first out of three reasons for not having more children, followed closely by the stress of raising children in Singapore at 56%, and the difficulty of managing work and family demands at 33%.

sections.label: 4G leadership and finances
sections.summary: The 4G leadership takes power as expenditures rise with changing demographics, with Temasek in the NIRC framework and a $15.7 billion surplus for FY2016 and 2017.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Unlike their predecessors, the 4G leadership is coming into power when expenditures will rise in concert with the changing demographics in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On the question of finances, the inclusion of Temasek into the Net Investment Returns Contribution (NIRC) framework from 2016 has also put more money and, by extension, more political capital in the hands of the current Government and 4G leaders than any generation of PAP leaders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To put this in perspective, the overall Budget surplus for this term of Government for FY2016 and 2017 is currently at $15.7 billion and this is after transfers to endowments and trust funds like the GST Voucher Fund.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The $15.7 billion could potentially cover two more Pioneer Generation Packages of about $8 billion each, covering almost an additional one million more elderly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In comparison, the first and only drawdown of the reserves in 2009 requiring Presidential approval amounted to $4.9 billion for the Jobs Credit scheme, which extended a cash grant for every local worker on a qualifying employer’s payroll, with a smaller amount allocated to financial institutions for the Special Risk Sharing Initiative.

sections.label: Insufficient skills coverage
sections.summary: The speaker believes Singapore uniquely faces not a skills gap problem but insufficient skills coverage.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In other words, I strongly believe what Singapore faces quite uniquely among advanced economies is not so much a problem with skills gaps, but more one of insufficient skills coverage.

sections.label: Workforce skills as crux
sections.summary: The speaker believes the crux of ongoing industry transformation efforts is workforce skills.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In short, Sir, I believe that the crux of the on-going industry transformation efforts is workforce skills.

sections.label: SkillsFuture and government roles
sections.summary: SkillsFuture focuses on skills issues, and all Government Ministries and agencies have a role in skills development beyond the natural lead agencies.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The SkillsFuture movement is providing a much needed focus on the skills issues.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Even though the Ministry of Education (MOE) is the one coordinating all these efforts through SkillsFuture Singapore, all Government Ministries and agencies have a role to play in this and I would urge each and everyone to accept the role on the skills endeavour entrusted upon them as leaders in all areas of skills development.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The roles of Ministries, such as MOM, MTI, the Ministry of Communications and Information (MCI), the Ministry of Finance and agencies, such as the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) and the National Research Foundation, are clear but they must go beyond these natural lead agencies to include all others who have influence over shaping work attitudes and, therefore, work ethics.

sections.label: Equality of opportunity over income inequality
sections.summary: The speaker argues focus should be on equality of opportunity, not income inequality, and that these efforts must be refreshed across life stages.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Although income inequality is a legitimate concern, I would argue that we should focus on it not to the exclusion of the much more fundamental need to ensure equality of opportunity.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Singapore has strong and reliable institutions which provide opportunities for all segments of society to access basic social and municipal services, not to mention opportunities for social mobility.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Ultimately, better equality of opportunity should reduce income inequality in the long run but it cannot be something that can be done in a rush.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Singapore has grown from strength to strength over more than 50 years because of focus on equality of opportunity when it comes to jobs, in particular.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is important to refresh and rejuvenate these efforts in the current industry transformation push and to continue to emphasise equality of opportunity in acquiring skills at every stage of our citizens' lives, regardless of whether it is in the schools, in National Service, in the workforce, in re-employment or even as a non-working member of society.

sections.label: Industry Transformation Map objectives and reach
sections.summary: The Industry Transformation Map objectives are good, but the plans have not been widespread across industry sectors and impact is not felt throughout.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: For example, the objectives of the Industry Transformation Map, are good.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The Industry Transformation Map (ITM) plans have not been widespread throughout the different sectors of industry.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The impact is felt at some level but not felt throughout.

sections.label: ITM not one size fits all
sections.summary: An ITM within a sector cannot be a one size fits all approach.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: ITM within a sector cannot be a one size fits all.

sections.label: ITM strategy and industry consolidation
sections.summary: The ITM strategy covers skills, innovation and facilitating consolidation, with workforce transition and skilling across different sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: It is part and parcel of building a stronger industry.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: So, the ITM strategy is not just about skills nor innovation; it may also be facilitating this consolidation, having a broad view about what the sector should do and, also in this consolidation process, transition to workforce within the sector, change their jobs, you can skill them, skill them differently so they have jobs all across different sectors.

sections.label: ESG identifying industries for consolidation
sections.summary: ESG needs to identify industries requiring consolidation, expansion or innovation, but not all industries should be managed the same way.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: ESG needs to identify industries that require consolidation, expansion or innovation but not all industries should be managed in the same manner.

sections.label: Streamlining grants and schemes under ITM
sections.summary: Grants and schemes across different Ministries can be streamlined, perhaps under the ITM for each sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: As for grants and schemes, we can streamline the grants and schemes across different Ministries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Maybe it should be streamlined under the ITM for each sector.

sections.label: Overseas markets for startups
sections.summary: It says solutions can start here but businesses must launch overseas, beyond Singapore, to commercialise and survive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: We can start and develop our solutions here.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: It is a springboard but you definitely have to launch your business or startup almost immediately overseas – markets beyond Singapore – to commercialise what you have developed with a chance to succeed or survive.

sections.label: New economic growth indicators
sections.summary: It states that what cannot be measured cannot be managed, and new indicators to measure economic growth and success are probably needed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: But we cannot manage what we cannot measure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: We probably need new indicators to measure economic growth and success.

sections.label: Chan Chun Sing on connectivity
sections.summary: It says Mr Chan Chun Sing mentioned the need for connectivity, the importance of talent, and making 300 million friends and fans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Mr Chan Chun Sing mentioned the need for connectivity and the importance of talent for Singapore as well as saying that we need to make 300 million friends and fans.

sections.label: Government, labour laws, work environment
sections.summary: It says the Government must guarantee a level playing field between organisational forms, and labour laws, regulations and the work environment need rethinking.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The state or Government must be the guarantor of a level playing field between organisational forms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: And one thing is certain: we will need to rethink our labour laws and regulations and the whole work environment – training, retirement and unemployment insurance – in a world of rapid technological and organisational change.

sections.label: Global talent and redistribution
sections.summary: It says countries not competing globally for talent cannot redistribute wealth to the poor, so Singapore must be more flexible to global talent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: So, countries not taking part in this global competition for talent will not be able to redistribute wealth to the poor, because the poor will be all that they have.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: So, as such, it is inevitable that Singapore will have to be more flexible to global talent to make our economy more vibrant and to, surprisingly, make us more inclusive too.

sections.label: TAFEP protecting employee rights
sections.summary: It says TAFEP has used various methods to protect employee rights and combat workplace discrimination and inequality, referring complaints to MOM when warranted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Over the years, TAFEP has relied on a range of methods to protect employee rights and combat workplace discrimination and inequality.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: TAFEP would refer complaints to MOM if further investigations are warranted.

sections.label: TAFEP top worker grievance
sections.summary: TAFEP says this grievance was the top complaint of Singaporean workers for five years and a third of 213 grievances in 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: According to TAFEP, it remained the top gripe of Singaporean workers for five years in a row and made up a third of the 213 grievances lodged in 2015.

sections.label: Legal powers for TAFEP
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Minister for Manpower to consider giving TAFEP legal powers to act on errant employers flouting discrimination laws.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Upskilling is certainly important and a personal responsibility, but we also must give Singaporeans the assurance that they will get jobs if they work for it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: So, I urge the Minister for Manpower – and I think it is somewhat highlighted in the Addendum for MOM – to consider giving TAFEP legal powers to act on errant employers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: It is necessary to go beyond curtailing work passes to penalise employers who are blatantly flouting discrimination laws.

sections.label: Future Ready Fund proposal
sections.summary: The Government may consider setting up a Future Ready Fund beyond the SkillsFuture Study Award for employers, corporates and SMEs to tap.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The Government may want to consider setting up a Future Ready Fund beyond the existing SkillsFuture Study Award for employers that we have now, where corporates and SMEs can tap.

sections.label: Regulating cryptocurrency platforms
sections.summary: The speaker notes ASEAN's 490 fintech companies and says it is time to look into policies legalising and regulating cryptocurrency platforms and exchanges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In ASEAN, we have the largest sector, of which, 490 fintech companies that we have – the top few of our most well-funded fintech companies deal with cryptocurrency platforms and exchanges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I do think it is time to start looking into policies legalising and regulating it.

sections.label: Fintech grants and digital divide
sections.summary: MAS launched grants under StartupSG, and the speaker hopes for more assistance for companies' financial technologies while warning of a digital divide and rising global inequality.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The MAS has launched several grants to support fintech ventures, consolidated under StartupSG.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: And, while the focus appears to be on startups, I hope more assistance can also be given to companies to create and expand their own financial technologies, such as cashless payment apps and online purchasing platforms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: At the same time, technology potentially causes a digital divide between the rich and the poor, adding yet another level of social disparity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Global inequality is on the rise, according to the World Inequality Report.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: We must be mindful to ensure that wealth is fairly distributed, that the poor continue to get their needs met and they can go on to obtain skills and education to support their families and, in turn, our economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: We are at the cusp of a technological revolution and we must work doubly hard to make sure no one gets left behind. 4.00 pm

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I believe we can aid our efforts in each of these areas, to greater or lesser degrees, by an increased focus on our school curriculum on teaching Bahasa Melayu.

sections.label: Conversational Malay in primary school
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether conversational Bahasa Melayu could be part of the regular primary school syllabus without exams, citing multiculturalism and learning languages young.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It will also protect and preserve our multi-culturalism and promote national integration and a sense of identity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We currently have conversational third language programmes for Malay at the primary school level as enrichment, but not as part of the regular curriculum.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As learning languages is best done when young, could we look into making the conversational Bahasa Melayu programme part of the syllabus for our primary school students who do not otherwise learn Malay, perhaps included as part of the regular curriculum for every primary school student, but without the pressure of exams?

sections.label: Teaching Bahasa Melayu to non-Malay students
sections.summary: A speaker suggests that in the next 50 years, non-Malay students study Bahasa Melayu, the national language, to basic proficiency through the education system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   Mr Speaker, Sir, the President said that in the last 52 years, through the education system, we adopted a common working language in English that enabled our diverse communities to interact with one another and succeeded in nurturing a distinct Singapore identity and that we have come far.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I suggest that we complement this nation building effort in the next 50 years and enable, through our education system, all non-Malay students to study Bahasa Melayu, our national language, to basic levels of proficiency.

sections.label: Bahasa Melayu as national language
sections.summary: Bahasa Melayu is Singapore's national language, an important tool of nation building that promotes communication among the Chinese, Malays and Indians.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In Mr Lim’s words applied to today’s Singapore, Bahasa Melayu is our national language, it is an important tool of nation building and promotes the communication among the three main races in Singapore: the Chinese, Malays and Indians.

sections.label: Studying school-based volunteer programmes
sections.summary: The passage cites NVPC's finding that one in three Singaporeans volunteered in 2016 and calls for studying the effectiveness of school-based volunteer programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The National Volunteer & Philanthropy Centre (NVPC) found that one in three Singaporeans volunteered in 2016, up from one in 10 in year 2000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: And we have SG Cares, a brilliant initiative to increase acts of kindness and volunteerism.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: To further increase volunteerism and sustain it, perhaps we first need to take a step back and study the effectiveness of our school-based volunteer programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It is important as that lays the foundation in our youths for volunteerism.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Mr Kwan Jin Yao raised several points about this, including, "To what extent does involvement in VIA, Community Involvement Programme (CIP) and service-learning projects affect whether students continue volunteering after graduation?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Are students who chalked up a high number of VIA or CIP hours more likely to volunteer for a social cause after leaving school?"  Ms Tan Rong Ying's view was that, "It is important to reconsider the rewards and mandatory aspect of volunteerism in schools so as to increase and make clearer students' intrinsic motivations.

sections.label: Employers and volunteer leave
sections.summary: The passage cites Salesforce Singapore's seven days of annual volunteer leave and hopes the Public Service extends public servants' one-day volunteer leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: To ensure the flames of volunteerism is not extinguished by the demands of work, employers are a key partner in building a nation of volunteers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We need to follow the positive example set by Salesforce Singapore, which offers seven days of volunteer leave annually.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: They have a particularly successful volunteer scheme with all of their employees making use of their volunteer leave in 2016 and clocking in more than 11,000 hours.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I hope the Public Service, as the largest employer, can take the lead by extending the one-day volunteer leave currently given to public servants and consider allowing them to use their leave in blocks of hours instead of full days.

sections.label: Regular consultations with civil society
sections.summary: The speaker hopes Ministries consider making consultations with civil society organisations a regular part of policy- and law-making.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: As such, I hope that the Ministries consider making consultations with civil society organisations a regular part of the policy- and law-making process.

sections.label: Meritocracy's limits
sections.summary: The passage states meritocracy is the fairest allocation system when working properly but is imperfect, especially when narrow, brittle or monopolised over generations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: When working properly, it is the fairest allocation system imaginable.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: But meritocracy is not a perfect system and does not always work properly, especially when it is a narrow and brittle one; one which only focuses on outcome or engenders ruthless competition, at the expense of cooperation; or one where those who have more at the starting line monopolise success over generations.

sections.label: Singapore brand of meritocracy
sections.summary: Amid anxieties over immigration and resources in Europe, Singapore must grow its own brand of meritocracy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Some in Europe are turning towards extreme right-wing parties amidst anxieties over immigration, at a time when the struggling masses feel the squeeze for resources and space and their lack of progress.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: That is why we must grow a Singapore brand of meritocracy.

sections.label: Three ingredients of meritocracy
sections.summary: Singapore's meritocracy has three ingredients: successful giving back, common spaces and experiences, and Government support, with a Bernanke quote on luck.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Singapore's brand of meritocracy is characterised by three ingredients: first, the successful giving back to society; second, common spaces and experiences for all Singaporeans; and third, support from the Government.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: I quote from an address entitled "The Ten Suggestions" at Princeton University in 2013 by then-US Federal Reserve Chairman Ben Bernanke: "A meritocracy is a system in which the people who are the luckiest in their health and genetic endowment; luckiest in terms of family support, encouragement and probably income; luckiest in their educational and career opportunities; and luckiest in so many other ways difficult to enumerate – these are the folks who reap the largest rewards." It is tempting for those who have succeeded to attribute their success solely to their own capabilities and efforts.

sections.label: SG Cares movement
sections.summary: Everybody can join the SG Cares movement to play a part and give back.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Everybody can join the SG Cares movement to play a part and give back.

sections.label: Meritocracy moral, not resource allocation
sections.summary: Meritocracy is moral when the successful feel duty to society and share success rather than hoard gains.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: And that is because success that benefits others is success which we all can be grateful for.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: This is how meritocracy can be moral and not just a method of allocating resources: when the successful demonstrate a sense of duty to society, when the successful share the fruits of success with others, instead of hoarding the gains for themselves.

sections.label: Meritocracy benefiting others
sections.summary: Meritocracy functions morally when the rewarded benefit others and help them succeed, narrowing social distance while improving the Gini coefficient.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Whether the outcome of meritocracy is the accumulation of wealth or authority, it will only function morally when those who are rewarded find ways to benefit others and help others succeed too.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: This is how we can narrow our social distance, even as we improve the Gini coefficient.

sections.label: Rental housing distribution
sections.summary: Basic rental housing must give tenants a decent home, and Government must distribute rental housing across the island and mix public and private housing.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Our most basic rental housing must, therefore, continue to provide tenants with a decent home.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: That is also why as the Government shapes our future urban landscape, it must distribute rental housing across the island and mix public and private housing more deliberately.

sections.label: Shared responsibility for heartland schools
sections.summary: Singaporeans must resist pushing undesirable facilities into rental blocks and keep providing good teachers and resources to heartland schools.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Every Singaporean must play our role – resist the "not in my backyard" tendency to shove critical but undesirable facilities like funeral parlours behind rental blocks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: We must continue to provide the best teachers and educational resources to our heartland schools and maintain our motto of "Every School a Good School".

sections.label: Equalising opportunities since Independence
sections.summary: Since Independence, policies have tried to equalise opportunities for each generation, though outcomes can never be equalised.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Since Independence, our policies have attempted to equalise the opportunities for each generation, even as we know that we can never equalise outcomes.

sections.label: Meritocracy leaving nobody behind
sections.summary: Singapore's meritocracy must leave nobody behind, with government policies acting as enablers, ladders and bridges for upward mobility.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: The Singapore brand of meritocracy must ensure that nobody is left behind.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: First, Government policies have to act as enablers, as ladders and bridges, to provide a fair chance for everyone to move up in society, not only across families of jobs, but also over time.

sections.label: SkillsFuture and future workforce readiness
sections.summary: The workforce must be ready for future opportunities as current skills may become redundant, with investment in SkillsFuture and ITMs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: It has already recognised that the workforce must be ready for future opportunities, as their current skills could become redundant.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: We are investing in SkillsFuture to support the lifelong development of skills and knowledge, and ITMs to enable our workforce to seize opportunities in the future economy, a future that, as former Minister Lim Swee Say observed, will see workers transit "from one job in one career" to "many jobs in many careers".

sections.label: Malay post-secondary education rise
sections.summary: In 1980, 2.3% of Malay residents attained post-secondary education and above, rising to almost 40% in 2015.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: The evidence is this: in 1980, only 2.3% of Malay residents attained post-secondary education and above.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: However, this figure increased steadily to almost 40% of Malay residents in 2015.

sections.label: Asatizah Recognition Scheme accreditation
sections.summary: Religious messages must be effective and relevant to life in Singapore, so the Asatizah Recognition Scheme must be strengthened and led by the Mufti's Office.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: This is because the religious message must be effective and relevant to life in Singapore and should not merely be appealing to the listener.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Therefore, we must ensure that the Asatizah Recognition Scheme (ARS) continue to strengthen and be led by the Mufti’s Office and supported by our religious teachers, to accredit religious teachers so that teachings are conducted in line with Singapore’s way of life and context, without compromising basic Islamic values.

sections.label: MESRA community focus at WGS
sections.summary: MESRA will have a community focus at Wisma Geylang Serai under Dr Mohamad Maliki, and such programmes will be increased in more residential areas and at the MESRA Centre.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Soon, MESRA will have a community focus at Wisma Geylang Serai (WGS) under the leadership of Senior Minister of State Dr Mohamad Maliki which will be sustained for the benefit of the community.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: This clearly proved to be attractive to new segments of our community.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: We will increase such programmes and implement them in more residential areas as well as at the MESRA Centre in WGS.

sections.label: People's Association Advisory Council of MESRA
sections.summary: The People's Association Advisory Council of MESRA is established, comprising seven advisors, MESRA's highest Exco and professional members.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: With this, I am heartened to announce the establishment of the People’s Association Advisory Council of MESRA comprising seven advisors, MESRA’s highest Exco and those professional members.

sections.label: Officeholder MPs work as one team
sections.summary: The officeholder MPs will work together as one united team, and Zaqy Mohamad is appointed Vice-Chairman of MENDAKI.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Second, since the effort to drive M3 to overcome the community’s challenges is a heavy one, we, the officeholder MPs – that is, myself, Senior Minister of State Dr Mohamad Maliki, Minister of State Zaqy Mohamad, Senior Parliamentary Secretary Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim and Senior Parliamentary Secretary Amrin Amin – will work together as one united team.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: As the first step, I am appointing Minister of State Zaqy Mohamad as the Vice-Chairman of MENDAKI.

sections.label: M3 institutions as one ecosystem
sections.summary: M3 institutions should strengthen their networks to become an effective last mile and exist as one ecosystem delivering one another's and Government programmes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: I think that we have sufficient programmes produced by M3 institutions and their affiliates to assist the community and help it progress, including programmes by the Government.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Therefore, we would like M3 to develop and strengthen the respective networks in order to become an effective "last mile": MUIS with our mosques, madrasahs and religious leaders; MENDAKI with its Malay/Muslim affiliate bodies; and MESRA with the professionals and the general public.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Moving forward, all their institutions and networks must exist as one ecosystem whereby the three institutions are not only innovative when crafting community programmes, but also help one another by delivering the other institution’s programme as well as Government programmes through their networks, wherever it can be beneficial.

sections.label: Malay/Muslim community standing collaboration
sections.summary: The collaboration will enhance the Malay/Muslim community's standing from a model minority into an exceptional minority community, like the Gurkha community.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Our collaboration will enhance the standing of the Malay/Muslim community in Singapore, from a model minority community into an exceptional minority community just like the Gurkha community whose members are known for their courage in the battlefield and are an exceptional Nepalese minority community.

sections.label: Singapore brand of meritocracy
sections.summary: The Singapore brand of meritocracy must remain the means to build a good society, not just a richer society.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: The Singapore brand of meritocracy must remain the means to build a good society, not just one to build a richer society.

sections.label: Social class divide in Singapore
sections.summary: The speaker notes friends from the same school and class, and cites an IPS study showing social ties and divides follow class more than race or religion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Her circle of friends was mainly from the same school, the same social class as her.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Thus, it is not surprising that the IPS study on social capital in Singapore showed that those staying in private housing are more likely to have ties with people staying in private housing as compared to those staying in public housing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: In fact, the IPS survey reveals that the social divide in Singapore is more likely based on class rather than race or religion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: To this end, I am glad that the President acknowledged the need for the 4G leaders to deal with income inequality and social stratification seriously in her Address.

sections.label: Study on school attendance
sections.summary: A 2016 study showed children from higher socio-economic backgrounds are more likely to attend IP Secondary schools, affiliated Primary schools and GEP schools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: A 2016 study showed that children from higher socio-economic backgrounds are more likely to attend Integrated Programme (IP) Secondary schools and their affiliated Primary schools as well as those that offer the Gifted Education Programme (GEP).

sections.label: RI and RGS intake
sections.summary: RI and RGS still take students from roughly the same number of Primary schools, but the speaker estimates less than half come from non-elite primary schools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Today, RI and RGS still take in students from roughly the same number of Primary schools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: However, my estimate is that less than half are from the "non-elite" primary schools.

sections.label: Nomination for non-elite students
sections.summary: Concerned that elite school intake is narrowing by family affluence, the speaker suggests each non-elite Primary principal nominate one deserving student to a top Secondary school.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Despite the claim that "Every School is a Good School", I am concerned that the range of students getting into the perceived “elite” schools in Singapore is narrowing in terms of family affluence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: To address this issue, I would like to suggest that the principal of each “non-elite” Primary school be allowed to nominate one deserving student from their respective school to enter a top Secondary school. “Deserving” implies that the student is of the intellect, temperament and potential to go to a top school.

sections.label: Increase in SAP schools
sections.summary: The number of SAP schools increased from nine to 11 in 2011, and many have developed into elite schools with success stories.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: The number of SAP schools has increased from the original nine to 11 in 2011.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: SAP schools are very popular and many of the SAP schools have also developed into elite schools and their success stories abound.

sections.label: Question on SAP schools
sections.summary: Many people are asking whether SAP schools are still needed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Many people are asking: do we still need to have SAP schools?
