sections.label: SAP schools and non-Chinese students
sections.summary: The Chinese tradition of SAP schools cultivates bi-culturalism, but their development has hindered non-Chinese students, as only those who studied Higher Chinese can attend; the policy could be reviewed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Hence, the Chinese tradition of the SAP schools is a very important factor in cultivating bi-culturalism in Chinese and English.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: However, the development of SAP schools has hindered the chance of non-Chinese students entering SAP schools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Now, only those who have studied Higher Chinese can go to a SAP school.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: To fix this faultline, perhaps we can review the policy and allow non-Chinese students to attend SAP schools.

sections.label: Lowering SAP school threshold
sections.summary: Lowering the threshold for non-Chinese students to go to SAP schools is complicated and sensitive, and MOE should discuss it with people from all walks of life.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Lowering the threshold for non-Chinese students to go to SAP schools is a complicated and sensitive issue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: I hope MOE can face the issue squarely and discuss with people from all walks of life.

sections.label: Policies to fight inequality
sections.summary: Three sets of policies are proposed to fight inequality and bridge social divides, the first being making SG Cares a centerpiece of Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: With that in mind, I would like to propose three sets of policies that can fight inequality and bridge social divides.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: First of all, by making SG Cares a centerpiece of Singapore.

sections.label: Extending SG Cares nationwide
sections.summary: SG Cares is piloted in two towns, and over the next five years it could be extended and connected with the five CDCs and grassroots across Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: SG Cares is already piloted in two towns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Over the next five years, I hope we can extend and connect SG Cares with our five Community Development Councils (CDCs), as well as with the grassroots across Singapore.

sections.label: Piloting SG Cares collaboration
sections.summary: Over the next two years, the SG Cares/CDC/grassroots collaboration could be piloted for a quarter of all Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: At the same time, I am advocating that over the next two years, we can consider piloting the SG Cares/CDC/grassroots collaboration for a quarter of all Singapore.

sections.label: MAS and MTI mandates
sections.summary: MAS can mandate unified presentation of interest rates and a simplified template for mass-market financial product information, while MTI can tighten hire-purchase regulations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: MAS can mandate businesses to present interest rates to consumers in a unified manner.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: MAS can also mandate a simplified template for presenting mass-market financial product information.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: MTI can tighten the hire-purchase regulations to clean up unfair practices and charges that some of our needy get entangled with.

sections.label: Spent criminal records review
sections.summary: A former inmate with no prior convictions and jailed up to three months or fined up to $2,000 can apply to have the record spent after five crime-free years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Today, a former inmate with no prior convictions and who is jailed for no more than three months or fined no more than $2,000, can apply for the criminal record to be spent after a five-year crime-free period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Perhaps, MHA can review and propose a wider scope of criminal records that can be spent over time, if former inmates go through voluntary community rehabilitation.

sections.label: 4G leadership earning trust
sections.summary: The speaker says Mdm President's Address stressed that 4G leaders must earn trust and connect with Singaporeans by listening and showing they have heard.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: These were all addressed by Mdm President and they struck a cord with all Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But to me, Sir, the most important points of Mdm President's Address were about the 4G leadership earning the trust and connecting with Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The trust that we currently have between Singaporeans and the Government will not automatically pass on from one generation to another.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: She added, the 4G Leaders they will need to listen to the views and feelings of the people and, by their own words and deeds, show that they have heard”.

sections.label: Self-awareness for leaders
sections.summary: A MIT Sloan Management Review paper cited self-awareness as the most important leadership capability, and a Korn Ferry study found it impacts company bottom lines.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In a paper published in the MIT Sloan Management Review in February this year, self-awareness was cited as the most important capability for leaders to develop.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A Korn Ferry International study also found that self-awareness impacts the bottom lines of companies.

sections.label: Trust and 4G bold moves
sections.summary: The speaker says President Halimah Yacob asked 4G leaders to make bold moves, which requires trust, and hopes they stay self-aware as trust is earned.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: (In English): Sir, President Halimah Yacob, in her speech, asked for the 4G leaders to make bold moves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For this to happen, trust has to be paramount.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If there is no trust, people will not believe the messenger and bold policy decisions will be that much harder to effect.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: My hope is that the 4G leadership strives to be continually self-aware as they engage with the people of Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Trust is earned, not given; I am confident that the 4G leadership will build their own strong connections in the years ahead. 6.08 pm

sections.label: 3G to 4G transition
sections.summary: Singapore will transit progressively from 3G to 4G over the next two to five years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
sentences.text: Singapore will transit progressively from 3G to 4G over the next two to five years.

sections.label: Feedback Unit formed 1985
sections.summary: In the mid-1980s, as 2G leaders took on daily running of the country, people were asked to air views, and the Feedback Unit, precursor of REACH, formed in 1985.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
sentences.text: After about 20 years in the mid-1980s, as the 2G leaders began to take on the day-to-day running of the country and things settled down a bit, the people were then asked to air their views.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
sentences.text: It is no surprise that the Feedback Unit, which was the precursor of REACH, was formed in 1985.

sections.label: Feedback Unit becomes REACH
sections.summary: Active citizenry was encouraged, shown by the Feedback Unit becoming REACH in 2006.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
sentences.text: Active citizenry was encouraged and this is best encapsulated by the evolution of the Feedback Unit into REACH in 2006.

sections.label: Costs, healthcare, transport concerns
sections.summary: Living costs, healthcare affordability and public transport reliability still elude us, and the PAP Government is committed to address these with the people.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
sentences.text: The only basic or "daily-living" questions that admittedly still elude us a little are the high costs of living, affordability of healthcare and reliability of our public transport system.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
sentences.text: The PAP Government, whether current or future, is determined and committed to address these issues together with the people.

sections.label: 3G and 4G leadership challenges
sections.summary: The 3G leadership gave voice and choice, the 4G should do likewise, while watching technological disruptions, fake news, extremism and the widening social and income divide.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
sentences.text: The 3G leadership has evolved and made appropriate changes in giving voice and choice to the people and the 4G leadership should do likewise, albeit in a more challenging environment.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
sentences.text: But there are other forces at work, such as technological disruptions, the proliferation of fake news and sometimes extremist views and ideologies that we need to be watchful about if we are to protect and improve upon the cohesion we have.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
sentences.text: The first challenge is the widening social and income divide.

sections.label: Marshalling the middle ground
sections.summary: The second challenge to cohesion is marshalling the middle ground.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
sentences.text: The second challenge to cohesion is marshalling the middle ground.

sections.label: Shared life anchors and cohesion
sections.summary: The more shared life anchors there are, the more cohesion there is.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
sentences.text: The more shared life anchors we have, the more cohesion we have.

sections.label: 4G leaders and economic transformation
sections.summary: Each generation charts its own way, and the President called on 4G leaders to boldly promote change and lead Singapore into the next development phase.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
sentences.text: As Prime Minister Lee has said, each generation has to chart its own way.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   Mr Deputy Speaker, Sir, the focus of my speech today is: "Building a Government-business collaborative relationship in a new era that is based on mutual trust and mutual learning in order to achieve breakthroughs in transforming the economy." In outlining the Government's policy objectives, the President issued the call that the 4G leaders must boldly promote change and lead Singapore into the next development phase.

sections.label: Government-business collaboration and transformation
sections.summary: It states that understanding industries is hard, so economic transformation needs 4G leaders' courage and new Government-business collaboration based on mutual trust and learning.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In these times and circumstances, it is not easy for the Government to understand deeply the actual situations of various industries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Therefore, to achieve a breakthrough in economic transformation not only requires courage and resolve from 4G leaders, but also the building of a new-era Government-business collaboration that is based on mutual trust and mutual learning, which will help set free the energy of the enterprises with an inclusive mindset.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For example, the Industry Transformation Maps (ITMs) promoted by the Government have already got a clear industry clustering strategy framework.

sections.label: Missed opportunity and new leaders
sections.summary: It says an opportunity was missed, so new leaders designing industrial policies must canvass wide business opinion and understand links between old and new industries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This was an opportunity we missed at the time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Therefore, when a new generation of leaders is designing industrial policies and allocating resources for development, it must canvass opinions from a wide swathe in the business community and, particularly, it must understand the links between the old and new industries.

sections.label: Tripartite cooperative model foundation
sections.summary: It states that the Tripartite cooperative model of workers, businesses and Government has always been an important foundation for Singapore's competitive edge.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Tripartite cooperative model of workers, businesses and the Government has always been an important foundation for Singapore to keep its competitive edge and overcome all difficulties in the past and in the future.

sections.label: Business cooperation and whole-of-nation framework
sections.summary: It states that business cooperation affects economic policy effectiveness, and supports upgrading to a whole-of-nation framework and a new Government-business relationship.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Whether businesses are willing to cooperate with Government policies will affect the effectiveness of national economic policies, especially in this day and age when the business cycle has been greatly shortened and companies have to look much further ahead.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There is a good saying: "If you want to go fast, you go alone; if you want to go far, you go in a group." In the highly versatile market, a temporary success may be due to a single seizure of opportunity, but if you want sustainable development, businesses must build up real strengths.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As Minister Chan Chung Seng has said, we must upgrade from "whole-of-Government" cooperation to a "whole-of-nation" framework in line with the country's strategy to build long-term competitive strengths.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To sum up, I support the Government's policy objectives and look forward to the 4G leaders coming up with a new economic growth blueprint via the new-era Government-business relationship based on mutual trust and mutual learning.

sections.label: Developed countries inward-looking, China Belt and Road
sections.summary: It states that the US and EU are pulling back from trade deals while China rolls out Belt and Road initiatives providing capital to developing countries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The US was once a champion of free trade but, following the last election, has started pulling back from some of these treaties, including the TPP and now the Iran Nuclear Deal, and even NAFTA appears to be under reconsideration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The EU had been considerably expanding both its membership and its areas of coverage, but Brexit – or the British voting to leave EU has marked an important swing away from this trend.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Even as developed countries appear to be becoming more inward-looking, China has taken a different approach.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Its Belt and Road initiatives are being rolled out, providing large amounts of capital to developing countries, both near and far.

sections.label: Singapore venue for Trump-Kim meeting
sections.summary: It states that Singapore was picked as the venue for the historic meeting between President Trump and President Kim.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In this regard, another thing that happened last week – which was a pleasant surprise to many of us and a huge honour for Singapore is that Singapore was picked as the venue for the historic meeting between President Trump and President Kim, a move that may spark a thaw in what is probably one of the last legacies of the Cold War.

sections.label: ASEAN and multilateralism
sections.summary: ASEAN cooperation on a rules-based order, cybersecurity, transnational crime, terrorism and economic integration could show multilateralism still matters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: If ASEAN countries can come together more strongly, this may set a positive example for other regions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I understand that our objectives include committing to a rules-based regional order and to tackle issues, such as cybersecurity, transnational crime and terrorism.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: If we can get important achievements in these, it will be a signal to the rest of the world that multilateralism is still relevant and still important.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: If we can get further economic integration, that will also be an important achievement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I think the best way to sell the message that multilateralism is still an important part of our world is to show that we can thrive through multilateralism.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: If someone else comes on board, I think it will be necessary for them to learn as well.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: So, in the face of countries getting increasingly more insular, I certainly hope that Singapore and Singapore's leaders will continue to prevail as a voice for multilateralism and integration in this world.

sections.label: KidSTART preschool pilot
sections.summary: The Government targets the preschool arena, and KidSTART is a pilot programme aiming to narrow the inequality gap of disadvantaged young children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: One of the areas where the Government has targeted is in the preschool arena.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: KidSTART is a pilot programme that aims to narrow the inequality gap of young children from disadvantaged, less privileged backgrounds.

sections.label: Support for meritocracy
sections.summary: Additional support in housing, education, skills training and employment is needed so meritocracy works and everyone can succeed regardless of background.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: I think it bears repeating and I shall do so briefly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: We need to provide the right additional support to those needing it – in housing, education, skills training and employment – so that meritocracy works well.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Only then can everyone do well through hard work, talent and skills, regardless of their backgrounds.” Mr Speaker, Sir, I see this as a bold shift in the policy stance of the Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: It is a promise, not only to create opportunities for Singaporeans to succeed, but a commitment to provide the “right additional support” to those who need it.

sections.label: Social compact and stratification
sections.summary: If Singaporeans lose belief, social stratification will occur and the social compact will be broken, which must not be allowed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Once any number of Singaporeans loses this belief, social stratification will occur and our social compact will be broken.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: We cannot and must not allow Singaporeans to have a sense of resignation about their station of life or, worse, that of their children.

sections.label: Belief in equal opportunity
sections.summary: All Singaporeans must believe they or their children have equal opportunity, and the new generation of leaders must earn the right to lead.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: As such, all Singaporeans, regardless of background, must believe, deep in their hearts, that they or their children have an equal opportunity to improve their lives and achieve their goals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: So, while the task of “tweaks” or “bold” changes to policies or mechanisms put in place to address inequality is crucial, of equal importance is the need to imbue and inspire the belief amongst Singaporeans that all Singaporeans, regardless of backgrounds, have an equal chance of achieving their dreams and aspirations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: The right to lead has to be earned, trust and bonds have to be forged.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: But this is not the first transition of a new generation of Government leaders and I am fully confident that they will meet the challenges as well as, if not better, than previous generations have.

sections.label: Growth against inequality
sections.summary: Growth with reinvestment in people and communities is a force against inequality, while a slow economy favours old money and rentiers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Because growth, combined with reinvestment in our people and our communities, can be a very powerful force, a force against inequality.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: A slow economy favours old money: those who already own capital; those who already own land; those who can charge rents without labour or innovation; those who build a rentier society without value creation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Quality growth rebalances an economy, so that the rates of return on capital can be matched or surpassed by the rate of return on work, whether it is deeply skilled work, the work that an artisan does with his hands through years of experience and knowledge; the deeply-skilled work that a specialised nurse brings to caring for patients and supporting caregivers.

sections.label: Tripartite reinvestment in workers' skills
sections.summary: The passage states that in Singapore the Government, businesses and workers can reinvest and regenerate, citing tripartite efforts to upgrade workers' skills.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Clayton Christensen calls it “The Capitalist’s Dilemma" – when short-term considerations run up against long-term issues in the business.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: But Mr Speaker, in Singapore, with the support of fellow Singaporeans, the Government, businesses and workers can come together and reinvest and regenerate, for example, investing in workers and shared skills, because it helps workers and helps businesses.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: The ongoing tripartite effort by our brothers and sisters in the Labour Movement to upgrade workers' skills is reinvestment in our human captial, reinvestment in our workforce.

sections.label: FoodInnovate shared infrastructure programme
sections.summary: Enterprise Singapore leads FoodInnovate, a multi-agency programme, with the theme of shared infrastructure such as a high-pressure processing resource.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Enterprise Singapore, one of our agencies, is leading FoodInnovate, a multi-agency programme, and the theme of shared infrastructure comes through again, for example, if you imagine some equipment items, like a high-pressure processing resource (HPPR).

sections.label: Professional Conversion Programme for Southeast Asia
sections.summary: Enterprise Singapore and Workforce Singapore teamed up on a programme helping mid-career professionals develop skillsets for regional Wholesale Trade and Logistics jobs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: For example, Enterprise Singapore and Workforce Singapore have teamed up to help mid-career professionals develop skillsets for regional jobs in the Wholesale Trade and Logistics Sector.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: The programme is called the Professional Conversion Programme for Southeast Asia, but the key message is that there are ongoing reinvestment and regeneration.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: It is one key way in which we can continue fighting inequality.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: We are price takers when the trade system around the world undergoes changes, when oil prices go up and down, when the price of goods shifts.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: But when we invest in our people and continue investing, when we uplift and empower our workers, we build towards better jobs, better prospects and better capability to cope with that cost of living.

sections.label: Motorcycle Certificate of Entitlement prices
sections.summary: The passage asks why the Ministry has not taken bolder steps on motorcycle COE prices burdening low-income owners who need motorcycles as income.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The first is the Certificate of Entitlement (COE) for motorcycles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I have repeatedly highlighted this issue and made several suggestions so that motorcycle owners, especially those from the low-income group who need motorcycles as a source of income, would not need to bear this burden and be able to continue to afford a motorcycle.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Regarding this issue, why has the Ministry not taken a bolder step to regulate and improve the situation for the benefit of the low-income who have been burdened and affected by excessive COE prices?

sections.label: Housing for single parents
sections.summary: The passage states the second example is about housing for single parents, especially unmarried single mothers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The second example is about housing for single parents, especially unmarried single mothers.

sections.label: Single parents and HDB housing policies
sections.summary: The passage states incremental changes have had little impact and many single parents still struggle with HDB's stringent public housing policies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Although some incremental changes have been made, they do not have any great impact or benefits to this group.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: There are still many more single parents who are still burdened by the difficulties of getting a roof over their head and their children’s heads, due to the Housing and Development Board's (HDB's) rather stringent public housing policies.

sections.label: Double standards on sensitive issues
sections.summary: The speaker says ruling party Members raised the same sensitive issue without the reaction non-ruling party members face, and asks leaders not to practise double standards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As we all know, the sensitive issue that I raised has also been highlighted by several Members from the ruling party, but they were not subjected to the same reaction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I asked that our leaders do not practise double standards where only Members from the ruling party are allowed to voice out sensitive issues, whereas if the same issues are highlighted by non-ruling party members, it is deemed unacceptable and inappropriate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Existing policies that have become obstacles, problematic or contradict efforts to achieve the people's aspirations should be revamped, improved or even abolished if necessary.

sections.label: Constructive discussion in democracy
sections.summary: Constructive discussion, bold comments and voicing sensitive issues through correct channels are positive practices in a democracy based on justice and equality.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Constructive discussions, being bold enough to give comments and voicing out sensitive issues via the correct and proper channels, are positive practices in a nation that adopts a system of democracy based on justice and equality.

sections.label: Cash use in Singapore
sections.summary: KPMG reported 60% of consumers and businesses use cash for non-stored-value-facilities payments, while Paypal found 43% of Singaporeans cited cash as most frequent or preferred.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: KPMG reported that 60% of consumers and businesses in Singapore use cash for non-stored-value-facilities payments, whilst Paypal found 43% of Singaporeans cited cash as their most frequent or most preferred mode of payment.

sections.label: NETS machine for hawker payments
sections.summary: A hawker asked for cash, and the speaker said NETS provides the machine free with no transaction fee for at least three years and a one-time cash incentive.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Aunty asked me to pay in cash because she has to switch on a machine, which she hid in a drawer, to confirm receipt of my money after I scan the QR code.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: I said that based on my understanding, the Network for Electronic Transfers (NETS) provides the machine for free and charges no transaction fee for at least three years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: It is free for hawkers and consumers and there is a one-time cash incentive six months after the hawker installs the equipment, so why not try it?

sections.label: QR code payment providers
sections.summary: Besides NETS, Alipay, WeChat Pay, PayLah and FavePay, a local private provider, can offer QR code payment in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Apart from NETS, Alipay, WeChat Pay, PayLah and even FavePay, a local private provider, are able to offer QR code payment in Singapore.

sections.label: Government role in transformation
sections.summary: The Government must play a key role to shepherd this and Singapore's overall transformation and, if need be, dictate technical parameters and solutions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: The Government will need to play a key role to shepherd this and the overall transformation that Singapore is currently undergoing and, if need be, dictate certain technical parameters and solutions.

sections.label: Digital inequality and STEM education
sections.summary: The passage states the need to avoid widening the digital gap and to help students embrace STEM education and appreciate technology.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: We must not inadvertently create a new inequality or widen the existing gap between those who can access and exploit the new digital technologies and those who cannot.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: We need to help our students embrace science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM) education and develop a certain level of appreciation in technology possibilities, even if they do not eventually major in such subjects.

sections.label: Coding in digital economy
sections.summary: Coding is described as fundamental to understanding and designing technology and critical to jobs in a digital economy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Coding is fundamental in understanding and designing technology, critical to jobs in a digital economy.

sections.label: Singapore doing the same
sections.summary: The passage states that Singapore will do well to do the same.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Singapore will do well to do the same.

sections.label: MacPherson digital platform for elderly
sections.summary: In MacPherson a platform is being developed to connect vulnerable elderly to community information, resources, services and support networks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: In MacPherson, we are now developing a platform to pull together different digital solutions aimed at connecting our elderly, especially those who are financially, physically and socially more vulnerable, connecting them to community information, resources and services, such as Friendly Neighbourhood General Practitioner (GP), connecting to existing and new support networks, such as befrienders and volunteers-on-demand – just think of "Uberisation" of volunteerism to meet ad hoc needs.

sections.label: Funding for scaling community platform
sections.summary: The passage states that scaling up would need more resources and that Government funding and support would be useful.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: If successful and, if we are to take it further or scale it up, we will need more resources.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Therefore, it would be most useful if the Government can set aside some funding and support to help enthusiastic communities like ours.

sections.label: Digital economy and Singapore adoption
sections.summary: The digital economy is called important, the Government is promoting it, and Singapore is cited as fastest in digital adoption in Asia Pacific.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Digital economy is one of the most important elements in our future economy and the Government is actively promoting the development and coverage of the digital economy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: According to the 2017 Digital Evolution Index Report, Singapore is the fastest country in terms of digital adoption in the Asia Pacific with significant outcomes in promoting digitalisation and Internet penetration.

sections.label: Digital future and inequality
sections.summary: The Government must ensure everyone is ready for the digital future and shares its fruits, so it does not create new inequalities and wealth gaps.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: The Government has to ensure that everyone, regardless of their background and age, is ready for the digital future and shares the fruit of the digital economy and Smart Nation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: We must make sure that a digital future will not create new inequalities and new wealth gaps inadvertently.

sections.label: Smart Nation as national priority
sections.summary: The transformation into a Smart Nation with a vibrant digital economy needs dreamers and must be a national priority.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: We will need dreamers who do not just want to become successful professionals in traditional jobs, but imagine a new world of exciting possibilities and are prepared to work hard to create this new world.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: This next transformation into a Smart Nation with a vibrant digital economy has to be a national priority.

sections.label: Tripartite partners and Industry Transformation Maps
sections.summary: The tripartite partners have collaborated extensively on the Industry Transformation Maps for the 23 sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: The tripartite partners have collaborated extensively on the Industry Transformation Maps (ITMs) for the 23 sectors.

sections.label: Median income rise
sections.summary: The median income has risen almost 22% in the last five years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: In fact, the median income has risen almost 22% in the last five years.

sections.label: Progressive Wage Model wage gains
sections.summary: The Progressive Wage Model, mooted in 2012 for cleaning, security and landscape, moved wages up for over 70,000 workers, with real median gross wages growing up to 6.4% per annum from 2011 to 2016.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Back in June 2012, the Labour Movement under former Secretary-General Lim Swee Say, mooted the Progressive Wage Model (PWM) for the cleaning, security and landscape sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Collectively, these efforts by the tripartite partners have moved wages up for over 70,000 workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: From 2011 to 2016, the real median gross wages of these workers grew by up to 6.4% per annum.

sections.label: Support for freelancers and independent workers
sections.summary: The Labour Movement will work with the Government to prevent workers stagnating and ensure freelancers, self-employed and part-timers enjoy CPF protection, medical coverage and skills development.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: We will work with the Government for better support and prevent them from stagnating.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: We must also take care of the freelancers, such as food delivery riders, the self-employed, part-timers, people in the creative field and other forms of freelance work.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: With this emerging form of project-based employment, we should ensure that our independent workers enjoy CPF protection, medical coverage and skills development.

sections.label: Teachers welcome Retirement Re-employment Act
sections.summary: Teachers from the Singapore Teachers' Union welcomed the Retirement and Re-employment Act passed last year, which extended the re-employment age to 67.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: In another conversation, this time with teachers from the Singapore Teachers’ Union, they told me they welcomed the Retirement and Re-employment Act that we passed in this Chamber last year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: This Act extended the re-employment age to 67.

sections.label: New Tripartite Committee for ageing workforce
sections.summary: A new Tripartite Committee is proposed to support the ageing workforce and help mature workers continue working if they choose to.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Furthermore, I propose to set up a new Tripartite Committee to provide better support for our ageing workforce and help our mature workers to continue working if they choose to.

sections.label: 23 ITMs launched for businesses
sections.summary: Over the last two years, the Government launched 23 ITMs to help businesses transform and enhance capabilities to seize future opportunities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Over the last two years, the Government has launched 23 ITMs to help businesses transform and enhance capabilities to seize future opportunities.

sections.label: NTUC Training Council and worker courses
sections.summary: NTUC set up the Training Council to turn training roadmaps into programmes, and will introduce suitable courses, encourage employer support, and offer bite-sized modular courses.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: NTUC will strengthen our efforts to help our workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: We have set up the Training Council to turn training roadmaps into training programmes which will benefit our workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: We will design and introduce courses that are suitable for our workers, encourage employers to support their employees to undergo training, and introduce bite-sized modular courses which will allow our workers to acquire new knowledge anytime, anywhere.

sections.label: Monitoring housing, healthcare and education costs
sections.summary: The cost of housing, healthcare and education will be monitored closely, and the Government will continue finding ways to help Singaporeans improve their lives.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: The cost of housing, healthcare and education will be monitored closely.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: The Government will continue to find ways to do more and do better in helping Singaporeans improve their lives.

sections.label: Competent workforce and closing social gaps
sections.summary: A competent, relevant workforce is imperative, and social gaps must be closed by addressing struggles of working people, especially the sandwich middle class and lower-income workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: It is imperative that we have a workforce that is competent and able to stay relevant.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: We must continue to close social gaps by addressing the struggles of all our working people, especially the sandwich middle class and lower-income workers.

sections.label: ITMs and future economy
sections.summary: All ITMs of 23 industries have been launched, drawing up a collective vision for economic transformation requiring collective action.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: With all ITMs of 23 industries launched, the collective vision of transformation for our economy has been drawn up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: We, as stakeholders of our future, now need to take collective action to co-create our future economy together.

sections.label: Jobs assurance and AI impact
sections.summary: Workers need assurance of jobs, and questions were asked on laws and a national study on AI's impact on jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: We also need to assure the working people that there are jobs which they can prepare themselves for and that the Government and Labour Movement will walk with them through this journey of transformation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: This has been the central tenet behind the work undertaken by the Future Jobs, Skills and Training capability at NTUC which was set up last year in January 2017.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: With the advent of the use of AI and autonomous machines, I have previously asked the Government whether new laws and regulations should be promulgated to ensure that we address the issues arising from the development and use of these technologies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: I have also asked if the Government would consider conducting a national study on the potential impact of AI and technology on jobs and on our people to get conversations going and pave the way for ethical development of technology against growing concerns on issues, such as liability, privacy, consent, safety, security, diversity and transparency.

sections.label: Labour Movement jobs and skills work
sections.summary: The Labour Movement shared in-demand jobs and skills, held a forum, and NTUC is identifying jobs at risk of displacement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: In 2017, the Labour Movement shared infographics highlighting the in-demand jobs and skills in the Financial Services, Infocomm and Technology, Healthcare, Engineering in manufacturing and Wholesale Trade sectors with the working people, with a call to action to take up available upskilling programmes to enable them to be equipped with the skills for these in-demand jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: The Labour Movement also held the inaugural Future Jobs, Skills and Training Forum earlier this year in January to envision the future and inspire action among stakeholders through the sharing of opportunities on the horizon for Singapore’s economy, identification of driving forces impacting jobs, uncovering of specific action plans to transit workers from current at-risk jobs to future in-demand jobs and exploring issues concerning skills acquisition and how our learning models have to evolve so that we are able to prepare our workforce for jobs which do not yet exist.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Leveraging the findings from the foregoing, NTUC is working on the identification of jobs at risk of displacement in identified sectors and stands ready to co-create relevant programmes and interventions with our tripartite partners and partners in our expanded Labour Movement network for the progression of our workforce.

sections.label: Job-risk assessment and information sharing
sections.summary: Industries need to conduct job-risk assessment, and employers must promptly share developments with union leaders and workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: First, in order to deal with the challenges brought about by the digital economy, various industries need to conduct job-risk assessment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Second, employers must share with union leaders and workers promptly the latest development, so that they can come up with solutions together to deal with the rapidly changing market and workplace situation.

sections.label: Transport productivity loss concerns
sections.summary: The speaker focuses on transport, asking whether the Government studied productivity loss from train delays and disruptions from 2011 to 2017.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In my speech today, I will be focusing on certain issues relating to our transport.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: At the Committee of Supply debates in 2016 and 2017, I said that we should be greatly concerned over the loss of productivity to all our workers and our economy arising from the manhours lost to all train disruptions and delays over the last few years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I wonder whether the Government has ever done a study to measure the loss of productivity to our economy arising from train delays and disruptions between 2011 and 2017, or the time wasted due to delays from getting to work and getting home after a tired day at work, including unhappiness, stress and anxiety generated.

sections.label: Planning capacity for new MRT lines
sections.summary: With new MRT lines being built, the speaker hopes the Government plans for sufficient and greater capacity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: As our Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) network increases with the building of new MRT lines, such as the Thomson-East Coast Line, Jurong Region Line and Cross-Island Line, I hope that the Government will, for example, be learning from our experience with the North-South and East-West Lines and plan for a system with not merely sufficient capacity when each line opens, but with provisions built into the plans for greater capacity for more or longer trains in all our new lines and greater capacity for passengers in all stations.

sections.label: Active Mobility Act footpath sharing
sections.summary: The Active Mobility Act allows PMD users and cyclists to share footpaths, which was previously prohibited.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The new Active Mobility Act also allows PMD users and cyclists shared use of footpaths which was previously prohibited.

sections.label: Lowering PMD speed limit
sections.summary: It asks whether the Government will consider lowering the PMD speed limit to 15 km per hour across all surfaces, from 25 km per hour on park connectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Will the Government consider lowering the speed limit for PMDs to 15 kilometres (km) per hour across all surfaces?

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Currently, PMDs are allowed up to a maximum of 25 km per hour on park connectors.

sections.label: Airport pollution study proposal
sections.summary: The Minister said no study on air or noise pollution was done and will consider the proposal to study air pollution, with calls to monitor pollution regularly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: According to the Minister, the Ministry has not done any study on air or noise pollution and will consider my proposal of doing a study, especially on air pollution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Government should ensure that the airport extension, together with projected increase in flights, will not lead to an increase in air or noise pollution affecting residents living nearby, say, within a radius of at least 10 km to 15 km of the airport.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: That will hit the estates I mentioned plus, I believe, Bedok, East Coast and even parts of Marine Parade and beyond.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I urge the Government to carry out such a study soon and, in fact, to monitor the pollution levels regularly on a long-term basis as our airport and flights may continue to grow in the coming years.

sections.label: Helping maritime SMEs beyond ITM focus
sections.summary: It asks how to help maritime SMEs that may not benefit from the Sea Transport ITM focus on autonomous systems, robotics, data analytics and digitalisation, and how to encourage them beyond traditional categories.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Our maritime business community consists of many more local SMEs up and down the value chain beyond ships and offshore building and port management.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: How can we help those who may not be able to benefit from the current focus on autonomous systems, robotics, data analytics as well as digitalisation under the current Sea Transport ITM or, for that matter, under any other ITMs?

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: And how can we encourage SMEs to think beyond traditional categories of maritime businesses to come up with products and services that straddle across or beyond traditional categorisations?

sections.label: All 23 ITMs launched
sections.summary: All 23 ITMs have been launched, laying a roadmap to chart the transformation of each industry.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: All 23 ITMs have been launched, laying a roadmap to chart the transformation of each industry.

sections.label: ITMs and at-risk jobs
sections.summary: The ITMs lay a roadmap for future jobs but do not touch on jobs at risk now of becoming obsolete, with employers and workers asking what to train and train for what.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: While the ITMs lay a roadmap for the jobs of the future, they do not touch on the jobs that are at risk right now of becoming obsolete.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Companies are aware that they need to transform their business operations, they are aware that they need to send their workers for training and reskilling.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: But while both employers and workers know that they need to go for training, they are asking two questions: firstly, train what; and secondly, train for what?

sections.label: Strategy centred on 3Rs
sections.summary: The speaker proposes a strategy centred around 3Rs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: To do so, I propose a strategy centred around 3Rs.

sections.label: McKinsey automation job risk study
sections.summary: A McKinsey Global Institute study found up to 800 million workers globally at risk of losing jobs to automation by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: A study by the McKinsey Global Institute found that up to 800 million workers globally are at risk of losing their jobs and replaced by automation by the year 2030.

sections.label: Korn Ferry Singapore talent crunch
sections.summary: A Korn Ferry study found Singapore will lack one million skilled workers by 2030, risking billions in annual losses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: A recent study by HR firm, Korn Ferry, found that Singapore will lack one million skilled workers by 2030.

sentences.text: However, an abdication of responsibility is not what we signed up for and should not be allowed to take root here, neither for our freelancers, nor for our workers.

sections.label: Measures supporting older workers
sections.summary: The passage describes legal protection against age-based termination, wage subsidies, training subsidies and a job redesign grant, and reports higher employment rates for older workers from 2007 to 2017.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Chee How (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: As a result of all these efforts, workers in Singapore have legal backing not to have their services terminated by their companies on account of age alone before reaching the Re-employment Age ceiling, and that ceiling has been raised to 67 last July.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Chee How (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The Special Employment Credit and the Additional Special Employment Credit are two examples of wage subsidies given to employers to defray part of the cost of employing older workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Chee How (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The additional training subsidies, intentionally given to support training undertaken by older workers, is aimed at spurring skills updating and upgrading on the part of our older workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Chee How (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The WorkPro Job Redesign Grant incentivises companies to render their work equipment and processes more age-friendly and even ageless.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Chee How (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: All these measures have helped improve the employment rate for older workers over the years which, for the cohort aged 55 to 59, has increased from 8% to 9.4% between the years 2007 and 2017 and, in the age band from 60 to 64 in those same 10 years from 2007 to 2017, from 3.5% doubling to 7.3% and then, for the even older groups aged 65 to 69 between 2007 and 2017, from 1.7% to 4.1%.

sections.label: Industries with older workers
sections.summary: The passage lists the four industries with the most resident workers aged 50 and above: wholesale and retail trade, transportation and storage, manufacturing, and accommodation and food services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Chee How (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: If we cut it in a different way, we cut it by industry, and then look at which are the four industries with the largest number of workers aged 50 and above, then we will come to these conclusions: the first one, wholesale and retail trade, 140,000 workers above the age of 50, resident workforce; transportation and storage, 93,000 workers; manufacturing, 85,000 workers; accommodation and food services, 66,000 workers.

sections.label: Three Es and ITM skills
sections.summary: The passage sets out extending the working life runway, improving the workplace environment, and enabling older workers, and urges that ITM implementation include uplifting older workers' skills.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Chee How (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The first one is Extend the working life expectancy runway – so, retirement age, re-employment age ceiling, and such items will have to be revisited from time to time; two, improve the workplace Environment – the physical part, the processes, job designs, attitudes, make them more age-universal, age-neutral, ageless; third, Enable and energise our older workers through strengthening their capability and confidence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Chee How (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: What specifically can we do to put into effect these three Es?

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Chee How (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I urge action in three areas: first, make sure that the implementation of the ITMs include the uplifting of older workers' skills.

sections.label: WorkPro uptake and retirement review
sections.summary: The passage says about 650 companies used MOM's WorkPro programme, benefiting some 10,000 older workers, and calls for reviewing retirement and re-employment with tripartite partners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Chee How (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The MOM's WorkPro programme is a very good programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Chee How (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Thus far, some 650 companies have made use of it to redesign their workplaces and processes for greater age-universality, and some 10,000 older workers working for these companies have already benefited.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Chee How (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Ten thousand is an encouraging number but, nonetheless, it still represents a small fraction of the total number of companies, or 650; and the proportion of older workers in Singapore, or 750,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Chee How (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Third, review the way forward for retirement and re-employment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Chee How (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I have spoken on this at this year's Budget Debate about the need for the tripartite partners to come together to discuss the next steps for extending the worklife runway, given that we have reached the earlier stated goal of raising the statutory re-employment age ceiling from 65 to 67, so I shall not repeat myself here.

sections.label: Ageist behaviour and older workers
sections.summary: The message calls for societal pressure against ageist behaviour and tripartite efforts to reward age-friendly companies and promote related initiatives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Chee How (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: This message, I repeat, really, is for both management and our workers because it takes two hands to clap.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Chee How (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: We must thus rally societal pressure against those who persist with ageist behaviour because they are both an affront to fairness and an impediment to progress.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Chee How (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: At the same time, we must redouble our tripartite efforts to nurture, recognise and reward more companies with the right attitudes and practices towards older workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Chee How (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: We must also do our utmost to promote the adoption of the Tripartite Standard on Age-Friendly Workplace Practices, the Human Capital Partnership and other like-minded initiatives to value the initiative, determination and achievement of companies and our older workers.

sections.label: Amazon checkout-free store
sections.summary: Amazon recently launched a checkout-free store in Seattle and is looking to learn from it and expand further.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industy (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Amazon has also recently launched its checkout free store in Seattle in America and is looking to learn from this and expand further.

sections.label: Automation examples in use
sections.summary: Examples already taking place include automation detecting fraud at the Development Bank of Singapore and generating simple news reports and Tweets.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industy (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Some examples which are already taking place include the use of automation in detecting fraud by the Development Bank of Singapore, and in generating simple news reports and Tweets, such as those covering financial and sports results.

sections.label: Productivity growth and slowing labour force
sections.summary: As labour force growth slows, productivity growth will allow economic growth and more resources to support those with less.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industy (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: As our labour force growth slows in the next decade, productivity growth will allow us to achieve economic growth and continue to provide us with more resources as a society, both for ourselves and to support and care for those with less.

sections.label: Strong position for innovation-driven economy
sections.summary: Despite fear and uncertainty, the speaker says Singapore is in a strong position to ride change and create an innovation-driven economy.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industy (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Despite the fear and uncertainty, I can confidently say that we are in a strong position to ride this wave of change and create an innovation-driven economy.

sections.label: Mindset change as hurdle
sections.summary: The speaker says the most difficult hurdle is one of mindset change.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industy (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: In my mind, the most difficult hurdle is one of mindset change.

sections.label: SkillsFuture and lifelong learning
sections.summary: The passage states that continual upgrading and lifelong learning must be developed, and that this is the basis of SkillsFuture.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industy (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: We need to develop in us the DNA of continual upgrading and lifelong learning.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industy (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: This is the basis of the SkillsFuture initiative.

sections.label: Port automation and PSA workers
sections.summary: The port tests automation technologies, and PSA reassured over 1,000 staff that jobs would remain and training would be sponsored.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industy (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: The port has been testing and adopting many automation technologies to enhance productivity.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industy (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: This includes the testing of unmanned automated guided vehicles (AGVs) as well as automated and remotely-controlled yard cranes and quay cranes, which help to provide better service levels and enable our port to remain competitive in the face of mounting global competition.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industy (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: PSA has not pursued automation at the expense of its drivers and crane operators.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industy (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: In fact, automation has allowed for the creation of higher-skilled and better-quality jobs for them.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industy (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: When I spoke to him, he confessed that he was initially apprehensive when PSA decided to automate its yard cranes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industy (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: However, PSA, working together with the Singapore Port Workers Union (SPWU) and the Port Officers’ Union, reassured him as well as the more than 1,000 other PSA staff going through the transformation journey with him, that jobs would still be available for all of them and that PSA would sponsor their training in the required skills.

sections.label: Swee Heng new factory output
sections.summary: The new factory let Swee Heng triple daily production capacity to 30,000 cakes and 120,000 bread dough while cutting manpower by 50%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industy (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: The new factory has enabled Swee Heng to triple its former daily production capacity, and it is now producing 30,000 cakes and 120,000 bread dough daily while, at the same time, reducing the manpower required by an average of 50%.

sections.label: Tablet orders at shopfront
sections.summary: Shopfront retail employees now place orders through tablets instead of paper and fax, cutting order consolidation time by three times.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industy (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Its shopfront retail employees have moved from writing on paper and faxing orders to the headquarters, to placing orders directly through the tablets.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industy (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: This reduces order consolidation time by as much as three times, allowing the production site to have access to quicker and more accurate order information.

sections.label: Listening to workers and businesses
sections.summary: The passage states that workers and business owners must be listened to so strategies and tools evolve with the changing environment.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industy (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: In making our ITMs work, we must continue to listen to our workers and our business owners to ensure that we build this partnership, so that as the transformation progresses and the operating environment changes, our strategies and tools must evolve in tandem to meet those new needs and challenges.

sections.label: ITMs and worker skills
sections.summary: Each ITM is an integrated plan bringing tripartite partners together, with the ultimate aim of equipping workers with the right skills.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industy (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Each ITM is an integrated plan bringing the tripartite partners together to drive change for its particular sector.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industy (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: While the ITMs have, as their starting points the transformation of enterprises, we must not forget that the ultimate aim is to ensure that our workers are equipped with the right skills and knowledge to benefit from the fruits of this transformation and innovation.

sections.label: Adapt and Grow Programme
sections.summary: The Government supports workers to learn and upgrade skills, especially displaced workers, through initiatives like the Adapt and Grow Programme.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industy (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: We heard earlier the resolve of this Government to ensure that inequality does not set in, that we take care of the vulnerable.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industy (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: We need impactful initiatives like the Adapt and Grow Programme in which the Government provides support for our workers to learn and upgrade their skills throughout their lives, with particular attention to helping displaced workers learn new skills and utilise them in better jobs.

sections.label: Air Transport ITC
sections.summary: The Air Transport ITC was set up in 2015 and includes management from CAAS, government agencies, Changi Airport Group, NTUC, airlines and ground handling agents.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industy (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: The Air Transport ITC was set up in 2015 and comprises top management from the Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore (CAAS) and relevant Government agencies, Changi Airport Group, NTUC, the airlines and ground handling agents, which together account for over 85% of total employment in this entire sector.

sections.label: Company-specific operational-technology roadmaps
sections.summary: Companies are supported to develop company-specific operational-technology roadmaps mapping how technologies can meet their needs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industy (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: In such cases, we support companies to develop company-specific operational-technology roadmaps (OTRs) to map out how they can use technologies to meet their needs.

sections.label: Pre-scoped technology solutions and platforms
sections.summary: Firms are offered pre-scoped, pre-approved technology solutions supported by the Productivity Solutions Grant, and technology platforms like the National Trade Platform.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industy (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: First, based on our engagement of firms in the industry, we pre-scope and pre-approve technology solutions which meet the firms’ problem statements.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industy (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: These pre-scoped solutions are specific to the needs of each industry and can be supported through the Productivity Solutions Grant, available online on the Business Grants Portal.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industy (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Our second approach is to develop technology platforms, such as the National Trade Platform, which allow for digitalisation of documentation in the sector and also provide innovative value-added services.

sections.label: Businesses and people leading change
sections.summary: Businesses must lead change and people must upgrade skills, develop ideas and take risks, with collective effort shaping Singapore's future.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industy (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Businesses must lead change as they bring together and organise their resources in new ways, while our people have a responsibility to upgrade their skills, develop new ideas and take risks to make change happen.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industy (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: If we can hunker down and band together, our enterprises and our people will emerge all the better for it.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industy (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Singapore is not defined by the progress and accolades it has achieved, but our constant striving to do better.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industy (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Our story has always been about the future that we create through our collective efforts.

sections.label: Tackling poverty and income inequality
sections.summary: Poverty and lack of mobility from low income are objectionable, so income inequality focus is on poverty, services, education, health and social mobility.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: What is objectionable, therefore, is poverty and lack of mobility arising from low income.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Hence, in dealing with income inequality, the primary focus is on tackling poverty, access to important services, such as education, health, social mobility and social mix.

sections.label: GST impact on low-income families
sections.summary: The Government says low-income families get about $4 in transfer benefits for every dollar of tax paid.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Cost of living issues have a disproportionate impact on low-income families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I note specifically that this Government has committed in the President's Address to "help families cope with the costs of living".

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The Government often refers to the unique structuring of the GST system with voucher schemes extended to low-income families so as to make GST implementation more "progressive" vis-a-vis them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: It is mentioned that for our low-income families, for every dollar they pay in tax, they get about $4 in transfer benefits.

sections.label: Hawker food prices and GST
sections.summary: Hawker and market food prices will be affected by GST, so transfers pegged to GST paid are insufficient.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Yet, hawker and market food prices will naturally be affected by GST and the low-income family will have to pay higher costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Hence, pegging the amount of transfers just on how much GST they directly pay would not be sufficient.

sections.label: Bukit Batok leader's education
sections.summary: She became a Bukit Batok community leader and graduated from NTU with a Second Class Upper Honours degree in accountancy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: She also became a Bukit Batok community leader after graduating from Ngee Ann Polytechnic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: She later secured entry into Nanyang Technological University (NTU) and graduated three years later with a Second Class Upper Honours degree in accountancy.

sections.label: Preschools and compulsory education
sections.summary: The Government pledged to raise preschool quality and help at-risk children, and she raises intervening when children do not attend school.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I am heartened to note that the Government, in the President's Address, pledged to do more in terms of raising the quality of preschools and helping children at risk.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I wish to once again raise for the consideration of the Government the merits of intervening where families do not ensure that their children attend school, in contravention of the Compulsory Education Act.

sections.label: Intervening in dysfunctional families
sections.summary: There may be a need to enhance powers of intervention into dysfunctional families which do not send their children to school.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: To prevent a permanent underclass from taking root in Singapore, there may be a need to enhance powers of intervention into dysfunctional families which do not send their children to school.

sections.label: Co-locating rental flats
sections.summary: She suggests the Government consider returning to co-locating rental flats within regular units.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I agree with them and I would go further.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I suggest that the Government consider going back to the old policy of co-locating rental flats within regular units.

sections.label: Economic growth and social spending
sections.summary: The passage states that without economic growth there will be difficulty, and that social expenditure is close to $40 billion, more than a 100% increase from a decade ago.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Without economic growth – and that is the challenge of the 4G Government leaders – we will face difficulty.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: We are already spending close to $40 billion on social expenditure, which is a more than a 100% increase, compared to the figures a decade ago.

sections.label: Household income versus family income
sections.summary: The speaker says they previously asked in the House why household income, not family income, is used to determine social assistance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I spoke about this before in the House.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I asked why we are still using household income as a determinant for social assistance as opposed to family income.

sections.label: Social spending, families, technology, values
sections.summary: The passage states Singaporeans must accept the Government's duty to spend social funds correctly, families must remain the first line of support, and technology and data analytics should be leveraged.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: All Singaporeans must accept that the Government owes them a duty to ensure that each dollar spent for social spending is spent correctly, and does not allow the expenditure to balloon beyond what is necessary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Therefore, families must continue to remain as the first line of support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Also, the Government needs to leverage more on technology and data analytics to identify families that need Government help and advise families who do not have other options.
