sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In addition, as a country, as a community, we must always promote family values – strong family, strong society, strong country.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: We should nip in the bud the incidents of well-to-do children passing the buck of taking care of their elderly parents to the state.

sections.label: Toxic environment and political recruitment
sections.summary: The passage states that if the environment turns toxic, with warning signs in the digital space, it will be harder to attract able people into politics as 5G leaders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: If the environment turns toxic, and we are seeing warning signs of this in the digital space, I fear that the repercussion will be that it will be more difficult to attract people with ability and the heart to step up, enter politics, become our 5G leaders and beyond.

sections.label: Small island, bold changes
sections.summary: The passage states Singaporeans know the small low-lying island has faced big macro-economic constraints, and the President asked them to go for bold changes, not marginal tweaks.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Singaporeans know or have been taught that our "small" low-lying island state has been confronted by "big" macro-economic constraints and problems.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But as we enter the next stage, the President has asked us to stand ready to "go for bold changes, and not merely to tweak things at the margins".

sections.label: NMPs and education Motion
sections.summary: The passage states the Nominated Members of Parliament look forward to working with MOE to propose a Motion on education in the coming months.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: My fellow Nominated Members of Parliament and I look forward to working closely with MOE as we prepare to propose, hopefully in the coming months, a Motion that underscores the importance and future of education, of tertiary and lifelong education and even preschool education, to explore what different successes entail.

sections.label: Mental well-being and IMH cases
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Government to acknowledge inconvenient truths, citing a 20% rise since 2010 in IMH outpatient cases involving clinical depression, alcohol abuse and obsessive compulsive disorders.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Second, just as Singaporeans must be faced always or be prepared to face brutal and hard truths, the Government, I dare say, should acknowledge inconvenient ones as well.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I asked this in specific regard to the attention that I think we should pay to Singaporeans' mental well-being, particularly when the Institute of Mental Health (IMH) has noted that there has been a 20% increase since 2010 in the number of outpatient medical cases that relate to clinical depression, alcohol abuse and obsessive compulsive disorders.

sections.label: Family, fairness and Singaporean trust
sections.summary: The speaker hopes to revisit what matters to average Singaporean families, reassuring them Singapore is a home where diverse voices are heard and views debated.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I note the emphasis on family, fairness and equality.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I hope that we will revisit what is important for the average Singaporean family to reassure them that Singapore is not only a hub for innovation but, first and always, a home, a safe space where their diverse voices are heard, a place where different views can be debated and could inform future policy and perhaps even allow us to re-evaluate certain policy out-of-bounds markers that are unrelated to national defence and security.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The message that we give them matters and their trust is hard won at every stage.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: They accept all aspects of our national pledge but, beyond prosperity and progress, this group of perhaps 5G Singaporeans, places a high premium on the pursuit of happiness, Mr Deputy Speaker.

sections.label: Helping companies and workers transform
sections.summary: The national agenda must be to help companies transform and create better quality jobs so Singaporean workers can compete internationally amid restructuring.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: As companies make big decisions in restructuring, we cannot let Singaporean workers suffer the fallout.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Therefore, our national agenda must be to help companies transform and create better quality jobs for our workers so that they can compete internationally.

sections.label: AI and auditor redundancy
sections.summary: AI could make many auditors redundant if the profession does not evolve.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Otherwise, AI could make many auditors redundant, if the profession does not evolve.

sections.label: Stable share of contingent workers
sections.summary: Singapore has not seen this happening in a big way, and the share of contingent workers has remained quite stable over time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: In Singapore, we have not seen this happening in a big way.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: The share of contingent workers has remained quite stable over time.

sections.label: ITMs and built environment restructuring
sections.summary: ITMs lay out industry-wide restructuring plans, and BCA has formulated a master plan for integrated construction and prefabrication hubs supporting DfMA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: A key pillar for our economy is the ITMs, which lay out industry-wide economic restructuring plans and identify growth opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: For example, in the built environment sector, the Building and Construction Authority (BCA) has formulated a master plan for the development of integrated construction and prefabrication hubs (ICPH).

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: These are high-density manufacturing facilities that are land-efficient, highly automated and manpower-lean, and they support the Design for Manufacturing and Assembly (DfMA) by producing prefabricated construction elements that help replace labour-intensive construction methods.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Another practice that BCA does is to publish the pipeline of projects requiring DfMA technologies so that firms can plan their resources accordingly.

sections.label: SMEs and industry transformation
sections.summary: Industry transformation also applies to SMEs, which can tap the Lean Enterprise Development Scheme to invest in productivity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Industry transformation applies not just to the big players in the industry, but also to our SMEs, which can tap on the Lean Enterprise Development Scheme to invest in productivity.

sections.label: PCPs under Adapt and Grow
sections.summary: The PCPs are part of the Adapt and Grow initiative, which supports agility and adaptability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: The PCPs are part of the Adapt and Grow (A&G) initiative, which supports agility and adaptability.

sections.label: Progressive Wage Model for lower-wage workers
sections.summary: The Progressive Wage Model enables lower-wage workers in cleaning, security and landscaping to earn higher wages sustainably.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: The Progressive Wage Model (PWM) enables lower-wage workers in the cleaning, security and landscaping sectors to earn higher wages in a sustainable way.

sections.label: PWM benefits and tripartite partnership
sections.summary: A Cleaning Supervisor earns more than double her previous salary; PWM, initiated by the Labour Movement and supported by tripartite partners, has benefited over 70,000 resident workers, and extending it needs union and employer partnership.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Today, she is a Cleaning Supervisor and earns a salary that is more than double what she used to earn.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: PWM, which was initiated by the Labour Movement and supported by the tripartite partners, has benefited more than 70,000 resident workers in the cleaning, security and landscaping sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: As we review extending PWM to other sectors, we will continue to need the strong partnership of unions and employers.

sections.label: Appointment as MENDAKI deputy chairman
sections.summary: Minister Masagos Zulkifli announced the speaker's appointment as deputy chairman of MENDAKI.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Coincidentally, yesterday, Minister Masagos Zulkifli announced my appointment as the deputy chairman of MENDAKI.

sections.label: Malay MPs review community strategies
sections.summary: Malay Members of Parliament will review and monitor efforts and strategies benefiting more community members in education and skills upgrading.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Going forward, my fellow Malay Members of Parliament and I will review and monitor the overall effort and strategies that will benefit even more members of our community, in terms of education as well as skills upgrading.

sections.label: KIFAS minimum attendance requirement
sections.summary: ECDA's website states a child must attend at least one day per month to receive KIFAS subsidies, and teachers say they persuade parents to send children more regularly.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: On the Early Childhood Development Agency's (ECDA’s) website, it states that a child must meet the minimum attendance of one day per month in order to receive the Kindergarten Fee Assistance Scheme (KIFAS) subsidies.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Teachers feedback to me that they have had to persuade some parents to send their children to school regularly, beyond the minimum one-day requirement.

sections.label: Compulsory preschool education proposal
sections.summary: The speaker urges MOE to legislate to make preschool studies part of compulsory education for all children.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: This lack of foundation leads to a vicious cycle, right from the very start.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: I would, therefore, like to urge MOE to legislate to make preschool studies part of compulsory education for all children.

sections.label: Elite school socialising survey
sections.summary: An Institute of Policy Studies survey shows children from so-called elite schools tend to socialise exclusively with others from similar schools.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: A recent survey by the Institute of Policy Studies shows that children from so-called “elite” schools tend to socialise exclusively with others who went to similar schools.

sections.label: Enhancing CCE and Social Studies
sections.summary: The speaker suggests enhancing Character and Citizenship Education and Social Studies.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: My suggestion is to enhance our Character and Citizenship Education (CCE) and Social Studies.

sections.label: Two women's career paths
sections.summary: Two women without straight academic routes later gained qualifications and now work as an HR manager and in a company respectively.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: When she did not get into the course she wanted in polytechnic, we offered her a permanent job as HR assistant.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Through the years of her employment, the company sent her for courses and she now holds a Diploma in Business Management, and Workforce Skills Qualification (WSQ) HR-related certificates.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Ten years on, she is now 27, and a HR manager in a subsidiary of 300-strong.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Another lady told me she scored 199 for her PSLE, failed English at GCE "O" levels and dropped out of an engineering course in polytechnic.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: She worked and did a part-time accountancy course and, today, aged 28, she is doing well in the company and recently bought a condominium.

sections.label: SME transformation challenge
sections.summary: The passage says SME transformation is the most difficult step and that new Enterprise Singapore must closely watch SMEs' development after helping them transform.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Take the transformation of small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) for example.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It is said that "it is difficult to start a business, but to stay in business is even more difficult." We can add one more sentence: "Transformation is the most difficult." How SMEs transform will be a major challenge.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The new Enterprise Singapore, after helping SMEs to transform, must pay close attention to their development.

sections.label: HDB flats and HIP
sections.summary: The passage asks whether HDB flats built after 1986 can be included in the Home Improvement Programme.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For example, can we include the Housing and Development Board (HDB) flats built after 1986 into the Home Improvement Programme (HIP)?

sections.label: Yishun residents and Nee Soon Hub
sections.summary: The passage asks when Yishun residents can have a Nee Soon Hub, Nee Soon Integrated Complex or Kampong Nee Soon.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: After talking about it for so many years, I wonder when Yishun residents can have the pleasure of having a Nee Soon Hub or Nee Soon Integrated Complex or Kampong Nee Soon.

sections.label: Character building and CCE
sections.summary: The passage agrees on the importance of character building and notes the Education Minister's assurance on Character and Citizenship Education and Values-in-Action.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I agreed with hon Member Miss Cheryl Chan that what is more important is character building, good moral values and whether the children can be contributing positively to the family, society and country.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am indeed very pleased that our Education Minister had assured in the Addendum that his Ministry would continue to strengthen its focus on Character and Citizenship Education (CCE) and enhance Values-in-Action programmes.

sections.label: Dog in playground and smoking
sections.summary: The passage describes a man training his dog on playground equipment and a man smoking in his home, asking which NPark Act prohibits the dog training.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Recently, a man brought his dog to the playground and used the children's playground equipment to train his dog.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Many parents were very unhappy; some emailed me.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It is very unhygienic." On the other hand, the man with the dog said, "Why not?" Which NPark Act says that he cannot use the playground equipment to train his dog?

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Another example is that of a man who smokes in his home.

sections.label: Growing Singaporean companies overseas
sections.summary: The passage asks whether strong Singaporean companies can be helped to build track records and go overseas, and says more such companies are needed.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can we help them to build their track records and bring them overseas?

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We have a few strong Singaporean companies such as the banks – DBS, UOB, OCBC – and we have airlines like Singapore Airlines (SIA), Scoot, SilkAir, and others such as Keppel Corp, CapitaLand and so forth.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: But we need to grow more of such "Singapore Inc." to boost our economic growth.

sections.label: MediSave use liberalisation
sections.summary: The passage states that over the years the speaker and others have called for liberalisation of MediSave use, particularly for outpatient treatments.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Over the years, I and many others within this House have called for the liberalisation of MediSave use, in particular for outpatient treatments.

sections.label: MediSave limits for chronic disease
sections.summary: It proposes raising MediSave coverage to up to 80% of expenses with doctor's certification, noting most elderly are already covered.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: For some Singaporeans with multiple chronic diseases or whose illnesses cannot be adequately controlled by medicines on the Standard Medication list, the out-of-pocket cash outlay for medical treatment, even at polyclinics and with Pioneer Generation (PG) benefits, can still remain quite high due to the current utilisation limits on MediSave.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Perhaps, as a start, up to 80% of the expenses, and this can be adjusted as needs arise.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: This should be subject to a doctor's certification.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Such a move would not change matters for the majority of elderly patients, for whom the current chronic disease withdrawal limit of $400 and the Flexi MediSave limit of $200 would already more than adequately covered 80% of their annual outpatient treatment costs.

sections.label: GST exemption for primary healthcare
sections.summary: It notes CHAS and PG schemes strengthened general practice and suggests considering exempting primary healthcare services from GST.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The CHAS and PG schemes have helped to deliver Government subsidies to our family doctors and have strengthened general practice through the reduction of market distortions due to larger subsidies received by polyclinic patients.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I believe we can do even more in this field, or in this regard, and I would like to consider or for us to think about potentially exempting primary healthcare services from the Goods and Services Tax (GST).

sections.label: GST removal and GP care
sections.summary: It states that removing consumption tax from primary healthcare could nudge patients back to family doctors and encourage treatment compliance.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Removing this consumption tax from all primary healthcare services could nudge more patients back to family doctors or GPs for care, and encourage compliance with treatment and follow-up, by reducing costs.

sections.label: MediShield Life universal health insurance
sections.summary: It states MediShield Life provides universal health insurance for Singaporeans and marked a proud day for the healthcare system.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The introduction of MediShield Life, which provides universal health insurance or coverage for Singaporeans, marked a proud day for Singapore’s healthcare system, exemplifying the caring and inclusive society that President Mdm Halimah Yacob spoke of.

sections.label: MediShield Life coverage gaps
sections.summary: It notes pregnancy-related complications and mental health conditions are not covered under MediShield Life and suggests expanding coverage.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: First, with regard to pregnancy-related complications; and, second, about conditions related to mental health.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: These are still not covered under MediShield Life when hospitalisation is required.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I believe that we should consider expanding coverage to these conditions as well.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: We have also been slowly but significantly expanding our support for mental health, even as the disease burden inches up within our community.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I hope that when MediShield Life is reviewed, consideration can be given to expand coverage to some, if not all, mental health-related hospitalisations.

sections.label: Fiscal prudence and currency stability
sections.summary: It states leaders must exercise fiscal prudence, grow Reserves, and keep the currency stable and strong to counter imported inflation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Our leaders must exercise fiscal prudence and grow our Reserves, which is absolutely vital for our long-term survival and stability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: We need to keep our currency stable and strong to counter imported inflation, so that we will have more levers with which to manage local inflation and cost of living.

sections.label: SkillsFuture and Adapt and Grow
sections.summary: The Government has put in place a framework making guidance and assistance available to all, such as SkillsFuture and Adapt and Grow programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Even better, the Government has put in place a framework to make guidance and assistance available to all, such as SkillsFuture and Adapt and Grow programmes.

sections.label: Reaching low-income households
sections.summary: The speaker suggests reaching out to every low- and lower-middle income household with guidance and assistance in addition to GST vouchers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Perhaps it would be good to reach out to every household in the low- and lower-middle income with guidance and assistance in addition to the GST vouchers.

sections.label: Household Transformation Map proposal
sections.summary: The speaker proposes a Household Transformation Map, considered by the Prime Minister's Office, to reach out to families and assist them in achieving their aspirations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Perhaps a new scheme or a Household Transformation Map – since we have the Industry Transformation Maps (ITMs), I think we can consider the Household Transformation Maps (HTMs) – in totality of all relevant programmes can be looked at by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) to reach out to all these families to assist and guide them to achieve their aspirations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This “upward mobility elevator” instead of “poverty elevator” would be a step forward in building a cohesive and progressive nation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: There are many good policies and schemes that benefit Singaporeans, for example, our Build-To-Order (BTO) flat prices are pegged against the average income of an income group, there are various housing grants, special employment credit, job credit and various Ministry of Manpower (MOM) schemes to help our workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: There could be further think-out-of-the-box approaches for existing policies, for example, to review the existing childcare grant to include parents who have left the workforce temporarily to look after their young children and to grandparents, nannies, or babysitters who help look after the grandchildren or children to support parents to increase the total fertility rate (TFR).

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: HDB shall remain the key developer of housing for 80% of our population.

sections.label: Broadening Edusave Progress Award
sections.summary: The speaker suggests strengthening and broadening the Edusave Progress Award to encourage Singaporeans to improve themselves by giving incentives to lifelong learners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Here, I would like to suggest that we further strengthen and broaden the Edusave Progress Award to encourage Singaporeans to improve themselves proactively by giving incentives to lifelong learners.

sections.label: Challenges ahead for Singapore
sections.summary: The speaker states there are many challenges ahead, including a rapidly ageing population, rising protectionism and the threat of terrorism.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: (In English): Sir, there are many challenges ahead of us with our rapidly ageing population, rising protectionism and the threat of terrorism, just to name a few.

sections.label: Healthcare manpower increase
sections.summary: MOH and healthcare institutions are working towards a diverse healthcare workforce, expecting to increase healthcare manpower by 9,000 between 2017 and 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources and Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Indeed, these are precisely the outcomes that the Ministry of Health (MOH) is working towards, together with our healthcare institutions, for a diverse healthcare workforce, as we expect to increase our healthcare manpower by a further 9,000 between 2017 and 2019 to staff new and expanding facilities in our public healthcare and aged care settings.

sections.label: Elderly and young population shares
sections.summary: Francis Tan of UOB said 2018 is the first year the share of people 65 and above matches those under 15.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources and Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Mr Francis Tan of UOB recently pointed out that this year, 2018, is the first year in our history when the share of the population that is 65 years old and above will match that of those younger than 15 years old.

sections.label: Re-employment of older healthcare staff
sections.summary: Nine in 10 staff at retirement age are re-employed, and the public healthcare sector raised its re-employment age from 65 to 67.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources and Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Today, nine in 10 staff at retirement age are re-employed.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources and Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: The public healthcare sector raised the re-employment age for staff before legislation kicked in, from 65 to 67 since July 2016.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources and Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: In 2017, over 1,400 retired nurses aged above 62 were working, compared to 1,200 in 2015, and 20% percent of them are working part-time.

sections.label: Mid-career healthcare conversion programmes
sections.summary: About 150 mid-career locals were supported in 2017 through healthcare conversion programmes, triple the number three years ago.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources and Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: In 2017, we supported about 150 mid-career locals through healthcare conversion programmes, such as the Professional Conversion Programmes (PCPs) and the Senior Management Associate Scheme (SMAS), to help individuals acquire skills and take on good jobs in healthcare in a variety of roles such as Nursing, Allied Health and Administration.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources and Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: And this is triple the number compared to three years ago.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources and Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: We enhanced the PCP for nursing by providing employers with more funding to support the training of mid-career nurses.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources and Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Earlier this year, MOH together with the National University of Singapore (NUS) and Workforce Singapore (WSG) also introduced a new degree-level PCP-Registered Nurses (PCP-RN) to attract more mid-career Singaporeans into the nursing profession.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources and Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: The course commences in July this year, with an estimated inaugural cohort of about 40 mid-career trainees.

sections.label: Social stratification and class
sections.summary: A researcher said Singapore has shifted from a race-based to a class-based society, and the Minister said social stratification is becoming entrenched.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: The lack of resolve to look into certain problems from a fresh angle can have serious consequences because lives are impacted by policies and we cannot turn back time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: It was reported in the news that one of the researchers of the study said Singapore has shifted from a society based on race to one that is based on class as well.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: We just heard from the Minister yesterday that social stratification is fast becoming entrenched here.

sections.label: MOE plans on education inequality
sections.summary: MOE intends to set up more kindergartens, build more student care centres, and reserve places in affiliated secondary schools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: From the Addendum to the President's Address, the Ministry of Education (MOE) intends to tackle the inequality in our education system by setting up more MOE Kindergartens to improve quality, affordability and accessibility in the preschool sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: The Ministry also wants to build more school-based student care centres to cater to the holistic needs of students especially those from disadvantaged families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: MOE also intends to tackle the lack of diversity in our schools by reserving more places for students with no affiliation priority for admission into affiliated secondary schools.

sections.label: Unequal funding between schools
sections.summary: The speaker said schools are not equal because per capita funding differs, and popular schools raise funds more easily than neighbourhood schools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: Two years ago, in the Committee of Supply (COS) debate in 2016, I said that all schools are created not equal because the funding per school is different to begin with.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: Based on per capita funding per student, popular schools with a large student enrolment will always have more funds by default, whilst shrinking neighbourhood schools will always struggle to find money to run extra enrichment programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: It is also a known fact that popular schools will have less problems raising additional funds from their well-connected alumni, while neighbourhood schools will struggle in this area.

sections.label: Secondary 1 posting change proposal
sections.summary: The speaker proposed giving top-tier primary students direct admission to a secondary school of their choice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: In the same COS debate, I also proposed a fundamental change to the Secondary 1 posting exercise to address the lack of diversity in our popular schools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: I shall not repeat the details here, but in a nutshell, I propose that students finishing in the top tier of their primary schools based on PSLE results be given direct admission to a secondary school of their choice.

sections.label: Minister on tackling inequality
sections.summary: The Minister said yesterday that tackling inequality remains unfinished business.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: The Minister has stated yesterday that we all have an unfinished business in tackling inequality.

sections.label: President's speech longer-term priorities
sections.summary: The President's speech sets out the current term's programme and longer-term priorities beyond this term.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: However, our President’s speech this year is slightly different.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: It sets out not only the programme for the current term, but also longer-term priorities beyond this term of Government.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: The speech took this approach because Parliament is re-opening at a special moment in our history.

sections.label: 4G Ministers draft President's speech
sections.summary: The speaker asked 4G Ministers to draft the President's speech as they would carry out its agenda.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: A new generation born long after Independence is coming to the fore, with different views and aspirations.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: We are also in the midst of a political transition, with the fourth generation (4G) Ministers preparing to take over within the next few years.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Therefore, it is timely for the Government to set out a broader vision, a longer-term agenda in the President's speech.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: I asked the 4G Ministers to draft the President’s speech, because they would have to carry out this agenda, continuing beyond my time as Prime Minister.

sections.label: US-China trade tensions
sections.summary: US-China trade tensions hurt business and their unilateral actions undermine the multilateral trading system.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: The trade tensions between US and China hurt business, but more broadly, their unilateral and tit-for-tat actions undermine the multilateral trading system.

sections.label: Pakatan Harapan forms government
sections.summary: Pakatan Harapan, led by Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamed, now forms the government after UMNO-led BN lost power.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Pakatan Harapan, led by Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamed, now forms the government.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: For the first time ever, the United Malays National Organisation (UMNO)-led Barisan Nasional (BN) lost power.

sections.label: Visit to meet Dr Mahathir
sections.summary: The speaker plans to visit Malaysia on Saturday to meet Dr Mahathir and work with him for mutual benefit.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: The expectations of the new Malaysian government are very high, and I think Dr Mahathir will be very busy in the days to come.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: But I plan to visit Malaysia on Saturday to meet Dr Mahathir and to tell him that I look forward to working with him again for mutual benefit.

sections.label: GDP growth since Independence
sections.summary: Since Independence in 1965, GDP has grown more than 40 times in real terms, and growth forecast is now moderated to 2% to 4%.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Since Independence in 1965, our GDP has grown more than 40 times in real terms.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: We can see it in all our lives.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Now that we have become more developed, our growth forecast is moderated to 2% to 4%.

sections.label: Joint Laboratory with Rolls Royce
sections.summary: A Joint Laboratory with Rolls Royce and Singapore Aero Engine Services opened last year, creating manufacturing jobs and giving SMEs and workers access to new technologies.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: For example, we have a Joint Laboratory with Rolls Royce and Singapore Aero Engine Services that was opened last year.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: These projects will create good manufacturing jobs, and SMEs will benefit and so will workers, because through these research collaborations, they will get access to the new technologies.

sections.label: Good start and open opportunity
sections.summary: Every child must have a good start in life regardless of family, and every opportunity must be open to anyone with the right attitude and ability.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Well, first of all, every child must have a good start in life, regardless of which family you were born into.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Thirdly, every opportunity has to be open to anyone with the right attitude and ability.

sections.label: English proficiency and Singlish class marker
sections.summary: Without everyone being proficient in standard English, children whose parents do not speak good English at home will be at a permanent disadvantage and Singlish will become a class marker.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Otherwise, those children whose parents already speak good English at home will be fine, but others will grow up at a permanent disadvantage.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: And without everyone being proficient, speaking standard English, Singlish will become a class marker.

sections.label: Elite groups as obstacle
sections.summary: Elite groups who become closed circles, preventing outsiders from getting in, are a further obstacle to social mobility.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: In any other Parliamentary chamber, in this part of the world or anywhere in the world, we will be togged up in our Sunday best, just to show that we are somebody in society.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: There is a further obstacle to social mobility – elite groups who become closed circles, preventing outsiders from getting in.

sections.label: Social networks and social capital
sections.summary: Such networks are an important part of social capital, but social networks must always remain open and permeable.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Such networks are an important part of our social capital.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: But social networks must always remain open and permeable.

sections.label: RI diversity over the years
sections.summary: RI has a strong tradition of accepting students from diverse backgrounds so long as they make the cut, but over the years it has become less diverse.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: It has a strong tradition of accepting students from diverse backgrounds, so long as they make the cut.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: But over the years, RI has become less diverse.

sections.label: RI students' varied backgrounds
sections.summary: RI students do come from varied backgrounds, and just over half, 53%, live in public housing.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Because, in reality, RI students do come from varied backgrounds.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: And just over half the students live in public housing, 53%.

sections.label: MOE working with popular schools
sections.summary: MOE will work with RI and other popular schools so that these schools never become self-perpetuating, closed circles.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: MOE will work with them, and other popular schools too, so that these schools never become self-perpetuating, closed circles.

sections.label: OBS mixing and Coney Island extension
sections.summary: After 50 years, OBS remains a valuable opportunity for students to mix and interact across different schools and social groups, and an extension is being built on Coney Island.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: After 50 years, OBS remains a valuable opportunity for students to mix and interact across different schools and social groups.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: And we will do more of this, so we are building an extension of OBS on Coney Island.

sections.label: Meritocracy working in Singapore
sections.summary: With universal education, home ownership, and the Government's determination to widen opportunities and make the most of every citizen, meritocracy has been made to work in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: With universal education, with home ownership, with the Government’s determination to widen opportunities and make the most of every citizen, we have made meritocracy work in Singapore.

sections.label: PSLE and T-scores change
sections.summary: Educators and parents hold differing views on PSLE, and the first step is doing away with T-scores.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Educators have very different views, and even parents have very different views; whether it is PSLE, it will be better off without the PSLE.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: But we are taking the first steps to change the status quo, by doing away with T-scores.

sections.label: Nation-building progress and cohesion
sections.summary: The nation is more cohesive than 50 years ago, when there were no integrated HDB estates, townships or shared National Service.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: We have made much progress in our nation-building.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: We are now much more cohesive than 50 years ago, when we did not live in integrated HDB estates, townships nor did we do National Service together.

sections.label: Social cohesion and tidal pulls
sections.summary: Social cohesion has grown stronger, but tidal pulls have grown stronger too.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Today, though our social cohesion has grown stronger, but these tidal pulls have grown stronger too.

sections.label: Extremist teachings and terrorist attack
sections.summary: In the Internet age, exposure to extremist and exclusivist teachings means a terrorist attack would cause great fear and distrust between Muslims and other Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Furthermore, we are exposed in this Internet age to extremist and exclusivist teachings.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: And if there is a terrorist attack, it will cause great fear and distrust between Muslims and other Singaporeans.

sections.label: Widening Labour Movement membership
sections.summary: Fewer workers do jobs traditionally covered by trade unions, so the Labour Movement should embrace new groups, as Mr Chan Chun Sing did in NTUC.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: But in the new economy, fewer workers are doing jobs traditionally covered by the trade unions.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: So, if these new groups are left out, and that union coverage shrinks as a result of the changing work force composition, and you have more people who are not represented, not taken care of, do not feel protected and look for other solutions, it would weaken tripartism and our social compact.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: So, it is better for the Labour Movement to embrace them, to adopt their concerns and to become more inclusive.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: And that is what Mr Chan Chun Sing did in NTUC, widening the Labour Movement membership beyond trade unions, to include the NTUC U-Associates, the PMETs and freelancers.

sections.label: Immigrants and population top-up
sections.summary: Immigrants are part of Singapore's history and identity, and a steady flow is needed to top up the population.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Immigrants are part and parcel of our history and our identity.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: And if you look ahead, we need a steady flow of immigrants – not too many, not too few, just right – to top up our population.

sections.label: Leadership renewal and new generations
sections.summary: It states that history should be remembered but not trapping, making leadership renewal crucial for new ideas, bonds and connections each generation.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Remember our history, but do not be trapped by it.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: That is why leadership renewal is crucial: new ideas, new bonds and new connections are needed with every new generation.

sections.label: Constitutional minimum opposition MPs
sections.summary: It states the Constitution was amended to ensure at least 12 opposition and Non-Constituency MPs in the House regardless of General Election outcome.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: We take every debate in the House seriously.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: And that is why we amended the Constitution to ensure that there will be always at least 12 opposition Members of Parliament and Non-Constituency Members of Parliament in the House, whatever the outcome of the General Election.

sections.label: Malaysian election and GST
sections.summary: It states GST was a hot issue in the Malaysian election, Pakatan Harapan won, Dr Mahathir said the new government would abolish GST, and economically GST is better than the Sales Tax it replaced.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: In the recent Malaysian election, one hot issue was their GST.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: After Pakatan Harapan won the election, Dr Mahathir announced that his new government would abolish the GST.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: From the economic point of view, the GST is better than the Sales Tax that it replaced.

sections.label: Spending needs and raising taxes
sections.summary: It states the country will sometimes need to spend more on healthcare, defence, education or something else, and if revenues are insufficient it must raise taxes.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: From time to time the country will need to spend more – on healthcare, defence, education, or something else – and if revenues are not enough, it will have no choice but to raise taxes.

sections.label: Cabinet reshuffle and 4G leaders
sections.summary: It states the Cabinet was reshuffled, some Ministers moved and others given expanded responsibilities, 4G Ministers helm two-thirds of Ministries, and a leader is expected to emerge before the next General Election.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: We want a strong, cohesive team so that Team Singapore is the winner.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: I have just reshuffled the Cabinet, have moved some Ministers to new portfolios, I have expanded the responsibilities of others.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: The 4G Ministers now helm two-thirds of the Ministries.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: They have a major say in policies and the direction to take Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: I am confident that in the fullness of time, we will see a clear outcome and a leader will emerge from the process.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Certainly, I expect this to happen before the next General Election.

sections.label: Considering future generations
sections.summary: It states decisions must consider future generations, whose lives and futures depend on wise and far-sighted decisions for Singapore to endure and flourish, and expresses confidence in good stewards at handover.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: But above all, it must consider future generations, whose lives and whose futures depend on us; the present generation depends on us thinking of their interests, acting on their behalf, making wise and far-sighted decisions to cause Singapore to endure and to flourish for many more years.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: I am confident that when the time comes for me to hand over to a new Prime Minister, Singapore will be put into the hands of good stewards.

sections.label: 4G leaders and political elite
sections.summary: The passage asks whether 4G leaders from the SAF or Civil Service signal a political elite class, and says people are judged by contribution, not origin.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Given that the 4G leadership, especially the three frontrunners for the next Prime Minister, largely come from the Singapore Armed Forces (SAF) or the Civil Service, is it not a sign that there is now a political elite class in Singapore?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: When you look at the person, you ask: "Is he making a contribution, what are his strengths and weaknesses, what are his contributions, does he or does he not measure up?" You do not ask "Where did he come from?

sections.label: Searching for best Singapore team
sections.summary: The passage says it is not a horse race and that people are sought from the private sector, doctors, lawyers and backbenchers to form the best team for Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: I just said it is not a horse race.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: I have people from the private sector, I have doctors, I have lawyers, I have brought in new people from the backbenchers, some of whom are also from the private sector with business experience.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: So, we are looking for people, wherever we can find them, to bring in to form a Singapore Team.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: And I cannot help it because of my objective.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: I just want the best team for Singapore.   4.02 pm

sections.label: Moving forward as one people
sections.summary: The passage states that in facing an uncertain future, Singaporeans should move forward as one people and one nation and ensure no one is forgotten or left behind.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As we prepare to face an uncertain future, we should always remind ourselves that we need to move forward as one people and one nation and ensure that no one is forgotten or left behind.

sections.label: Success includes helping those in need
sections.summary: The passage states success should also be measured by helping those in need so society progresses together regardless of race and religion, leaving no one behind.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In my view, success should also be measured based on, and by including, the things that we can do to help those in need so that we succeed together, and help the whole society progress together, regardless of race and religion, so that no one is left behind or forgotten.

sections.label: Malays achieving pinnacle of success
sections.summary: The passage states that based on official figures, evidence and anecdotes, more and more Malays have achieved the pinnacle of success.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In general, based on official figures, evidence and anecdotes, we can see more and more Malays who have achieved the pinnacle of success.

sections.label: Reviewing Community Leaders Forum platforms
sections.summary: The passage calls for stepping forward as one bold community and reviewing current platforms like the Community Leaders Forum so it stays relevant as a launchpad.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Let us all step forward as one bold community and review all the current platforms like the Community Leaders Forum (CLF), so that it stays relevant and functions as our community’s launchpad that can fulfil our aspirations and meet the challenges in the coming years and decades.

sections.label: Vulnerable risk in uncertain future
sections.summary: When the future is uncertain, the most vulnerable tend to be at higher risk of needing financial and social help.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: When the future is uncertain, the most vulnerable tend to be at a higher risk of needing financial and social help.

sections.label: Tax rises and inter-generational conflict
sections.summary: Tax rises to support an ageing population may cause unhappiness, inter-generational conflict and job market anxieties among the young.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As we have all been made aware, a rise in taxes in the near future to support an ageing population may be expected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But while Singaporeans have so far accepted tax increments to help fund subsidies for vulnerable groups, including the elderly, unhappiness may arise among other groups if this were to continue in the long run.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Our younger citizens may demand a reduction in older citizens’ benefits or expect similar benefits for themselves in the future, leading to inter-generational conflict.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A rising number of seniors may also want to remain in their last jobs or aspire to better jobs while the next generation is eager to take over positions at the top.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This could heighten job market anxieties among the young, particularly if special provisions are made for older employees to retain their jobs for a longer period.

sections.label: More female than male graduates
sections.summary: Last year about 8,200 women and 7,700 men graduated with a first degree from local universities.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Last year, more women than men graduated with a first degree from our local universities.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: We had about 8,200 female graduates, compared to 7,700 males.

sections.label: Female employment rate growth
sections.summary: The female employment rate grew from 64% in 2007 to 72% in 2017.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Our female employment rate has grown from 64% in 2007 to 72% in 2017.

sections.label: Women earn less than men
sections.summary: In 2017, women in the resident workforce generally earned 9% less than men.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: In 2017, women in our resident workforce, in general, earned 9% less than men.

sections.label: Employers adopting the Standard
sections.summary: More than 500 employers, with about 300,000 employees, have adopted this Standard to date.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: To date, more than 500 employers, with about 300,000 employees, have adopted this Standard.

sections.label: Older resident employment and re-employment
sections.summary: Employment rate of residents aged 55 to 64 rose from 56% in 2007 to 67% in 2017, and over 98% of private sector local employees wishing to work at 62 were offered re-employment since 2012.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: In the last decade, the employment rate of residents aged 55 years old to 64 years old has grown from 56% in 2007 to 67% in 2017.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: This places Singapore in the ninth place when compared to the OECD countries, and higher than countries such as Australia, Korea, the US and the UK.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Since re-employment laws were introduced in 2012, over 98% of private sector local employees who wished to continue working at 62 years old, were offered re-employment.

sections.label: Fresh graduate employment rates
sections.summary: About 90% of autonomous university and polytechnic graduates and 85% of ITE graduates are employed.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Today, the employment rate of our fresh graduates is healthy – about 90% of those from the autonomous universities and polytechnics, and 85% for ITE graduates.

sections.label: Career Starter Programme for graduates
sections.summary: A new Career Starter Programme by Workforce Singapore with autonomous universities, polytechnics and ITEs will offer job search training, industry engagement, career fairs, job referrals and post-placement support.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: In addition, tools such as the MySkillsFuture portal as well as internships, learning journeys, mentorships and career talks – all these form an immersive experience to help our young graduates gain a better understanding of the industries they are trained for.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: We will boost the job search skills of graduating students and enhance their lifelong learning career planning with a new Career Starter Programme.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Offered by the Workforce Singapore (WSG) in collaboration with our autonomous universities, polytechnics and ITEs, this new initiative will also offer job search-related training workshops, industry engagement opportunities, virtual and physical career fairs, job referrals and also post-placement support.

sections.label: School facilities funding
sections.summary: Government schools are fully funded for standard facilities while government-aided and independent schools co-fund some, and MOE does not fund non-standard facilities such as tennis courts.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: For standard facilities such as indoor hall or basketball courts, Government schools will be funded 100% while the Government-aided and independent schools have to raise funds to co-fund some of these facilities.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: So, this is actually contrary to what Mr Png has mentioned earlier.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: I must also add that MOE does not fund non-standard facilities such as tennis courts.

sections.label: MOM support for flexible work arrangements
sections.summary: MOM will focus resources on supporting companies to provide flexible work arrangements to help women fulfil career and family aspirations.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: In this area, MOM will focus our resources on supporting companies to provide FWAs to help our women fulfil both their career and family aspirations.

sections.label: MOE philosophy on pathways
sections.summary: Achievement and success can come in many forms, consistent with MOE's philosophy of "Many pathways, New Opportunities".

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Achievement and success can come in many forms.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: This is consistent with MOE’s philosophy of "Many pathways, New Opportunities".

sections.label: Pathlight School autism-focused setup
sections.summary: In 2004 MOE and the Autism Resource Centre set up Pathlight School, Singapore's first autism-focused school offering mainstream curriculum with life readiness skills.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In 2004, MOE partnered with the Autism Resource Centre to set up Pathlight School.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The aim was to create the first autism-focused school in Singapore that offered Singapore's mainstream academic curriculum together with life readiness skills and to cater primarily to students with autism and related disorders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: These students are cognitively able to access mainstream academic curriculum but require additional support, such as smaller class sizes, special accommodations and teaching staff trained in autism.

sections.label: Xavier Wong ADHD case
sections.summary: Xavier Wong, a 10-year-old Primary 4 student with mild ADHD, was featured in The Straits Times on 10 May this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Consider the case of 10-year-old Primary 4 student Xavier Wong, who was featured in The Straits Times on 10 May this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Xavier, who is able to solve mathematics problems that are two years ahead of his level and has an IQ that places him in the top 2% of the population, was diagnosed with mild attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), and his behaviour has, at times, proven to be disruptive to his classmates and teachers.

sections.label: Autonomous specialised primary schools proposal
sections.summary: The speaker asks MOE to consider facilitating autonomous specialised primary schools for neurodivergent students, with freedom over curriculum, class sizes, staff and fees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The class sizes, environments and curricula of the mainstream schools are also not ideal for neurodivergent students who have differentiated learning needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I would thus like ask MOE to consider facilitating the setting up of autonomous specialised primary schools to cater to these neurodivergent students so that these students are able to study in a specially designed and planned environment that caters to their unique learning needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Aside from the environment and learning spaces, such schools could be given the freedom to design their own curriculum, determine their own class sizes, hire their own staff with the specialised skill sets and even set their own fees.

sections.label: Vacant former MOE school sites
sections.summary: MOE could facilitate these schools and work with the Singapore Land Authority to set them up in compounds of vacant former MOE schools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: MOE could facilitate the setting up of these schools and could also further assist by working with the Singapore Land Authority (SLA) to allow for these schools to be set up in the compound of vacant former MOE schools.

sections.label: Tiered school fee structure
sections.summary: MOE could mandate a tiered fee structure where wealthier families pay full fees and less well-off families pay subsidised rates or qualify for bursaries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: One of the ways that MOE could mitigate this concern is by mandating a tiered-schools fee structure where families who have financial means will pay the full school fees of such schools, while families who are less well-off could pay a subsidised rate, or they could qualify for bursaries from the school itself.

sections.label: Specialised schools set up quickly
sections.summary: In less than 10 years, institutions such as the Singapore Sports School, School of The Arts, NUS High and others were all set up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In less than 10 years, institutions such as the Singapore Sports School, School of The Arts, School of Science and Technology, NUS High, Integrated Programme (IP) institutions, International Baccalaureate (IB) schools and privately funded international schools were all set up.

sections.label: Parental choice in education
sections.summary: The speaker hopes parents will have more choices and options in how they educate their children, linking this to the country's future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: What I am hoping for is for parents to have more choices and options in terms of how they would like to educate their children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: And if we get the education of our children right, then we get the future of our country right. 4.48 pm

sections.label: SkillsFuture credit and special needs
sections.summary: SkillsFuture credit take-up doubled from 6% to 12%, but the speaker urges a review to include the non-traditional workforce such as those with special needs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The take-up rate of the SkillsFuture credit of $500 per adult citizen has, in the last year, doubled from about 6% to 12%; a positive sign, but there is much more to do.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: For the non-traditional workforce such as those with special needs, the SkillsFuture movement has not yet made them its priority and accorded the attention it deserves.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: This will be a non-traditional workforce that can be tapped upon.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: So, I urge the Ministry to conduct a review with all its key stakeholders to: One, identify the root causes of why SkillsFuture has not attained more traction than it deserves.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Two, develop and resource further strategies, both bold and incremental, on how more adult Singaporeans can be transformed to take on the opportunities and threats posed by a global marketplace and the labour market.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Three, develop robust SkillsFuture plans to equip adult Singaporeans most at risk of being left behind, such as those with special needs.

sections.label: Singapore top in PISA
sections.summary: A Minister reminded the House that Singapore ranked top in the OECD's 2015 Programme for International Student Assessment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Singapore has often prided itself on doing well in the global stage.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: We were reminded yesterday again by Minister that we are top in the OECD’s Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA) ranking in 2015, second to none.

sections.label: Questions on education system outcomes
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the education system produces self-driven lifelong learners and what milestones and landscape it should aim for.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Surely, there should be other data points to measure if we are doing right in trying to develop every Singaporean to his fullest potential and nurture lifelong learners for the future – part of the Addendum that is released by the Ministry.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: These questions may soon be less important than asking ourselves the following questions: One, does our current education system for our young produce the self-driven, self-motivated, agile lifelong adult learners who are able to survive and thrive in the new age of rapid technological disruptions?

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Two, what are the process and outcome milestones we are driving at, in view of the external and domestic setting the 4G Government is now in?

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Three, if we were starting from a clean slate, what would our education landscape or education system look like?

sections.label: Ong Ye Kung on inequality
sections.summary: Minister Ong Ye Kung spoke about tackling inequality, the income gap, the middle-income core, social mobility and interaction between socioeconomic classes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Minister Ong Ye Kung spoke about the unfinished business of tackling inequality in this House yesterday – on the income gap that he is concerned about; about growing the middle-income core; social mobility and the need for interaction between groups from different socioeconomic classes.

sections.label: Tax system for transfers
sections.summary: The speaker says assistance for the needy must come mainly from tax revenues and needs Singaporeans' support for a tax system enabling transfers from the prosperous to the less fortunate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: To mitigate the impact of consequent inequality, we must provide more assistance to those in need, especially for basic necessities, public housing, healthcare and education.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Funds for the needy have to be sourced mainly from our tax revenues, with additional aid from voluntary donations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Hence, we need the endorsement and support from Singaporeans for a tax system which facilitates more transfers from those who are prosperous to those who are less fortunate.

sections.label: KidSTART and school support
sections.summary: The passage calls for support beyond KidSTART so children from vulnerable families progress well in primary and secondary school.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: We need to ensure that access to education is not just on a superficial level.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: We have the KidSTART programme to ensure that children aged six and below from vulnerable families have a "good start" in life through access to health, learning and developmental support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: To further ensure that children who have been identified and benefited from the KidSTART programme continue to progress well, there should be similar support for those who need it to do well in primary and secondary school as well.

sections.label: Ministries making exceptions for appeals
sections.summary: The passage welcomes Government acceptance of appeals and says Ministries and agencies should make exceptions within limits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Hence, I am glad that the Government acknowledges such differences and accept appeals, taking into account mitigating circumstances and changes in family situations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: It is important that all our Ministries and agencies be prepared to make exceptions, but I must stress – within limits – to assist those caught at the edges.

sections.label: Curriculum depth and Asian classics
sections.summary: The passage asks whether so many students need deep calculus and chemistry, and whether Asian classics should be taught alongside Shakespeare.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Basic and general knowledge in all subjects lay a useful foundation but do we need so many students studying calculus or chemical interactions in such depth?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: With the pivot to Asia, should our students not be exposed to great Asian classics, such as the "Dream of the Red Chamber", "the Romance of the Three Kingdoms" and "Ramayana", in addition to works from Shakespeare?

sections.label: AI productivity gains and income gap
sections.summary: The passage states AI brings productivity gains but threatens certain jobs, and calls for more equitable distribution of benefits to avoid widening the income gap.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: AI systems lead to gains in productivity but threaten jobs in low-paid and low-skilled production industries and jobs that are administrative, clerical and procedural in nature.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Most of the productivity gains resulting from the use of AI, robotics and IT will accrue to those who own the patents, the machines and the capital.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Hence, whilst we have to nurture more entrepreneurs and technology creators and innovators to reap the benefits and rewards of this technological development, we also need to find ways to more equitably distribute these benefits and rewards so as not to further widen the income gap.

sections.label: Party leadership transitions
sections.summary: The passage states that both the Ruling Party and the leading Opposition party are undergoing leadership transition.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Both the Ruling Party and the leading Opposition party are undergoing leadership transition.

sections.label: Earning the right to lead
sections.summary: The passage says the 4G leaders acknowledged they must earn the people's trust and that the right to lead must be earned.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The 4G leaders clearly acknowledged in the President’s speech that they must earn the trust of the people, forge their own bonds afresh with the people, earn the right to lead.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The mandate of the people is given only once at every general election.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: That mandate, in my view, entitles the winning party to form the Government.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But it does not give the winning party the right to lead.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: That right must be earned, no matter how long you have been in Parliament and it must continue to be earned.

sections.label: Government policies and social mobility
sections.summary: Government policies like universal education, National Service, mixed housing and meritocracy have produced socio-economic progress and social mobility for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Deliberate Government policies, such as universal education, National Service, mixed housing and meritocracy have resulted in significant socio-economic progress and social mobility for Singaporeans.

sections.label: Standing with Singaporeans against terror
sections.summary: The passage calls on the Government to protect vulnerable Singaporeans and pledges unity against evil and terror regardless of language, race or religion.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We grieve with fellow Singaporeans when their family members suffer mishaps whether in Singapore or overseas.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We call on the Government to protect Singaporeans who are vulnerable.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Even in situations of terror where our own people act or attempt to act against our country, we will stand with all Singaporeans, regardless of language, race or religion.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We will be united against evil and terror.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As our forefathers and founding fathers protected Singapore for us, we will protect Singapore for our children.

sections.label: Singaporeans determining their own destiny
