sections.summary: It states that Singaporeans determine their own destiny, must not let others influence it, and remain Singaporean wherever they live or die.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Whatever their motives, however noble their motives, we are the ones who determine our destiny.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We must not allow others to influence our destiny.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Whether we live or die, wherever we live or die, we are Singaporean.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And if we die in a foreign land, there will be that corner of a foreign field that will forever be Singapore.

sections.label: Singapore passport world recognition
sections.summary: The Singapore passport has recently been recognised as the most powerful passport in the world, giving visa-free access to about 180 countries.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The Singapore passport has recently been recognised as the most powerful passport in the world as it gets you through, I believe, 180 countries without the need for a visa.

sections.label: Platforms for fintech and innovation
sections.summary: Initiatives such as JTC Launchpad@one-north, MAS' Fintech Regulatory Sandbox and Punggol Digital District build ties and opportunities, with sandboxes positioning Singapore as a fintech innovation centre.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Initiatives, such as Jurong Town Corporation (JTC) Launchpad@one-north or Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS)' Fintech Regulatory Sandbox and the planned Punggol Digital District, are platforms that provide the environment and the ecosystem to encourage people to come together and to build ties and create new opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: MAS' use of regulatory sandboxes to encourage fintech experimentation has been instrumental in positioning Singapore in a short span of time as a major centre for fintech innovation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Deloitte's report on the world's best cities in which to launch a fintech firm, ranked Singapore as one of the best cities in the world for fintech.

sections.label: JTC Launchpad startup growth
sections.summary: The JTC Launchpad@one-north houses 750 startups, up from 250 when it was launched in 2011.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The JTC Launchpad@one-north houses 750 startups, up from 250 when it was launched in 2011.

sections.label: Startup talent and learning platforms
sections.summary: A report showed Singapore overtaking Silicon Valley for startup talent, and the speaker calls for platforms for people to learn from each other.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Last year, the Global Startup Ecosystem Report by Startup Genome, a US-based organisation showed Singapore overtaking the Silicon Valley as number one for startup talent, notwithstanding that Silicon Valley still remains number one overall and there are still areas for Singapore to improve.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: So, while SkillsFuture remains an important underpinning in supporting Singaporeans in developing new and required skills, I believe that there is a need for people to also have a platform to engage and to learn from each other.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The same way, with examples like Block 71 and the Fintech Sandbox, that the Government has effectively catalysed and enabled the environment for startups and fintech, I believe that, together with the Government, academia and the private sector, there could be platforms to support platforms of learning for people to come together in their learning journey, in the same way we have developed and will continue to develop segments and industry sectors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: With the disruptions and the gig economy, going forward, it may not be just about getting a job, but possibly, a few jobs with freelance work arrangements.

sections.label: Benefits of ecosystem participation
sections.summary: Participating in such an ecosystem promotes learning, builds confidence, resilience and trust, and helps one seize opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Participation within such an ecosystem not only promotes learning but builds confidence, resilience, trust and allows one to be better able to seize opportunities.

sections.label: Graduate under-employment survey
sections.summary: A recent survey found 4.3% of graduates in full-time jobs were severely under-employed, earning under $2,000 a month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In fact, a recent survey found 4.3% of graduates in full-time jobs being severely under-employed, earning less than $2,000 a month.

sections.label: Reserves, taxes and education strains
sections.summary: Public finance created reserves but also tax increases, while education produced world-class PISA scores but a tuition industry and stressed students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Our approach to public finance has created huge reserves for emergency purposes which help fund Budgets, but also created the need to raise costs via tax increases that place pressure on our people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Our education system has produced world-class PISA scores, but it has spawned a massive tuition industry that may erode social mobility and students who are substantially more stressed than the Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) average.

sections.label: Reviewing reserves for funding gaps
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether, when a Budget funding gap is imminent, policies on reserves, Net Investment Returns and land sales could be reviewed instead of raising taxes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: If and when a Budget funding gap is imminent, rather than raise taxes, is there more scope to review our policies towards the reserves, to tap more from the Net Investment Returns (NIR) and/or land sales, as my Party Secretary-General Mr Pritam Singh has eloquently argued?

sections.label: Low total fertility rate
sections.summary: The speaker says TFR is an existential issue, with evidence that cost-of-living and academic-competition anxiety contribute to Singapore's very low TFR.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: As Mr Pritam Singh said, TFR is an existential issue facing Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: There is some evidence that anxiety about the cost of living and academic competition contributes to a low TFR and, indeed, our TFR is one of the lowest in the world.

sections.label: HDB resale price pressure
sections.summary: Falling resale demand and more flats sold on marketplaces could pressure monetising HDB flats for retirement or supplementary income.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The possibility of HDB resale prices in the future performing poorly as more Build-To-Order (BTO) flats are built, resale demand remains soft and more flats get sold on the marketplaces pressure on the goal of monetising one’s own HDB flat for future retirement income or even emergency or supplementary income.

sections.label: Class size randomised trial
sections.summary: The question of class size warrants a large-scale randomised trial to quantify benefits versus costs for national debate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The question of class size at least warrants research in the form of a large-scale randomised trial to help quantify benefits versus costs, so that, as a country, we can debate this issue with all the facts on the table.

sections.label: Independent Ombudsman for Executive decisions
sections.summary: An MSM editorial called for a state not boxing local media into a corner, and an independent Ombudsman is proposed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The quote that I used comes from a recent MSM newspaper editorial which called for "a state that does not use its considerable influence, resources and enforcement powers to box the local media into a corner." Can we not have an independent Ombudsman to review complaints about Executive decisions without the complainant being faced with the costs and limitations associated with the process of seeking judicial review?

sections.label: Time bar and scholar bonds
sections.summary: A time bar for civil servants entering politics and scholar bond options in SME or civil society sectors are proposed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: To manage this, can we not consider a time bar for civil servants entering politics, as I have argued for earlier?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: And can scholars not only be given the option of serving part of their bond in the local small and medium enterprise (SME) sector or civil society sector, but also be encouraged to do so?

sections.label: Suggestions for a stronger society
sections.summary: Past suggestions, including harnessing ASEAN disruptive industry growth and an SME globalisation bank, could contribute to a stronger society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I have not touched on that subject in this speech, but my colleagues and I have made many suggestions on this subject in the past, from harnessing ASEAN disruptive industry growth to a dedicated bank for SME globalisation, to name but two.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: But giving serious thought to such suggestions can contribute to a more liveable, more future-ready, more democratic and more diverse society that will be a stronger and better home, built to last.

sections.label: Single fibre infrastructure backbone
sections.summary: Singapore has only one fibre infrastructure backbone, which is affordable but creates a single point of failure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: At present, there is only one fibre infrastructure backbone in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: This makes sense from the point of view of affordability, but it creates a single point of failure.

sections.label: UK France petrol diesel ban
sections.summary: The UK and France announced that sales of gasoline and diesel vehicles will not be allowed in their countries by 2040.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The UK and France have announced that sales of gasoline and diesel vehicles will no longer be allowed in their countries by 2040.

sections.label: BlueSG electric vehicle programme
sections.summary: BlueSG is a Government co-funded programme to provide 1,000 EVs and 2,000 charging points by 2020, with only 20% of charging points open to the public.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: BlueSG is a co-funded programme by the Government to provide 1,000 EVs and 2,000 charging points by the year 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: However, only 20% of these charging points will be open to the public.

sections.label: Yellow pages rule guiding principle
sections.summary: It asks whether the yellow pages rule, that Government should not provide services already provided by private enterprises, should continue as guiding principle.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Should the yellow pages rule that the Government should not provide services that are already provided by private enterprises in the yellow pages continue to be our guiding principle?

sections.label: Pre-approved vendors shut out competitors
sections.summary: Pre-approved vendors can be vetted for quality, but their competitors are shut out even with superior products, risking accusations of favoritism.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Some vendors are pre-approved and that is great for them because they can be vetted for quality but, at the same time, their competitors are shut out, even if they develop a superior product.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: This can quickly become an accusation of favoritism where insiders make lots of money and outsiders are left to wither on the vine.

sections.label: Clear rules for private ownership
sections.summary: If clear rules allow for private ownership, Government will not have to carry the entire burden of implementation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: If clear rules are in place that allows for private ownership, then Government will not have to carry the entire burden of implementation.

sections.label: Infrastructure trusts financing ownership
sections.summary: Infrastructure trusts are another way to finance infrastructure, democratising ownership by letting the man in the street have a stake.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Another way to finance infrastructure is through infrastructure trusts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: This has the benefit of democratising ownership by allowing the man in the street to have a stake in infrastructure.

sections.label: Social compact with younger Singaporeans
sections.summary: The President set out the Government's focus on complex challenges, and the speaker will focus on the social compact with younger Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: The President has articulated the Government's specific focus on facing complex challenges in an uncertain world, rooted with an appreciation of the needs of our elderly and the aspirations of our young.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: I will focus my speech on the social compact between the Government and the younger generation of Singaporeans who are coming of age and are trying to navigate a world very different from their parents when they were young.

sections.label: Support for low-income Singaporeans
sections.summary: Middle-class Singaporeans own homes and gained from selling HDB flats, while diverse approaches support the low-income group.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Our middle-class group	Singaporeans own homes and experienced significant capital gains when they sold their HDB flats.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We adopted diverse approaches to provide support to the low-income group through initiatives, such as the Many Hands Approach, ComCare, the WorkFare Income Supplement Scheme.

sections.label: Balance of meritocracy and compassion
sections.summary: It shows growing recognition that a balance must be struck between performance-based meritocracy and compassion and opportunities.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Instead, it shows a growing recognition that the balance will need to be struck between performance-based meritocracy on one hand, and compassion and opportunities on the other as our society and economy continue to grow and prosper.

sections.label: National Youth Council 2016 survey
sections.summary: The National Youth Council's 2016 survey highlights many positive characteristics of this generation of millennials.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: The National Youth Council's 2016 survey highlights many positive characteristics of this generation of millennials that I believe put us in good stead in a new environment.

sections.label: Forging social compact 2.0
sections.summary: This new social compact 2.0 would need to be forged with and by the younger generation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: After all, this new social compact 2.0, as I call it, would need to be forged with and by those from this younger generation.

sections.label: Youths seek purposeful experiences
sections.summary: The Singaporean Dream was once the 5Cs, but youths today crave memorable and purposeful experiences emphasising the journey over the destination.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: In the past, the Singaporean Dream was often encapsulated by the 5Cs: cash, car, credit card, condominium and country club membership.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: No longer satisfied with just the attainment of the 5Cs, our youths today crave memorable and purposeful experiences that emphasise the importance of the journey instead of being fixated with the destination.

sections.label: New social compact with citizens
sections.summary: The Government will partner citizens to redefine success and align public policy with Singaporeans' evolving aspirations without compromising national survival.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: To satisfy this generation's thirst for novel experiences, this Government will need to partner our citizens to re-define the meaning of success and recognise that, paradoxically, it might be one that continually shifts and always gives us something new and better to aspire towards.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: In this new social compact, the role of Government is to bring public policy in line with Singaporeans' evolving aspirations for ensuring that national survival is not compromised.

sections.label: Calls for national digital identity
sections.summary: Stronger calls have emerged to use a national digital identity to implement a national e-payment solution.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Increasingly, there have been stronger calls to leverage a national digital identity to successfully implement a national e-payment solution.

sections.label: People involved in engagement
sections.summary: About 1,800 people took part through design workshops, roadshows and surveys.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: About 1,800 people were involved through design workshops, roadshows and surveys.

sections.label: Partnering Singaporeans to better lives
sections.summary: The role is to partner Singaporeans in defining the Singapore Story and bettering lives, especially the under-privileged and vulnerable, reducing inequality.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Our role is to work together as we partner fellow Singaporeans in defining our chapter in the Singapore Story and delivering on our commitments to better the lives of every Singaporean, especially the under-privileged, the vulnerable and continue to reduce inequality.

sections.label: Countries sharing same Gini index
sections.summary: The United Kingdom, Sri Lanka, Uzbekistan and Cambodia all share the same Gini index of 0.36.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Take, for example, the United Kingdom, Sri Lanka, Uzbekistan and Cambodia.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: They all share the same Gini index of 0.36.

sections.label: Social mobility and integrated policy approach
sections.summary: A quoted writer says social mobility issues are multi-faceted and inter-dependent, requiring an integrated policy approach ensuring fairness and opportunities.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: He wrote, "Social mobility issues are multi-faceted and inter-dependent; thus, requiring an integrated policy approach.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: This is undergirded by ensuring fairness and opportunities for all Singaporeans." At present, the Government cannot afford to and will not hide behind excuses and statistics.

sections.label: Revisiting meritocracy and compassion balance
sections.summary: The Government says it is ready to revisit the balance between meritocracy and compassion to align policies with the generation's social compact.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: As a Government, we stand ready to revisit the current balance between meritocracy and compassion to keep our policies in line with the social compact of the generation.

sections.label: The Gift Community Baju Bazaar
sections.summary: Youths called The Gift Community sought support for Baju Bazaar, collecting donated Hari Raya outfits for lower-income Malay/Muslim families, and were offered Wisma Geylang Serai.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Recently, a group of youths, calling themselves "The Gift Community" approached me for support for their project they call "Baju Bazaar" – baju means outfit, where they planned to collect donated Hari Raya bajus or outfits to be distributed to lower-income Malay/Muslim families to celebrate Hari Raya.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Of course, I offered them to hold the event at Wisma Geylang Serai.

sections.label: Fifth strategy reaching millennials
sections.summary: The speaker concludes with the fifth strategy in reaching out to millennials: demonstrating value.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: (In English): Mr Speaker, allow me to conclude with the fifth strategy in reaching out to the millennials: demonstrating value.

sections.label: Recognising next generation's strengths
sections.summary: The passage says the next generation of Singaporeans should be recognised and given space to forge their social compact.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Just as the Pioneer Generation had entrusted Generation X to take Singapore into the knowledge-based economy, we should recognise the strengths and aspirations of the next generation of Singaporeans and give them space to forge the social compact of their time.

sections.label: Millennials as Singapore squad members
sections.summary: The passage calls this the hashtag SG squadgoals moment, recognising millennials as valuable members of Singapore's squad going forward.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: To borrow a term commonly used on social media, this is our "hash-tag SG squadgoals" moment, as a new hast-tag – hast-tag squadgoals – and this is our hast-tag SG squadgoals' moment where we recognise that, going forward, you, the millennials, will be valuable members of our Singapore "squad".

sections.label: 4G leaders must demonstrate ability
sections.summary: The passage states 4G leaders must demonstrate ability to lead, provide a vision for Singapore and assure Singaporeans' future remains bright.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: For those concerned about our future, the 4G leaders must demonstrate that they have the ability to lead the nation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: They must provide a vision for Singapore and give assurance that Singaporean's future remains bright.

sections.label: Rising cost of living burden
sections.summary: The speaker accepts the rationale for higher water, parking and GST charges but says the combined cost increase burdens citizens.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Although I understand the explanation, the rationale given why water must be priced correctly, why parking charges must be adjusted, understand the rationale why the Goods and Services Tax (GST) must be increased in a few years' time to provide for better healthcare, but, yet, when you add together all the increase in cost, this increase in cost of living will cast a financial burden on our citizens.

sections.label: Budgetary benefits tagged to household type
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the Government will review tagging budgetary benefits to household type to strengthen nationhood.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Next, to strengthen our sense of nationhood among our citizens, I hope that this Government will review the policy of tagging budgetary benefits to household type.

sections.label: Pioneer Generation Package appreciation
sections.summary: The Pioneer Generation Package was appreciated by many Singaporeans because the Pioneer Generation felt appreciated by the Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: The Pioneer Generation Package was appreciated by many Singaporeans because the Pioneer Generation felt appreciated by the Government.

sections.label: CHAS benefits tagged to household income
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the Government will review tagging CHAS benefits to household income, citing residents who lost blue CHAS card status after a small pay raise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: To better help our less fortunate, I hope that this Government will also review its policy of tagging the Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS) benefits to the household income of the individual.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: I have come across residents who lost their blue CHAS card status because they had worked harder and were given a small pay raise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Thus, for a $100 extra monthly income, they lose the medical benefits tagged to the blue CHAS card.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: They then end up paying more for medical care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: A graduated system may be fairer to those who really need the CHAS benefits.

sections.label: Built environment and industry transformation
sections.summary: The transformation of the built environment must be aligned with the proposed industry transformation in the 23 Industry Transformation Maps.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The transformation of our built environment must be aligned with the proposed industry transformation as laid out in the 23 Industry Transformation Maps (ITMs).

sections.label: Industrial premises for SME clusters
sections.summary: Building industrial premises in industry clusters, rented to promising SMEs on 20 to 30 year leases at affordable rental, to reduce operating costs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Third, building industrial premises for SMEs in industry clusters.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: These premises can be rented out to promising SMEs for longer leases of 20 to 30 years at an affordable rental so as to reduce the operating costs of SMEs.

sections.label: More BTO flats near families
sections.summary: HDB should build more BTO flats of various room types in older and newer estates so more Singaporeans can stay near family.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: HDB should build more BTO flats of various room types in both older and newer estates so that more Singaporeans have more choices to stay near their parents and families.

sections.label: Review EASE eligibility criteria
sections.summary: The speaker proposes that HDB review the eligibility criteria for its Enhancement for Active Seniors (EASE) programme to make more homes elderly-friendly.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: To further expedite the making of more homes elderly-friendly, I would propose that HDB review the eligibility criteria for its Enhancement for Active Seniors (EASE) programme.

sections.label: Shelter for public pools
sections.summary: The speaker proposes that Singapore Sports Council build shelter with skylight for all public pools.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: To overcome these challenges, I would propose that Singapore Sports Council build shelter with skylight for all public pools.

sections.label: Retailers face rising business costs
sections.summary: Many retailers struggle with rising business costs from labour shortage and high rental, causing shop turnover, resource wastage and service disruption.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Many retailers are struggling to survive and continue to face rising business costs due to labour shortage and high rental cost.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The high turnover of retail shops has resulted in much wastage of resources and disruption of services to consumers.

sections.label: Mega hubs and underground malls
sections.summary: The speaker proposes regrouping retail outlets and shopping centres into mega shopping hubs, and building underground shopping malls with factory outlets connecting MRT stations outside the city centre.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: First, regroup retail outlets and shopping centres to form mega shopping hubs so as to provide better experiences for shoppers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Second, build underground shopping malls with factory outlets to connect various MRT stations outside the city centre.

sections.label: HDB neighbourhood centres as malls
sections.summary: The speaker proposes transforming HDB neighbourhood centres into shopping malls and markets selling fresh produce and products.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Third, transform our HDB neighbourhood centres into shopping malls and markets selling fresh produce and products.

sections.label: Slower workforce and GDP growth
sections.summary: The workforce will not increase as quickly as before, and GDP will not grow as fast as before.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Our workforce will not increase as quickly as before.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: In GDP terms, we will not grow as fast as before.

sections.label: Streamlining food shop regulatory touchpoints
sections.summary: Companies face up to 14 regulatory touchpoints before setting up a food shop, and the PEP aims to streamline these into one form.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Currently, companies can have up to 14 regulatory touchpoints with different Government agencies before they can set up a food shop.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: The PEP is working with the Smart Nation and Digital Government Office and GovTech on this review.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: We have set for ourselves an ambitious target to streamline the 14 forms into one form and to correspondingly reduce the time taken and licence fees which companies have to pay to start a food business.

sections.label: MAS fintech regulatory sandbox
sections.summary: The Monetary Authority of Singapore has introduced a regulatory sandbox framework for the fintech industry.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) has introduced a regulatory sandbox framework for the financial technology or fintech industry.

sections.label: Reviewing licensing for micro-brewers
sections.summary: The PEP Secretariat and the speaker met three students to discuss reviewing licensing to lower entry barriers for micro-brewers during an initial trial period.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: The PEP Secretariat and I have also offered our help.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: We met the three students over dinner and had a good discussion on how our current licensing regime could be reviewed to lower the barriers of entry for micro-brewers to test out new products during an initial trial period, before applying a more rigorous set of rules when they subsequently scale up their production and sales.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: My colleagues and I are looking into this proposal and we will discuss with the regulatory agencies.

sections.label: Government procurement for Singapore companies
sections.summary: The Government will give fair consideration to Singapore companies when procuring products and services, and the Health Promotion Board appointed local SME Activate Interactive.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: The Government will give fair consideration to Singapore companies when we procure products and services, to seek out creative and innovative ideas from our companies; to partner them in our Government projects; to enable them to build up a track record to compete overseas.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: For example, the Health Promotion Board appointed Activate Interactive, a local SME, to develop the Healthy 365 mobile app and provide the step trackers for the first season of National Steps Challenge.

sections.label: Amazon picked Riverwood as vendor
sections.summary: Last year, Amazon picked Riverwood as the vendor to deliver their products in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Last year, Amazon picked Riverwood as the vendor to deliver their products in Singapore.

sections.label: Companies improving HR practices
sections.summary: About 150 companies improved HR practices and left the watch-list, showing a differentiated approach works.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: About 150 companies have improved their HR practices and moved out of the watch-list.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: This shows that a differentiated approach is effective in sending the correct signals to companies and incentivising them to adopt good practices that benefit Singapore and Singaporean workers.

sections.label: Pro-Singapore worker via economy
sections.summary: Being pro-Singapore worker is more effectively done by growing the economy and helping companies do well.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: To be pro-Singapore worker, I believe the more effective way is to grow our economy, help our companies to do well, so that they can provide better jobs, better pay and better life for our workers.

sections.label: Economy generating good jobs
sections.summary: To maximise people's potential, Singapore's economy must generate good jobs and give access to opportunities, networks and ideas.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: To maximise the potential of our people, Singapore’s economy must have the capacity to generate good jobs and provide our people access to the best opportunities, the best networks and the best ideas.

sections.label: Developing and attracting talent
sections.summary: Growing the economy requires developing Singaporean talent and attracting talent to compete with top-tier cities.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: To grow our economy, we have to develop Singaporean talent and also attract talent to our shores so that we can compete with other top-tier cities in the world.

sections.label: Strategic economic decisions history
sections.summary: In the 1960s leaders chose free trade and export-driven growth and attracted MNCs; in the 1990s and 2000s services were opened up.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: (In English): Mr Speaker, in the 1960s, our Pioneer Generation of leaders made two strategic economic decisions which were contrarian to the policies adopted by most developing countries at that time.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: First, we rejected import substitution and instead relied on free trade and export-driven growth.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Second, we attracted MNCs to invest in Singapore and made this a key pillar of our economic development strategy.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: In the 1990s and 2000s, we made bold moves to open up our services sector ahead of other countries in Asia by privatising Government-owned entities in industries like telecommunications and power and transforming our services sector through market competition.

sections.label: Resisting populism and protectionism
sections.summary: As a small open economy, Singapore must resist forces of populism and protectionism.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: As a small open economy, Singapore must resist these forces of populism and protectionism.

sections.label: Flats reaching 50-year mark
sections.summary: Only about 7% or 70,000 flats will reach the 50-year mark at the tail end of the next decade.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Only about 7% or 70,000 flats will reach the 50-year mark at the tail end of the next decade.

sections.label: Modified SERS system suggested
sections.summary: Suggestions were made by Members, and a modified SERS system could be considered in the future for expansion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: There have been a number of suggestions from hon Members of the House.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I would suggest that a modified SERS system be considered in the future for expansion.

sections.label: SERS at 60-year mark
sections.summary: At some point, it may make more sense and be more cost-effective to SERS flats at the 60-year mark and re-intensify land with topped-up leases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: At some point in time, we will have to consider how much of land is left and it may make more sense and be more cost-effective to eventually SERS some of the flats at the 60-year mark and re-intensify the land with topped-up leases.

sections.label: China's shorter leases
sections.summary: China faces a similar situation with shorter leases of 20 years and 70 years, some coming up by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: China, for example, faces a situation similar to us and their leases are shorter – 20 years and 70 years – some of which are coming up by 2030.

sections.label: Assisted living pilot for elders
sections.summary: Related to leases is housing for elders, and MND's Addendum that a new assisted living model will be piloted is welcomed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Related to the issue of leases is also housing for our elders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I, therefore, again, welcome MND's Addendum that a new model of assisted living will be piloted.

sections.label: Enhanced EASE programme
sections.summary: Ageing-in-place requires changes, so the enhanced EASE programme will transform existing flats for elders and the infirm.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Of course, ageing-in-place requires changes to be made.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: So, the enhanced EASE programme will transform existing flats into those suited for our elders and the infirm.

sections.label: Short-lease flats for younger singles
sections.summary: The speaker suggests extending short-lease flats under the Fresh Start Housing Scheme and 2-room Flexi Scheme to younger singles, with a minimum 20-year occupancy period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Yet, there are those who continue to find it a challenge.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I, therefore, suggest that the Government extend the short-lease flats currently available under the Fresh Start Housing Scheme and 2-room Flexi Scheme for elders to also younger singles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: They must, however, adhere to the minimum 20-year occupancy period.

sections.label: Singapore near 100% homeownership
sections.summary: Singapore is probably the only country that has achieved close to 100% homeownership.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Today, Singapore is probably the only country in the world that has achieved close to 100% homeownership.

sections.label: Multi-generation flats in HDB towns
sections.summary: The Government built multi-generation flats in HDB towns so three generations can live under one roof and races can live harmoniously.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The Government has built multi-generation flats in HDB towns to enable three generations to live under one roof and also to allow different races of Singaporeans to live harmoniously together.

sections.label: Metropolis must embrace all Singaporeans
sections.summary: The metropolis must embrace all Singaporeans in progress, and in the built environment people must be at the core.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Yet, more importantly, this metropolis must embrace all Singaporeans in that journey of progress or we risk becoming no more than one of many cities in the world – cold, utilitarian and unwelcoming.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: So, even as we embrace progress, let us not forget that in our role as stewards of the future, we are also our brother's keeper.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In a built environment, we must look after people and have them at the core.

sections.label: Metropolis for disadvantaged and unborn
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the metropolis is designed for the disadvantaged and disabled from the beginning and is a beacon for future generations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: To the disadvantaged and the disabled, may this metropolis be one designed with them in mind from the beginning, but not as an afterthought.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: To those as yet unborn, may this metropolis be a beacon of hope and light for future generations of Singaporeans, where every child, every life, is valued, protected, embraced and encouraged.

sections.label: Concentration of commercial retail space control
sections.summary: Control of commercial and retail space is concentrating, with a handful of large companies influencing leasing practices and rental rates, and SMEs typically offered three-year initial leases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Over the past few years, control of commercial and retail space is getting more concentrated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: A handful of large property management and investment companies now controls a large slice of the market and are in the position to influence leasing practices and rental rates collectively.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Typically, most SMEs leasing commercial or retail spaces from these big landlords will be offered an initial lease period of three years.

sections.label: Five-year lease option for tenants
sections.summary: Proposes landlords offer new tenants leases up to five years, with renewals at three years and an exemption for some tenants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: As such, I would like to propose that landlords have to give all prospective new tenants the option to lease for a period of up to five years, while subsequent renewals can remain at three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: An exemption from granting the five-year option may be made for tenants who take over existing furniture and fittings from a previous tenant and also do not have to reinstate the premises to a bare shell condition upon the expiry of their leases.

sections.label: Changi Terminal 5 and Tuas Megaport
sections.summary: States that plans for Changi Terminal 5 and Tuas Megaport are catalysts to transform major parts of the island.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We are taking bold and decisive steps to realise this vision.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We are all familiar with the plans for the new Changi Terminal 5 and Tuas Megaport.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: These are not just individual projects; they are the catalysts to transform major parts of our island.

sections.label: Tengah forest town and Paya Lebar
sections.summary: Describes Tengah forest town with first flats sold in November, new urban living concepts, and Paya Lebar as the next site.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: It is a forest town which we have designed and the first batch of flats will be sold in November this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We will improve on what we have done in Punggol so that Tengah will be even better, with new concepts of urban living, like smart home solutions, eco-friendly features and even autonomous vehicles (AVs) to provide shuttle services around the estate.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And besides launching Tengah, we are now already looking at the next new site and, that is, Paya Lebar, after the air base relocates to Changi.

sections.label: Greater Southern Waterfront extension
sections.summary: States the city will be extended to the Greater Southern Waterfront after the ports move to Tuas.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Next, we will extend the city further to the Greater Southern Waterfront, after the ports move to Tuas.

sections.label: Integrating rental and sold HDB units
sections.summary: States rental and sold units will be integrated within the same HDB block, with about 1,000 households becoming homeowners last year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This means that families grow up in the same neighbourhood and the residents share the same common areas and facilities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We are now going one step further to integrate rental and sold units within the same HDB block.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Last year, almost 1,000 households moved out of rental flats to become homeowners.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: They are supported by significant housing grants as well as new programmes like the Fresh Start Housing Scheme.

sections.label: Kampung Admiralty and more kampungs
sections.summary: States community services and amenities are under one roof, citing Kampung Admiralty, and more kampungs will be planned in other HDB towns.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: It means more community services and amenities, all under one roof, for convenient access.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And a good example of what we have done is Kampung Admiralty which was officially opened over the weekend.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Kampung Admiralty is just one small kampung with just over a hundred units, but we will plan for more “kampungs” in other HDB towns.

sections.label: HDB 99-year lease
sections.summary: The passage states that maintaining and renewing HDB towns is linked to the end of lease, and that the HDB lease is 99 years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The need to maintain and renew our HDB towns is also linked to the issue of the end of lease.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We have made clear from the outset that the HDB lease is 99 years.

sections.label: CPF for HDB purchase
sections.summary: The passage states that the Government is not stopping the use of CPF for HDB purchase.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Just earlier this week, a resident came to me, showed me the phone with the screenshot of the article and said, "Is the Government going to stop the use of CPF?" So, let me be very clear about this.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We are not stopping the use of CPF for HDB purchase.

sections.label: Resale flat prices by lease
sections.summary: The passage gives median prices for older 4-room and 5-room flats with less than 60 years remaining, noting higher prices in popular locations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: An older 4-room flat with less than 60 years remaining would sell for around $300,000, median price; and a 5-room flat would sell for around $400,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: For flats in more popular locations, prices can be significantly higher – more than double the prices which I just mentioned earlier, more than double.

sections.label: Right-sizing flat options
sections.summary: The passage states that sellers of 4- or 5-room flats can buy a 2-room flexi flat with a 40-year lease or a 3-room resale flat.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: For example, if you sell a flat now, a 4- or 5-room, you can purchase a 2-room flexi flat from HDB with a 40-year lease for around $100,000; or a 3-room resale flat for around $250,000, depending on location.

sections.label: Monetisation schemes for elderly
sections.summary: The passage states that the Lease Buyback Scheme and renting out a bedroom are available, working, and will be reviewed and enhanced.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: For those who prefer to stay in the same place, there is also the Lease Buyback Scheme, where you can sell part of the remaining lease to HDB; or the option of renting out a bedroom.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, the monetisation schemes we have are in place and they are working; and we will continue to review and enhance these schemes and help our elderly unlock the value of their flats for retirement.

sections.label: Matching HDB buyers and sellers
sections.summary: The passage states the need to better match HDB buyers and sellers, citing the HDB Resale Portal and providing more flat information.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, we need to find better ways to match buyers and sellers in the HDB market.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We started with the HDB Resale Portal, which has simplified and speeded up the resale transaction process and we will continue to do more.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We will provide more information on the available flats in the market – be it new flats or resale flats – so that we can help buyers and sellers transact more smoothly and we can help Singaporeans make more informed housing decisions that best suit their needs.

sections.label: Property market measures and monitoring
sections.summary: Measures have been put in place over the years, and market trends will continue to be monitored using various policy levers for a stable and sustainable property market.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, we have put in place various measures over the years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We will continue to monitor market trends closely and make use of various policy levers to ensure a stable and sustainable property market.

sections.label: Pulau Tekong polder development
sections.summary: One specific project being done is the polder development in Pulau Tekong.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: One specific project we are doing is the polder development in Pulau Tekong.

sections.label: Rules debated and enshrined in Constitution
sections.summary: The rules were discussed at length and debated thoroughly in the House to balance present and future generations, and are enshrined in the Constitution.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Mr Leon Perera said that this was not just a technical issue, but a philosophical issue and I agree with him.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But the rules were discussed at length, debated in this House thoroughly, so that we can find the right balance between present and future generations and we enshrine the rules in our Constitution.

sections.label: Fiscal position and reserves
sections.summary: The fiscal position is strong, but changing the rules or chipping away at reserves risks compromising the nation's long-term health, so Singapore looks ahead and prepares responsibly.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Our fiscal position is strong, but if we succumb to temptation; change the rules, chip away at our reserves, we run the very real risk of compromising the long-term health of our nation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The Singaporean way is to look ahead and prepare for the future responsibly.

sections.label: MND inviting Singaporeans' views
sections.summary: MND will invite Singaporeans to share views on areas from major projects like the Greater Southern Waterfront and Rail Corridor to new HDB town design and estate improvements.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: For the MND work, there are many areas where we will want to invite Singaporeans to share their views and perspectives, from major projects like the Greater Southern Waterfront and the Rail Corridor, to the design of new HDB towns and right down to specific improvements that can be made in your estate and neighbourhood.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: That is the work we have to do together over the next 50 years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And then, when we celebrate SG100, we can look forward to a greener, smarter and even more beautiful city, one that all of us are proud to call home.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Just following up on the speech of Minister Lawrence Wong, pertaining to Government surpluses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I noted in my speech that, at this current point, the Government has slightly in excess of $15 billion in accumulated surpluses.

sections.label: Resources for this term of Government
sections.summary: The Minister for Finance made clear that there are just enough resources to cover Government needs for this term, but beyond it expenditures will continue to rise, including healthcare spending.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Through the rest of the term, I think the Minister for Finance had made clear during the Budget Debate, and I would repeat, that we believe that we have just enough resources to cover Government needs for this term of Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But beyond this term of Government, we know that expenditures will continue to rise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: There is no doubt that healthcare spending will rise; there is no doubt about that.

sections.label: NIRC share of GDP
sections.summary: NIRC will keep providing steady revenues as a percentage of GDP, but is not expected to increase as a percentage of GDP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: NIRC, as a percentage of GDP, will continue to provide us a steady stream of revenues for the future, but we do not expect that to increase as a percentage of GDP.

sections.label: Government Budget size and economy
sections.summary: A Government Budget ballooning to 25%, 30% or 40% of GDP, as in some European countries, will be a drag on the economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: If the Government Budget – which means the revenues that we need to collect to meet the Budget – balloons to 25% of GDP, 30% of GDP, 40% of GDP like in some European countries, for sure it will be a drag on the economy.

sections.label: Public transport capacity and financing
sections.summary: The Rail Financing Framework addresses responsiveness, contestability, asset renewal and financial sustainability, alongside bus and rail capacity expansions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: We have the new Rail Financing Framework, again, hoping to deal with issues of responsiveness and contestability in the market, putting a different emphasis on renewal of assets and the financial sustainability of our public transport infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: We have seen an expansion in capacity, a $1.1 billion programme, the Bus Services Enhancement Programme for 1,000 Government-funded buses, improving capacity for 70% of bus services.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: We have seen the introduction of City Direct Services, shorter waiting times, new rail lines which have either been built, opened or for which construction has started in Downtown Line, the Thomson-East Coast Line, Jurong Regional Line, Cross-Island Line and extensions to many existing MRT lines.

sections.label: Barrier-free access and covered linkways
sections.summary: All bus interchanges are barrier-free, 97% of bus stops and 96% of buses have wheelchair access, and 200 kilometres of covered linkways are due by end-2018.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: All bus interchanges are barrier-free: 97% of bus stops and 96% of buses have wheelchair access.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: And by the end of the year, 2018, this year, we will have 200 kilometres of covered linkways under the Walk2Ride programme.

sections.label: MOT and LTA enquiries
sections.summary: MOT and LTA received more than 850,000 enquiries and points of feedback in the past year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: MOT and LTA received, in this year past, more than 850,000 enquiries and points of feedback.

sections.label: Sector GDP and jobs
sections.summary: It affects the economy, happiness, social life and family life, supports 1.1% of GDP and creates 123,000 jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: It affects our economy, it affects our happiness, it affects our social life, it affects our family life and our kids’.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: It supports 1.1% of our GDP, creates 123,000 jobs.
