sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: This can be about the services, the direct provision of services for transport; it can also be about the auxiliary services around transport, inter-operability of the modality of payments, for example.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: We then had to have the Parking Places (Amendments) Bill to introduce the licensing regime.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Well, we have seen and we will continue to see developments around the private hire car industry, the point-to-point industry – Uber, Grab and various other players.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: The introduction of those algorithms and their changes to the fares available and the opportunities that commuters took advantage of have been welcomed but they have also driven disruptions and changes to our taxi industry and the people who drive the taxis.

sections.label: Economy and land transport plans
sections.summary: Economic changes will affect land transport plans, with new employment centres at Jurong Lake District, Punggol Digital District, Sembawang, Woodlands and Changi.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: The changes in our economy are going to affect how we deal with our land transport plans.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: We see the new centres of employment that Minister Lawrence Wong talked about recently: Jurong Lake District, Punggol Digital District, Sembawang, Woodlands and Changi.

sections.label: Next land transport masterplan phase
sections.summary: Taking feedback, changes and challenges into account, the next phase of developing the land transport masterplan is beginning.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Taking all this feedback into account, looking at these changes, looking at these challenges, we are embarking on the next phase of developing our land transport masterplan.

sections.label: Seamless land transport vision
sections.summary: The vision is a seamless land transport system that can easily integrate new and innovative mobility solutions as they emerge.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Currently, what is our vision and what are we trying to achieve?

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: We want to provide a seamless land transport system, one that can easily integrate new and innovative mobility solutions as they emerge.

sections.label: Mobility-as-a-Service and light regulation
sections.summary: Mobility-as-a-Service aims for integrated seamless outcomes with lightest state intervention, standards for safety and inter-operability, and possibly software, data-sharing and API products.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: All these are different entities, but the solution to you is integrated, is seamless.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: So, you can have a functional outcome of Mobility-as-a-Service and that is where we want to go to, where the state, the Government, has the lightest possible intervention and regulatory touch, in order to make these different components synchronise together.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: It will require us to set some standards around safety, but also around inter-operability.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: It may be necessary for the state to just build a handful of products to interface software, to share data, to put up an API.

sections.label: Connectivity to regional centres
sections.summary: Stronger connectivity to regional centres will bring jobs and daily activities closer to home, possibly requiring transport investment ahead of demand.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Thirdly, we will develop stronger connectivity to the regional centres that we talked about – bring jobs and daily activities closer to home.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: But as we do that, as we prioritise these centres in order to drive the economic activity there, in order to drive investment there, we may have to invest ahead of demand for our transport connectivity.

sections.label: Car-lite walking cycling riding
sections.summary: Going forward with three big ideas assumes a car-lite direction and encouraging walking, cycling and riding as part of the solution.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: In going forward with these three big ideas, we assume that we must go in the direction of being car-lite and that we have to emphasise and encourage people to think about walking, cycling and riding as part of the solution.

sections.label: Public consultation and advisory panel
sections.summary: Views are invited on car-lite assumptions, with wide consultation and an advisory panel for the Land Transport Masterplan reporting to the House.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: But again, if you feel a need, a desire or some knowledge on the basis of which you want to challenge those assumptions of going car-lite or talking about walk, ride and cycle and how we address these solutions, we want to hear your views.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: We will consult widely and ask for public input through many channels.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: We are setting up an advisory panel with representatives from commuters, workers, academics and disruptive businesses and many more to address our needs for the Land Transport Masterplan going forward, to make recommendations to the Government and to report back to this House, where I anticipate we would engage in a robust and dynamic debate with many strong opinions on our transport system.

sections.label: Privilege, inequality and meritocracy
sections.summary: Addressing inequality requires acknowledging privilege and systemic factors, and the social stratification seen reminds us of meritocracy's imperfection.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: That knowledge might make us indignant, especially if we were never conscious of our privilege, let alone think that it is part of why we are successful.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We cannot talk about inequality without first acknowledging that some of us are more privileged than others.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If we want to address inequality, we must acknowledge the systemic factors that allow for unequal distribution of resources and opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We must think deeply about how we have all -- in some way or another -- contributed to the persistence and growth of inequality.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Hence, is it accurate when we say that meritocracy is the way to help keep inequality in check?

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In fact, the social stratification we see in our midst only reminds us of the imperfection of meritocracy.

sections.label: Ellison Building negotiations decision
sections.summary: Through the negotiations, a good decision was reached for the future of Ellison Building.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Through these negotiations, I am glad we have come to a good decision for the future of Ellison Building.

sections.label: Critical citizens and good leadership
sections.summary: Critical citizens are needed to demand good leadership, and governance involves what citizens demand of themselves, not just of Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: At the same time, we, as the people, must be critical citizens so that we can demand for good leadership.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In fact, I would even go so far as to say, without good and critical citizens, we will not be able to get good and responsible Government and leaders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Governance is not just about what we expect of the Government, but also what we demand of ourselves as citizens.

sections.label: World of disparate minorities
sections.summary: Rather than a world of us versus them or majority versus minority, the world is made up of disparate minorities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In fact, instead of saying that we are now living in a world of "us versus them", "majority versus minority", I would say that we are living in a world that is made up of disparate minorities.

sections.label: Students' letters to fourth generation leaders
sections.summary: Students hand-delivered 16 letters, one for each fourth generation leader, to the speaker's office three weeks ago.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Three weeks ago, those precocious students hand-delivered 16 letters to my office – one for each of the fourth generation leaders – hoping that I would bring them to Parliament on their behalf.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I will keep that promise and pass these to the Clerk for the team.

sections.label: Students' question on trust
sections.summary: The students' first question asks how much their future prime minister trusts them, echoing Mdm President's concern.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The students’ first question for their future prime minister is, “How much do you trust us?” This echoes Mdm President’s concern about the future leadership’s ability to listen to, trust and work with the people, particularly those with dissenting views.

sections.label: Dissenting views on the ground
sections.summary: The speaker senses more people hold dissenting views than Government-commissioned opinion polls reveal.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: My own sense of the ground, and I could be wrong and you may disagree with me, is that there are more people who have dissenting views about what is going on in our country than Government-commissioned opinion polls reveal.

sections.label: Leaders in unfortunate bubbles
sections.summary: Electoral shocks in the UK, US and Malaysia show some leaders can live in an unfortunate bubble.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The shock at the electoral results in the UK, US and Malaysia has shown that some leaders can live in an unfortunate bubble and, sometimes, it is not one entirely of your own making.

sections.label: Surveys and ground sentiment
sections.summary: The speaker worries surveys present too positive an assessment, and says his own ground experience differs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Everybody is working together to find the right answer.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And if they’re not, then you’ve got even more serious problems.” So, I do worry when I read surveys that seem to present too positive an assessment of public opinion on controversial issues like transport or water prices.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In a recent Straits Times interview regarding whether the ground cared about the six-hour questioning of Dr PJ Thum by the Select Committee, I saw this quote, “We went to the grassroots, into the constituency, door to door, and nobody asked about it, nobody wanted to talk about it and nobody was the least bit concerned about it.” And perhaps, but I respectfully offer you my observation that this has not been my own experience of the ground.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In my work, I do get to talk to a considerable number of youths and white-collar working professionals.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There were definitely some people asking about it, wanting to talk about it and showing concern about the general handling of dissenters.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Many of these lay observers, even those who were more establishment-leaning, did express their deepening discomfort with watching the establishment go for, what they perceived, as over-kill when it came to dealing with naysayers from the Opposition, from civil society and even from within the establishment’s own ranks.

sections.label: Including non-establishment voices
sections.summary: The speaker suggests intentionally seeking out more non-establishment types to participate in national bodies and Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The purposeful inclusion of more thoughtful voices who are unafraid of challenging establishment views will make our system stronger.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, can I suggest that we intentionally seek out more non-establishment types to participate in our national level focus groups, committees, boards, Ministries and Parliament?

sections.label: Housing for unwed mothers
sections.summary: The passage urges providing secure affordable housing to an unwed mother alongside education subsidies so her child can compete with richer households.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Their children would say the same thing, because that is what love says.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, as we provide education subsidies to support a child at school, let us simultaneously provide secure affordable housing to his unwed mother.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Stable housing with longer term tenancies and less crowded rooming conditions through the child's crucial schooling years will give these kids a fighting chance with kids from the richer households.

sections.label: Power gap in policies
sections.summary: The passage states the power gap is entrenched in housing, healthcare and education policies across Ministries because policy is power frozen in place.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The power gap is entrenched in policies about housing, healthcare, education across Ministries, because policy is, after all, power frozen in place.

sections.label: Beyond GDP as success measure
sections.summary: The passage hopes Singapore looks beyond GDP and implements a companion measure of holistic progress, citing Yeoh Lam Keong and Manu Bhaskaran's 2012 proposals.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Because if we lost it all and became the powerless ones, how would we want the system to work with us?

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I hope, some day, we can consider looking beyond just Gross Domestic Product (GDP) as an indicator of our success and implement a companion measure of holistic progress along.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In 2012, economists Yeoh Lam Keong and Manu Bhaskaran talked about how GDP growth must not become the be-all and end-all for Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: They proposed alternative indicators, such as measuring income inequality, the proportion of citizens’ "out of pocket" healthcare expenses and the breadth of outreach of our public hospitals.

sections.label: Cannot go back to past
sections.summary: The passage says that although we love our Pioneers, we cannot go back, quoting that the past is like a foreign country.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And that is the power of a people.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It made me consider, much as we love our Pioneers and admire the times our country came from, we cannot go back.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For they say, “The past is like a foreign country: they do things differently there." Where it was their time to plant, perhaps now is our time to uproot.

sections.label: We are not founding leaders
sections.summary: The passage states we must make of it what we will, and that we are not Lee Kuan Yews, Goh Keng Swees or Rajaratnams.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And we must make of it what we will.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We are not Lee Kuan Yews, Goh Keng Swees or Rajaratnams.

sections.label: Love for Singapore and Singaporeans
sections.summary: The passage recounts a man saying he is not brave but loves Singapore and Singaporeans, and supports the Motion and the country's future.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: When people praised him for being brave in stepping up to serve despite being perceived as too ordinary, he said, "I am not actually a brave man, but I love Singapore and I love Singaporeans." So, let our love find the way forward out of here.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I support the Motion and the future of our country.

sections.label: Reform starting at Ministry of Finance
sections.summary: The reform must start at MOF, recognising limits of price and cost as proxies for value and allowing officers' discretion in moral reasoning.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: The first practical implication of my idea: this reform must start at the Ministry of Finance (MOF), responsible for so many of our policy levers – a reform that requires an explicit recognition of the limits of price, cost and expenditure as a proxy for value, and to allow for greater use of discretion by public officers in recognising moral reasoning as a legitimate form of argumentation.

sections.label: Treating people unequally for equality
sections.summary: The speaker says stratification is higher than before and suggests treating people unequally to give the largest advantages to the disadvantaged.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: While it is true that inequality is lower today than at the start of Singapore's journey, we also worry that the stratification today is higher than it was in the past, a point which Minister Ong Ye Kung highlighted in his speech on Wednesday.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: And so, our measures must be correspondingly more aggressive, and we must slant inequality the other way.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: John Rawls famously said that we must try our best to treat people as equally as possible and any inequality ought to be to the benefit of the least advantaged.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: But today, where inequality exists, we must go further.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: And in a country where socialism is not a dirty word but a founding philosophy, we must be prepared to do more for equality.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: So, I suggest that we must increasingly and continually treat people as unequally as practicable, so as to provide the largest advantages to the disadvantaged.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: We must make sure that a boy born to poor parents must have more from the state than one born from the rich.

sections.label: More aggressively progressive policies
sections.summary: Because economic storms can wipe out fortunes, the speaker suggests more progressive policies asking more from the rich and lessening the poor's burden.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Economic storms can wipe out fortunes, making the rich today the destitute tomorrow.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Hence, my second suggestion for reform – we need more aggressively progressive policies, to ask more from the rich, and lessen the burden on the poor.

sections.label: Environmental behavioural change reform
sections.summary: The speaker suggests starting environmental behavioural change, urges a research fund on it, and says economic reasoning must be balanced with moral reasoning.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In this, we require both morality and economics to work together, for capital to power clean technology for the future, as well as a massive change in consumer behaviour today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: So, my third and final idea for reform – let us start an environmental behavioural change that will tackle the largest environmental problems of our times.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: To lower our carbon emissions with our energy efficiency and allow Singapore to impact the world by making it bluer, greener and less polluted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: This is an issue which remains under-invested today, especially in the social sciences, and I urge the Government to invest in a research fund on environmental behaviour and change.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: We need to insert and steer our values into the national conversation about prosperity and growth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: We need to balance the economic reasoning with moral reasoning.

sections.label: Fresh Start Housing Scheme
sections.summary: The Fresh Start Housing Scheme aims to help second-timer families with children living in public rental flats own a flat again.

sentences.text: For instance, we have the Fresh Start Housing Scheme which aims to help second-timer families with children and who live in public rental flats own a flat again.

sentences.text: I subsequently met the same resident I mentioned earlier a month later at a block visit.

sentences.text: He shared with me happily that his licence application had been approved.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Nevertheless, it seemed to me to be quite a straightforward application.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: So, the unhappy incident could have been due to a breakdown in communication arising from language difficulties.

sections.label: PM speech on social cues
sections.summary: The Prime Minister spoke about social cues and social markers in his Wednesday speech.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The Prime Minister, in his speech on Wednesday, spoke about social cues and social markers.

sections.label: Inequality and social stratification
sections.summary: Inequality can become a serious issue and social stratification can break Singapore's social compact.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Inequality can become a serious issue, and social stratification can break the social compact in Singapore.

sections.label: Policies, trade wars, restructuring
sections.summary: For over 50 years after Independence, policies look after residents' dignity, while Singapore now faces global trade wars and economic restructuring.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: For over 50 years after Independence, there are many welcome policies that look after the dignity of our residents, for example, the housing, MediSave and Baby Bonus policies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Currently, Singapore is facing the potential threat of global trade wars and the challenge of economic restructuring.

sections.label: Mr Wong's application approved

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Coming back to the story of Mr Wong, I learned that his application was approved within a short period of time.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The unhappiness before was likely a result of miscommunication.

sections.label: Singapore social network statistics

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: In 2016, Singapore had 3.3 million social network users.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: This figure is projected to grow to 3.6 million social media users in 2021.

sections.label: Henderson Dawson coordinating meeting
sections.summary: In Henderson Dawson, a regular coordinating meeting with agencies, community partners, business and volunteer groups shares information on helping residents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: In my Henderson Dawson division, I have a regular coordinating meeting with all the Government agencies, community partners, business groups and volunteer groups where we share information about who, what and how we are helping residents in need.

sections.label: Maureen at Henderson Dawson PCF
sections.summary: Maureen has worked at the Henderson Dawson PCF Centre since February 2017 and enjoys every day of it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Maureen has been working in the Henderson Dawson PCF Centre since February 2017 and enjoying every day of it.

sections.label: Global affairs affecting lives
sections.summary: Examples given include ASEAN Summit decisions, international treaties such as FTAs and the Paris Agreement, and hosting the Trump-Kim Jong-un Summit.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: For example, how decisions at the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summits impact our lives or, how our participation in international treaties and agreements, such as free trade agreements (FTAs) or the Paris Agreement on Climate Change, impacts on our lives; how important it is to be chosen as host to the Trump-Kim Jong-un Summit.

sections.label: MFA foreign policy information portal
sections.summary: A proposal for MFA to set up a portal with bite-size foreign policy information so people understand the Government's stand and decisions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: This can deepen our understanding of our foreign policies, and our man-in-the-street can be our ambassadors of our foreign policies, too.

sections.label: 4G leaders and community views
sections.summary: 4G leaders are well-versed in communication, but garnering views of NGOs, VWOs and volunteer groups is important for participation and ground buy-in.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: (In English) Mr Speaker, Sir, our fourth generation (4G) leaders are very well-versed on the powers of effective and timely communication in this information age.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: However, the need to garner the views of non-government organisations (NGOs), voluntary welfare organisations (VWOs) and volunteer groups in the community is very important.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: This is so that everyone has a sense of participation and involvement in all that we are doing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: It also helps in getting the buy-in from the ground.

sections.label: Singapore identity and history

sentences.text: These questions go to the very heart of our identity.

sentences.speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We do have a unique identity and defining characteristics.

sentences.speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We sometimes forget, but our history is not short.

sentences.speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: But our story actually stretches far back to 1299, to the first founding by Sang Nila Utama.

sentences.speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: It is a 700-year journey through time and space that has made us the people that we are and given us the attributes that are now part of our uniquely Singaporean DNA.

sections.label: Proclamation of Independence identity
sections.summary: The Proclamation of Independence declared Singapore a sovereign democratic nation, the day we became One People and a nascent Singapore Identity emerged.

sentences.speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Our hopes and dreams for the future were captured in the Proclamation of Independence, which said: "...Singapore shall be forever a sovereign democratic and independent nation, founded upon the principles of liberty and justice and ever seeking the welfare and happiness of her people in a more just and equal society.” That was the day we became One People.

sentences.speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: You could say that that was also the day that a nascent Singapore Identity emerged, shaped by the events of the preceding centuries, and to be further forged and honed in the next 50 years, as we made the journey from Third World to First.

sections.label: Singapore self-determination, diplomacy, deterrence, SAF, National Service
sections.summary: Singapore acts in its own best interests, defends self-determination through diplomacy and deterrence, supports a rules-based order, and maintains the SAF and National Service.

sentences.speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Countries larger and more powerful than us may, from time to time, try to dictate what we should do.

sentences.speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: However, we will act only in accordance with the best interests of Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: But we will defend ourselves if the need arises.

sentences.speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We advance and defend our right to self-determination through diplomacy and deterrence.

sentences.speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: That is why we act on principle and support a rules-based international order, where states must act in accordance with agreed rules and not purely on the basis of might or size.

sentences.speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: And that is why we have the Singapore Armed Forces (SAF), and that is why we support National Service (NS).

sections.label: Values defining Singapore
sections.summary: Singapore is defined by values including family, kindness, inclusiveness, honesty, integrity, anti-corruption, meritocracy, aspiration for equality, justice, fairness and rule of law.

sentences.speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: More than anything else, it is our values that define us: family, kindness, inclusiveness; honesty, integrity and anti-corruption; meritocracy and the aspiration for equality; justice, fairness and rule of law.

sections.label: Singapore Olympic and Paralympic medals
sections.summary: Joseph Schooling won Singapore's first Olympic gold, while Yip Pin Xiu and Theresa Goh won gold and bronze at the 2016 Paralympics.

sentences.speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Joseph Schooling won our first Olympic gold medal.

sentences.speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Yip Pin Xiu and Theresa Goh – gold and bronze medals at the 2016 Paralympics.

sections.label: PISA 2015 15-year-olds ranking
sections.summary: Singapore's 15-year-olds ranked No 1 in the world for Mathematics, Science and reading in PISA 2015.

sentences.speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Our 15-year-olds are No 1 in the world for Mathematics, Science and reading in the Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA) 2015, an international benchmarking test dubbed the World Cup for Education.

sections.label: Primary 4 and Secondary 2 Mathematics and Science
sections.summary: Singapore's Primary 4 and Secondary 2 students are the world's No 1 in Mathematics and Science.

sentences.speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Likewise, our Primary 4 and Secondary 2 students are the world’s No 1 in Mathematics and Science.

sections.label: Primary 4 Reading ranking
sections.summary: Singapore's Primary 4 students are No 2 in the world for Reading.

sentences.speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Our Primary 4 students are No 2 in the world for Reading.

sections.label: Cost of living and economic activity
sections.summary: The passage states that cost-of-living concerns are best addressed by generating economic activity with real wage and productivity increases, and notes Singapore's investment and competitiveness rankings.

sentences.speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We know and we understand the concerns about cost of living.

sentences.speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: However, we recognise that the best way to address this is by generating economic activity with real wage increases and real productivity so that our people can earn more in real terms.

sentences.speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Singapore is the top investment destination in Asia and second in the world.

sentences.speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We are the second most competitive economy in the world.

sections.label: Home ownership and public housing
sections.summary: The passage states that 90.7% home ownership exists, of which 80% is public housing.

sentences.speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We care that our people have good homes, to have a place where they can bring up their families.

sentences.speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We have 90.7% home ownership, of which, 80% is public housing.

sections.label: Volunteerism rate growth
sections.summary: The passage states that the volunteerism rate grew from 9% in 2000 to 35% in 2016.

sentences.speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Our volunteerism rate has grown over the years from one in 10 individuals (9%) volunteering in 2000 to one in three (35%) volunteering in 2016.

sections.label: Our Singapore Conversation and mutual support
sections.summary: The passage recalls Our Singapore Conversation distilling five things that mattered most to Singaporeans, and states that supporting one another keeps the country going.

sentences.speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Members will recall Our Singapore Conversation, which distilled the five things that mattered most to Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: It is because what keeps us going, what makes us able to take on all the challenges that we face – and there are many – is the knowledge that we are there for one another, supporting one another, leaving no one behind.

sentences.speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: But let me make a special call out to the young who are just starting out.

sections.label: Tackling the future together
sections.summary: The passage states that Singapore has beaten impossible odds together and must tackle the future together, and that adjustments will be made.

sentences.speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Together, we have beaten seemingly impossible odds time and time again.

sentences.speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Together, then, is how we must tackle the future.

sentences.speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: And we will succeed because of who and what we are –Singaporean.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: So, you would be glad to know I will be making some adjustments.

sections.label: Opportunity Fund and KidSTART support
sections.summary: The passage states that no one must be left behind and hopes the Opportunity Fund's administration and the KidSTART programme can be enhanced and developed more quickly.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: However, we must make sure that no one is left behind.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Now, there is an Opportunity Fund, a fund that can be used for beneficial co-curricular activities to further develop students from low-income families.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I hope that the administration of this fund can be enhanced to ensure that students are aware of the various opportunities that are available and that more students can benefit from this fund.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: We also have the KidSTART programme, which is a pilot programme that aims to provide comprehensive support to low-income families.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: It is hoped that this will increase the potential of children from such families, and these children will have the same opportunities as children from other families.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: However, I hope that this programme can be developed even more quickly so that it can benefit more families.

sections.label: Government compassion and unpopular decisions
sections.summary: The people want assurance the Government is compassionate, and unpopular decisions like GST increases and car park charges make them wonder if it hears and cares.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Above all, the people want to be assured that the Government is a compassionate one, one that would fight for its people, be on their side and do right by them.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: It seems that unpopular decisions like the Goods and Services Tax increases, imposing car park charges on teachers, no matter how logical they may sound, make people wonder if the Government has heard the people and really care.

sections.label: Leadership engaging and earning trust
sections.summary: The speaker has seen leadership engage, explain tradeoffs, review changes, make unpopular decisions, and earn trust one heart at a time.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I have also personally seen the leadership at work with the people and even behind closed-door discussions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: There is an earnest desire to engage, to lay out the various tradeoffs and explain why some things can or cannot be done.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: There is an earnest effort to review and make changes, where appropriate, to help ease difficulties.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: But there is also courage to make the right decisions, to make unpopular decisions, and to do what is important and right for Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Clearly, there is just no short cut to this except the hard work of engaging and helping each group, each person, each individual, and in earning their trust and respect, one heart at a time.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: The story of the resilience, grit and determination of our forefathers will continue to live in us.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I have faith in our collective wisdom to choose what is best for the country in the long run, not just for the short term, and to distinguish the truth from falsehoods, to appreciate sincerity and hard work in building Singapore and to find common ground in the midst of many differing views.

sections.label: Members reflecting residents' feelings
sections.summary: Members are listening to and reflecting residents' feelings, and action is being taken on people's needs and concerns, including cost of living.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I am glad Members are listening to and reflecting the feelings of their residents.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We are taking action to address our people's needs and concerns, including the cost of living.

sections.label: Industry Transformation Maps and Community Networks
sections.summary: Industry Transformation Maps and Community Networks for Seniors are major initiatives in this regard.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Our Industry Transformation Maps (ITMs) and Community Networks for Seniors, among other things, are major initiatives in this regard.

sections.label: Bettering lives across all spheres
sections.summary: In healthcare, education, economy, jobs, transport and security, bounds will be pushed to better lives, and Minister Ong Ye Kung spoke on tackling inequality.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In every sphere, from healthcare to education, from the economy to the creation of jobs, transport to security, we will push the bounds to continue to better the lives of all Singaporeans Minister Ong Ye Kung spoke about how we must strive ceaselessly to tackle inequality so that Singapore remains a place of opportunities for all.

sections.label: Shaping economy and society for potential
sections.summary: As schools bring out the best in every child, the economy and society can be shaped to give every Singaporean opportunities, skills and competencies to fulfill their potential.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Just as we run our schools to bring out the best in every child, we can shape our economy and society to give every Singaporean the opportunities, skills and competencies to fulfill their potential.

sections.label: Supporting workers to adapt
sections.summary: Ministers Teo and Ng build on predecessors' work by helping workers adapt and supporting low-wage, mature and middle-aged workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Minister Josephine Teo at the Ministry of Manpower and Minister Ng Chee Meng at the National Trades Union Congress are building on what their predecessors have built, by enabling workers to adapt and grow, and providing extra support for low-wage workers, mature workers and middle-aged middle-income workers.

sections.label: Singapore brand of meritocracy
sections.summary: Minister Masagos called for a Singapore meritocracy where the successful give back and policies help people move up.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Minister Masagos Zulkifli called for us to grow not just any meritocracy, but our Singapore brand of meritocracy where the successful give back to society, where we share common experiences, and where Government policies enable our people to move up.

sections.label: Respecting and supporting Singaporeans
sections.summary: The passage calls for supporting Singaporeans through service, platforms and opportunities, and moving away from over-emphasis on grades.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To bring out the best in our people, we must continually find ways to respect, encourage and support Singaporeans to give expression to our values, whether it is through acts of service, such as Values-in-Action education and philanthropic programmes to act on their care and compassion for others; through platforms, such as the Global Innovation Alliance for our people to venture out into the world, to innovate and create value; or through opportunities, like Our Singapore Fund, to celebrate our identity, cultures and all that make being Singaporean special.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Let us fire up their passion to explore and discover, and encourage them to invent and innovate, throughout their lives.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We should move away from an over-emphasis on grades, build on the strengths and interests of each child, and develop each to his or her fullest potential.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We must strive for multiple ladders of success, multiple peaks of excellence.

sections.label: 4G leadership building partnership
sections.summary: The 4G political leadership is committed to building this partnership and growing trust.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The 4G political leadership is committed to building this partnership and growing the trust.

sections.label: Community Network for Seniors
sections.summary: CNS partners government agencies, VWOs and community groups to help seniors stay active and well, reaching about a million seniors by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The Community Network for Seniors (CNS) is a good example of how we can partner one another to tackle one of our key challenges – an ageing society.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: CNS brings together Government agencies, VWOs and community groups as one team to help our seniors stay active and well.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The idea of partnership may appear simple, but the potential for this partnership to touch lives – about a million seniors by 2030 – is significant.

sections.label: Singapore as ASEAN Chair
sections.summary: Singapore is ASEAN Chair this year, working with neighbours for a more integrated, innovative and resilient ASEAN, including finance meetings.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Singapore is ASEAN Chair this year and the Prime Minister has chaired some very significant meetings.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We are using this opportunity to work together with our neighbours and to make our contribution towards a more integrated, innovative and resilient ASEAN.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I recently chaired the ASEAN Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors Meeting in Singapore, and co-chaired the ASEAN+3 Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors Meeting in Manila with the Korean Deputy Prime Minister.

sections.label: 4G leaders launch discussions
sections.summary: The 4G leaders and MPs will launch discussions with different groups of Singaporeans to kickstart this process.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The 4G leaders and MPs will launch a series of discussions with different groups of Singaporeans to kickstart this process.

sections.label: Taking stock of views
sections.summary: Views shared in the House will be taken stock of in coming weeks before details on a discussion series.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: As there has been a variety of views shared in this House, we will take stock of them in the coming weeks, before providing further details on a discussion series.

sections.label: 4G leaders engage people
sections.summary: The 4G leaders and MPs will engage people, hold discussions, strengthen communication, and prioritise Singaporeans' well-being.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The 4G leaders and MPs will continue to engage our people and consider all views with an open mind.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We will conduct a series of discussions, strengthen communication with different segments of the society, including charities and community organisations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The 4G leaders will remain true to our conviction, improve the lives of our people, and put the well-being of Singaporeans as a top priority.

sections.label: New spirit of partnership
sections.summary: For our generation, the new spirit must be one of greater partnership and trust.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: For our generation, our new spirit must be one of greater partnership and trust.

sections.label: Future economic metrics
sections.summary: Future economic metrics need to reflect societal trends such as sustainable income, retirement adequacy, quality of life and wealth transfer.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Our future economic metrics need to reflect societal trends and performance, such as sustainable income of the workforce, retirement adequacy, quality of life and intergenerational wealth transfer.

sections.label: ITMs and SkillsFuture efforts
sections.summary: With ITMs and SkillsFuture, efforts continue to transform sectors, upgrade worker skills and create opportunities for the future economy.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: With the ITMs and SkillsFuture, we are steadfast in our efforts to transform the sectors, upgrade our workers’ skills and create new opportunities, abreast with the future economy.

sections.label: Jobs, wages and skills
sections.summary: Efforts must translate into tangible jobs, reasonable real wage increases and skills relevant to a changing business environment.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: As with all efforts, they must ultimately translate into tangible jobs, reasonable real wage increases and skills that are relevant to changing business environment.

sections.label: Ecosystem of industries abroad
sections.summary: The speaker suggested creating an ecosystem of industries with more small and medium enterprises abroad, a point alluded to by three named Members.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: In my speech, I suggested to create an ecosystem of industries with more small and medium enterprises abroad, a point that was also alluded to by Mr Liang Eng Hwa, Mr Teo Ser Luck and Mr Thomas Chua.

sections.label: Local and global talents
sections.summary: While building local talents, global talents must also be included, particularly from fields currently lacking.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: As we build local talents, we need to be mindful that we include global talents, too, particularly from fields that we currently lack.

sections.label: Digital platform and seniors
sections.summary: Mr Henry Kwek suggested harnessing data and digitalisation for a single national digital platform, and Ms Tin Pei Ling said seniors must not be neglected in digitalisation.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Mr Henry Kwek suggested harnessing the value of data and digitalisation to create a single national digital platform where businesses can find new opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Ms Tin Pei Ling also highlighted that we must not neglect our seniors in the digitalisation process.

sections.label: Tackling inequality unfinished business
sections.summary: The topic was debated by several Members, and the speaker agrees with Minister Ong Ye Kung that tackling inequality is unfinished business requiring ceaseless efforts and refinement.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: This topic was vigorously debated upon by Mr Ang Wei Neng, Mr Png Eng Huat, Mr Sitoh Yih Pin and many more other Members I cannot mention in detail here.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: I agree with Minister Ong Ye Kung that we have unfinished business of tackling inequality and it requires ceaseless efforts and drive and continued refinement as we progress in our nationhood building, be it through education, jobs, housing or urban planning.

sections.label: Tetris safety net
sections.summary: The speaker says the Government and the people should begin making their own Tetris safety net.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Further, I say that the Government and the people should begin making our own Tetris safety net.

sections.label: Expanding protection for middle class
sections.summary: The passage states that while the lower-income group is always supported, reach should be expanded to give more protection and peace of mind to a burgeoning middle class.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: While the lower-income group is always supported, we have to begin considering expanding our reach in different aspects to give more protection and peace of mind to a burgeoning middle class.

sections.label: Inclusive growth, learning, workplace
sections.summary: The passage calls for rallying behaviours promoting meritocracy, diversity and inclusion, and encouraging age-friendly, women-friendly, worker-inclusive workplace standards, and notes gaps in healthcare services.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: From inclusive growth to inclusive learning to inclusive workplace, we should rally behaviours that promote meritocracy, diversity and inclusion.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: And encourage social norms, adoption of standards for age-friendly, women-friendly, worker inclusive workplaces, as advocated by Dr Amy Khor, Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef, Mr Heng Chee How and Ms Low Yen Ling.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Dr Chia Shi-Lu spoke about the need to further bridge the gaps in healthcare services for senior patients, individuals with mental health needs, and strengthening our primary healthcare.

sections.label: Government engagement with people
sections.summary: The passage states the Government must strengthen engagement with people for greater alignment of concerns and aspirations and a stronger sense of shared ownership.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: The Government must strengthen the engagement with our people so that there will be a greater sense of alignment of concerns and aspirations, and a stronger sense of shared ownership.

sections.label: Aspirations for Singapore's future
sections.summary: The passage states aspirations for Singapore: shared common values and spaces, many voices represented, and social mobility and continued equitable wealth distribution.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: So, looking ahead, what do we aspire to have in Singapore?

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: I say one where we share common values and spaces, one where many voices are represented, and, certainly, one that enables social mobility and continued equitable wealth distribution.
